project.name: concorde-development
project.description: Development environment for Concorde, a framework for architecture-aware Specs, project understanding, and scoped Pi worker agents invoked from Codex or Claude.

nodes.name: concorde.json
nodes.summary: The Framework package manifest for Concorde 7.0.0: it declares the package identity, license and repository, the architecture_profile 14 / workspace_protocol 15 / delivery_proposal 10 compatibility numbers, the concorde Skill namespace, the runtime launcher, Python floor, requirements lock and venv location, the pinned Understand Anything viewer release with its asset URL, SHA256, size and accepted graph paths, the distributed templates, the package_roots that may be distributed, the claude and codex integrations and the install framework root and receipt paths. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.build (Build), whose declared responsibility is resolving authored sources into deterministic worker instructions, installed Skills and runtime schemas.

nodes.name: package-lock.json
nodes.summary: Spec-declared binding of module.views (entity.views.publication-docsite: Publication docsite). The file exists (22280 non-empty lines) but UA's built-in default ignore rules excluded it from the native scan, so its contents were not analyzed.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Private npm manifest for the docsite template: pins Docusaurus 3.10.2 with the classic preset, local search, Mermaid ELK layout, React 19, gray-matter and parse5, plus tsx, TypeScript and vitest for tooling, and defines the validate / start / build / typecheck / test / check scripts that drive the publication pipeline. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity.

nodes.name: deploy-docsite.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow template scaffolded into consumer projects: it checks out the repository, conditionally builds Concorde's Skills, roles and Protocol assets when scripts/concorde.py exists, installs the docsite lockfile, builds the verified site and publishes it to GitHub Pages from a separate deploy job. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).
nodes.languageNotes: The `hashFiles('scripts/concorde.py')` guards let the same template serve both a Framework source checkout and an ordinary scaffolded consumer that has no Framework build command.

nodes.name: site.json
nodes.summary: Concorde's own project-owned site identity (schema 1): title, URL, baseUrl, organization and project names, repository, tagline, plus the optional homepage introduction with feature cards, the four-step workflow, a quickstart code block, a reference section tabulating Agents and task modes, the capability inventory, Harnesses and executable entry points, homepage links and the protocol custom-docs collection. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity; the docsite README states this content is deliberately not copied into consumer scaffolds.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript configuration extending @docusaurus/tsconfig with strict, emit-free type checking over the Docusaurus config, sidebars, plugins, scripts, src, the Concorde-only extension assets, tests and custom docs, with node and vitest global type packages. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity.

nodes.name: package-lock.json
nodes.summary: Spec-declared binding of module.harness (entity.harness.pi-worker-runtime: Pi worker runtime). The file exists (100 non-empty lines) but UA's built-in default ignore rules excluded it from the native scan, so its contents were not analyzed.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Private package manifest for the Concorde Pi runtime, declaring ESM module type and pinning pi-subagents 0.68.0, the delegation extension every worker loads alongside the Concorde worker extension. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.pi-worker-runtime (Pi worker runtime).

nodes.name: manifest.json
nodes.summary: Pinned manifest of the distributable Protocol bundle: declares schema_version 1, Protocol version 9.0.0, source_profile 14 and workspace_protocol 15, and records SHA-256 digests for three generated assets (generated/protocol/kinds/module.md, generated/protocol/principles.md and generated/protocol/schemas.json). Bound by module.spec as its Protocol assets entity, which packages the authored Protocol text for runtime distribution without becoming a second authority over its meaning. Observation: the manifest digests only the generated outputs; it records no digest of the authored chapters in this directory that those outputs are built from.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Python project metadata for the concorde-development checkout: requires-python >=3.11 with no runtime dependencies, a dev dependency group (jsonschema, langgraph >=1.2,<2), an optional studio group (langgraph-cli[inmem]), uv configured in non-package mode, pyright extraPaths pointing at src, and a [tool.concorde] section fixing the Python version and the unittest discovery test command. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.build (Build), the Module responsibility that resolves authored sources into distributable assets and the managed runtime.

nodes.name: package-lock.json
nodes.summary: Spec-declared binding of module.distribution (entity.distribution.managed-runtime: Managed runtime). The file exists (30 non-empty lines) but UA's built-in default ignore rules excluded it from the native scan, so its contents were not analyzed.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Installer-owned private npm manifest pinning the official understand-anything-viewer v2.9.0 release tarball as the sole dependency and requiring Node.js 18+, so the managed runtime is provisioned from a fixed lock rather than a floating registry range. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.managed-runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: Depends on a direct GitHub release URL rather than a registry version, which is why the README records the tarball SHA-256 and byte count alongside the lockfile integrity value.

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Role instructions for the concorde-answerer worker: answer one question about the project strictly from explicitly selected complete Module Specs, start from each Module's reading entry, treat the granted documents as one deduplicated pool, never read implementation contents, cite the source paths relied on, and return `completed`, `expand` naming only identified Module targets, or `spec_incomplete` with concrete gaps. Bound by module.harness as Model execution profiles; it is an authored instruction asset, not a registered Spec document unit.

nodes.name: scout.md
nodes.summary: Child agent definition for the code reviewer's `scout`: given one contract and the admitted paths, it searches only those paths and reports the files, functions, tests and line ranges that realize or verify the contract with a one-line reason each, says plainly when it finds nothing, and never judges defects, changes files or searches outside the grant. Bound by module.harness as Model execution profiles.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML front matter configures the child (tools, `systemPromptMode: replace`, and inheritProjectContext/inheritGlobalContext/inheritSkills all false) so the child starts from an isolated prompt.

nodes.name: verifier.md
nodes.summary: Child agent definition for the `verifier`: it may use bash and the host's configured `run_checks`, must run exactly the requested checks without modifying any file, and must report each command, its exit status and the output lines explaining a failure, reporting the attempted command and the missing input when a check cannot run and never marking a check passed it did not see pass. Bound by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Role instructions for concorde-code-reviewer: compare a registered Module's granted implementation and scoped changes with its complete admitted contracts, read the whole admitted document collection rather than only changed lines, treat a `verifies` declaration that does not exercise its scenario's steps as a defect while leaving out-of-context declarations to their owning Module, use the scout and verifier children for focused evidence, never modify Specs, source, tests or control files, and return `no_findings`, `findings` or `incomplete` with the representative tasks actually covered. Bound by module.harness as Model execution profiles.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Concorde's `@include prompts/workflow-host/review-scope-and-result.md` directive, so the shared review scope and result text is composed into the prompt at build time rather than duplicated here.

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Role instructions for concorde-context-assessor: decide whether the exact task can be carried out from the selected Module's complete Spec context, distinguishing sufficient information from missing information, a known prohibition and contradictory obligations, using only the Module's local dependency declarations rather than registry relationships, never reading the contents of declared implementation files and never searching for the missing information. Bound by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Role instructions for concorde-issue-solver: resolve one explicitly selected Issue from its reported problem, the complete admitted Module Spec and host-supplied progress by returning exactly one `issue_decision` — develop, spec-repair, verify, resolved, duplicate, not-actionable or needs-decision — with contract-level `intent` and an evidence-grounded rationale. It forbids reading implementation files, reclassifying the report, closing on a workaround or a single failed reproduction, and treats a failed tool, denied permission or reached iteration limit as an execution stop rather than a fabricated contract. Bound by module.issues as the Issue solver and by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: scout.md
nodes.summary: Child agent definition for the planner's `scout`: YAML front matter fixes its name, description, read-only tool set (read, grep, find, ls), `systemPromptMode: replace` and the disabled inheritance of project context, global context and skills, while the body instructs it to answer one focused question from the granted Spec documents and external references with exact paths, line ranges and quotations, and to say plainly when the grant does not answer it. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Authored instruction source for the `concorde-planner` worker, projected by the build into the agent definition that `capabilities/planner/__init__.py` names as its profile spec. Its Responsibilities, Goals, Accepted input, Expected results, Completion conditions and Missing-information sections require planning from the complete Module Spec alone (entity declarations may name files, but never their contents), forbid comprehensive remediation beyond the requested change, make vendored external references the only admitted source of third-party API facts, and describe the `scout` child. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: planner.md
nodes.summary: Authored role definition for the `planner` child of the Concorde programmer worker: its frontmatter grants only read-only tools (read, grep, find, ls), replaces the system prompt and inherits no project context, global context or Skills, while the body tells the child to turn one change, its tasks and acceptance into an ordered list of concrete steps naming file, function or section plus the checks that would show each step works, and forbids writing code or widening the change. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles), the service the Harness entry describes as combining an authored role with a Python profile into a reproducible WorkerBinding.
nodes.languageNotes: The frontmatter keys (systemPromptMode, inheritProjectContext, inheritSkills, completionGuard) are the Pi child-delegation execution profile, not Markdown content; only the prose below the fences becomes the child's instructions.

nodes.name: scout.md
nodes.summary: Authored role definition for the `scout` child of the Concorde programmer worker: read-only tools, a replaced system prompt and no inherited context or Skills, with a body instructing the child to answer one focused question by searching only the admitted paths and to report relevant files, symbols and line ranges with a one-line reason each, saying plainly when those paths do not answer the question. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles); its 'do not search outside the grant' rule is the instruction-level counterpart of the Harness context and permission boundary.

nodes.name: verifier.md
nodes.summary: Authored role definition for the `verifier` child worker: it adds `bash` and `run_checks` to the read-only tool set and instructs the child to run exactly the requested test commands or host-configured checks without modifying any file, report each command with its exit status and failure-explaining output, report the attempted command and missing input when a check cannot run, and never mark a check passed that it did not see pass. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles). Observation: the body addresses 'the verifier child of a Concorde worker' generically rather than the programmer specifically, and a separate copy of this child definition is registered under capabilities/code_reviewer/children/verifier.md.
nodes.languageNotes: `run_checks` is the host-mediated configured-check tool, distinct from a raw `bash` command; the Harness Spec notes that only configured checks run inside the OS-enforced read-only boundary.

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Authored instruction source for the `concorde-programmer` worker, the longest worker spec in this batch. It defines the write boundary (only files covered by the selected Module's entity listing entries, exact files or directory prefixes, never Specs, registry, configuration or worktree control state), scoped search over admitted paths, the `verifies` test-declaration syntax for Python and TypeScript, honest reporting of checks run and deferred host verification, and the bounded repair round driven by a `concorde-review-result`, plus its scout, planner and verifier children. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Authored instruction source for the `concorde-router` worker: route one task to exactly one owning Module identified by admitted Spec responsibility and selection conditions, read the discovery index and each Module's `spec_resolution` without ever reading implementation contents, and return `routed`, `expand` or a blocked outcome. It also states the per-capability route shape — a bare `target_id` / `focus_id` for `concorde-review`, `concorde-dev-loop` and `concorde-specify-loop` because the host binds the original task and constraints, versus a full task-carrying route for `concorde-main`. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Authored instruction source for the `concorde-spec-author` worker: return document replacements only for existing registered members owned by the selected Module, preserve document IDs and shared documents byte-for-byte, and recommend a topology change instead of silently widening authoring when a needed file lies outside every listed entry. It pulls in shared guidance with `@include prompts/workflow-host/spec-authoring.md`. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles). Observation: the text still instructs the author to preserve `main_visible` decisions, while the installed Protocol 9 Required format states schema-2 metadata has no `main_visible` property.

nodes.name: consistency.md
nodes.summary: Child agent definition for the Spec reviewer's `consistency` checker: front matter fixes read-only tools and disabled context/skill inheritance, and the body instructs it to verify that every scenario, requirement and entity ID is defined once, that ID-fragment links point at the defining document, that the Relationships diagram's node labels are exactly the declared entity titles and that every edge carries a label, reporting each inconsistency with path, line and identifiers. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: fact-check.md
nodes.summary: Child agent definition for the Spec reviewer's `fact-check` worker: front matter fixes read-only tools and disabled inheritance, and the body instructs it to decide whether one supplied claim is supported, contradicted or unsettled by the granted documents alone, quoting each relevant line with path and number, without judging significance, proposing changes or reading outside the grant. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Authored instruction source for the `concorde-spec-reviewer` worker: assess whether the complete admitted Module collection supports representative tasks, reviewing both Protocol-9 document roles as one contract, checking the Purpose / Terminology / Usage / Design / Relationships entry structure, explicit schema-2 roles, decidable single-SHALL requirements, GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios, entity metadata and labeled diagram edges, and judging readability from a newcomer's questions. It defines the `no_findings` / `findings` / `incomplete` result statuses, uses the fact-check and consistency children, and includes shared scope guidance via `@include prompts/workflow-host/review-scope-and-result.md`. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Authored instruction source for the `concorde-task-author` worker: turn the supplied plan and complete Spec into nonempty implementation tasks with stable IDs outside the host-supplied reserved set, observable acceptance citing the relevant scenario or requirement IDs, and `complete: false`. It fixes the implementation boundary (host checks, reviews, readiness, commits and delivery are never task acceptance conditions), and defines the two feedback rounds driven by `concorde-task-scope-feedback` and by a `concorde-review-result` over completed tasks. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Authored instruction source for the `concorde-topology-author` worker: author the documents of one accepted target descriptor from a topology proposal, preserving document IDs, candidate ownership and explicit references, keeping entity files equal to the accepted `target.files` entry for entry (a directory prefix stays a prefix), marking not-yet-existing entries pending without reading code, and returning every `target.documents` path exactly once in order. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles). Observation: like the Spec author instructions, it still names a `main_visible` decision to preserve, which the installed Protocol 9 Required format has removed from schema-2 metadata.

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: Role instructions for the concorde-topology-designer worker: design one candidate registry from explicitly selected complete Module Specs, task every added/changed target, `uses` edge and registry `files` entry, and never read implementation contents or invent Module behavior. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).
nodes.languageNotes: A capability role prompt: Responsibilities, Goals, Accepted input, Expected results, Completion conditions and gap handling, rendered into the worker system prompt alongside the common worker rules.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Maintainer documentation for the packaged, project-neutral docsite adapter: what the template excludes, Profile 14 / registry schema 5 admission, route and navigation rules, the Module Specs and Implementation Specs reading tabs with their schema-2 document roles, explanation-first authoring and Terminology conventions, the site.json identity fields, custom-docs configuration and migration, scaffolding commands, prerequisites, npm scripts and Build Manifest 21 promotion behavior. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity.

nodes.name: framework-profile.md
nodes.summary: The authored Concorde Framework execution profile (P5-P10 plus the authoring and publication conventions) that applies the independent Spec Protocol to Concorde's runtime: the four context kinds and their delivery, gap and review binding, explicit execution authority with the LangGraph Graph-API-only rule, coordinated topology and file-listing changes, worktree-bound evidence and P10 session handoffs. Bound by module.spec as part of entity.spec.protocol-assets (Protocol assets).
nodes.languageNotes: A profile chapter appended to every worker's rule bundle; it constrains Concorde's runtime without changing the Protocol standard itself.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Prompt assembly manifest (audience: shared) that composes the Module-kind rule bundle from @include directives for the Protocol's Module chapter and the Module and scenario templates. Bound by module.spec as part of entity.spec.protocol-assets (Protocol assets).
nodes.languageNotes: Front matter `audience: shared` plus `@include` paths: the prompt build resolves these into one rendered asset, so the file carries composition, not prose.

nodes.name: principles.md
nodes.summary: Prompt assembly manifest (audience: shared) that composes the Protocol rule bundle delivered with every worker's system prompt, @including the Protocol principles, Spec management, Spec and Context, required format chapters and the Concorde Framework execution profile. Bound by module.spec as part of entity.spec.protocol-assets (Protocol assets).

nodes.name: common.md
nodes.summary: The common rules prepended to every Concorde worker's system prompt: the single JSON input describing the admitted typed context, the path-listed documents readable in the workspace, the tool and grant discipline with final refusals, issue reporting classification and report_key retries, the single terminating submit_result call, and the one-level child delegation contract. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: dev-loop-flags.md
nodes.summary: Ambient-audience prompt fragment describing the development loop's request flags: optional `specify` and `run_reviews` (both defaulting to true) select the loop shape, a review requirement already recorded for a change cannot be cancelled by a later `run_reviews:false`, and `repair_task_scope:{tasks_digest:...}` repairs an incomplete task list whose acceptance wrongly demands later Host behavior, with the digest defined as sha256 over the canonical JSON task list. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources), which the Build command resolves into installed Skills.
nodes.languageNotes: `@include`-composed prompt sources carry a YAML `audience` header: `ambient` fragments end up in installed Skills read by the developer's own agent, `worker` fragments in Pi worker instructions.

nodes.name: gap-reporting.md
nodes.summary: Worker-audience prompt fragment defining how any Concorde worker reports a missing necessary contract, conflicting Specs or an implementation/Spec mismatch as an Issue of type gap through `report_issue`, how the returned receipt fields plus `blocked_step` go into `blockers` only when the Issue blocks the current stage, and how reviewers instead return `issues` with severity and affected_task. It forbids inferring obligations from implementation, inventing IDs, reusing another worker's records or relabelling a provider's definition as consumer-owned. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources and included by the shared worker preamble.

nodes.name: init-request-and-no-flags.md
nodes.summary: Three-line ambient prompt fragment stating that initialization uses its typed propose/apply request with the published request schema, that no domain flags or positional task arguments are accepted, and that configuration is never a context grant. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources and reused across the init, configure, validate, main, dev-loop and specify-loop Skills.

nodes.name: invoke-capability-opener.md
nodes.summary: Parameterized ambient opener telling the developer's conversation to invoke the capability in order to `{ACTION}`, because the host owns context resolution, agent execution, permissions and lifecycle state, and to supply the user's task as typed input instead of performing it directly or inspecting extra project files. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources; the build substitutes each Skill's own ACTION text.
nodes.languageNotes: The `{ACTION}` placeholder is filled by the include site (`@include ... ACTION="run the development loop"`), so one source produces the opener of every user-facing Skill.

nodes.name: lifecycle-no-cognition.md
nodes.summary: One-sentence ambient fragment marking a capability as a deterministic lifecycle capability that runs no agent cognition and selects no context. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources and included by the init, configure and validate Skills.

nodes.name: loop-completion-and-reviews.md
nodes.summary: Ambient fragment defining where the development loop stops and how its reviews behave: the loop ends at a verified `ready` candidate in the change worktree and never invokes deliver, partial progress and gaps persist in `.concorde/worktree.json`, delivery is a separate request from the source or primary worktree, and the loop calls `concorde-specify-loop` before planning, requiring independent Spec review before planning and read-only code review before ready, with explicit skip records, fresh sessions per mode and target, and invalidation of older conclusions by changed inputs. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources.

nodes.name: loop-task-request-fields.md
nodes.summary: Short ambient fragment stating that a new loop task request requires `task` and may supply `target_id`/`focus_id` (a scenario ID) only as routing hints, that main discovery selects the owning target before the bounded loop starts, and that existing changes keep their bound target. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources and shared by the dev-loop and specify-loop Skills.

nodes.name: main-may-inspect.md
nodes.summary: Parameterized ambient fragment stating that main discovery may explicitly admit complete Module Specs for routing but cannot read implementation files, and that it returns one typed route after which the host starts `{WORKERS}`. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources; it carries the Protocol's discovery-never-loads-implementation rule into the installed Skills.

nodes.name: review-scope-and-result.md
nodes.summary: Worker-audience fragment giving reviewers their scope and result contract: read the whole admitted document collection rather than only changed lines, derive representative tasks from the admitted request including dependencies and affected consumers, explain for each blocking finding how a missing promise or defect prevents an identified step, keep out-of-scope defects as advisory without calling them harmless, report each problem once through `report_issue` and return typed `no_findings`/`findings`/`incomplete` results bound to context, mode and input digest. It also forbids loading another target, repository guidance or other Skills and forbids modifying files or running validation. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources and included by the Spec and code reviewer capabilities.

nodes.name: spec-authoring.md
nodes.summary: The longest worker-audience fragment: the complete Spec-authoring instruction given to the Spec author and topology author. It restates the Protocol's document-unit model (module.md opening with Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design, Relationships; module-role topics carrying no req.*, scenario.* or concorde-contract definitions; implementation-role companions owned by the same Module; paired schema-2 metadata), the rules for requirements, scenarios, canonical contracts and participant bindings, the readability expectations for a reader without implementation knowledge, and the return format of UTF-8 replacements in `documents` validated as one overlay. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources.
nodes.languageNotes: This fragment is the operational projection of the Spec Protocol's P1–P4 reading and role rules into a worker prompt, so a Protocol change has to be mirrored here as well as in the Protocol bundle.

nodes.name: specify-loop-completion.md
nodes.summary: Ambient fragment defining the Spec loop's boundary: it authors or revises the selected Module's owned Spec documents and then independently reviews the complete contract and every affected consumer in separate fresh contexts, returning `completed` with artifact references while never claiming semantic completeness or implementation readiness. Blocking findings, incomplete coverage and contract gaps stop advancement, and continuing to implementation requires invoking `concorde-dev-loop` in the same change. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources.

nodes.name: specify-loop-flags.md
nodes.summary: Ambient fragment describing the Spec loop's optional `specify` and `run_reviews` flags: `specify:false` reviews the existing Spec without authoring, `run_reviews:false` records an explicit Spec review skip unless that review was already required for the change, a later request cannot cancel a recorded requirement, and this loop neither requires nor skips code review. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources.

nodes.name: stdin-invocation-config-input.md
nodes.summary: Single-sentence ambient continuation of the stdin invocation description, naming the `configuration` field (null to load initialized host settings, or a matching concorde-capability-configuration@1) and the `input` field (`{NAME}-request@1`). Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources; the `{NAME}` placeholder is substituted per Skill at build time.

nodes.name: stdin-invocation-open.md
nodes.summary: Ambient fragment opening the stdin invocation instruction: send one concorde-capability-invocation@3 JSON object to `{CAPABILITY}` with exactly type_id, schema_version:3, capability_id, mode `execute` or `describe-policy`, and the fields continued in the companion fragment. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources; it is the most widely reused source, appearing in every capability Skill including deliver.

nodes.name: target-identity-opener.md
nodes.summary: Two-line ambient fragment instructing the caller to use the supplied target identity and, when it is ambiguous, to ask the user to identify it rather than searching other Specs. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources and included by the init, configure and validate Skills.

nodes.name: task-request-fields.md
nodes.summary: Two-line ambient fragment listing the fields of a single-stage task request: `target_id` and `task`, with optional `focus_id` (a scenario ID), `constraints` and `change_id`. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources; it is the non-loop counterpart of loop-task-request-fields.md.

nodes.name: worktree-handoff.md
nodes.summary: Ambient fragment implementing the Protocol's P10 session handoff in the installed Skills: when a mutation starts in the primary worktree the host prepares a committed-base linked worktree and returns its identity plus a handoff draft without launching the next session, the caller must start that session automatically with the worktree as its initial directory, fresh context and its own Skills, ask the user for a manual start only when that is impossible, stop development in the current conversation and report gaps as returned rather than working around the boundary. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.skill-sources.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index chapter of the authored Concorde Spec Protocol 9.0.0 standard: it states the single Module Spec model, the split between complete content and its human-readable subset, and the two explicit document roles (module entry/topics versus implementation-role requirements, scenarios and canonical contracts), then lists the six chapters to read in order and records the Protocol 8 to 9 and 7 to 8 migration duties. Bound by module.spec as part of its Protocol text entity; it is authored standard text, not a registered Spec document unit of any Module.
nodes.languageNotes: The chapter list doubles as the standard's reading order; templates are named explicitly as starters that do not establish conformance.

nodes.name: format.md
nodes.summary: Required format chapter of the Protocol: prescribes the exact representation of both roles — paired Markdown and .md.json members, the five mandatory level-2 headings of module.md in order, the single Terminology table with Term and Meaning / definition columns, schema_version 2 metadata with document id/owner/role plus entities, dependencies and bindings arrays, the project-wide identity regex and readable anchor rules, requirement and scenario heading grammar, concorde-contract fences, relationship-diagram constraints, link and reference rules, and the Protocol 8/7 migration checklist. Bound by module.spec as part of its Protocol text entity.
nodes.languageNotes: This chapter is what a deterministic structural validator can check; it repeatedly warns that satisfying its syntax does not establish semantic completeness.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module specifications chapter of the Protocol: explains what each reading section must deliver (Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design, Relationships), then defines precise obligations — requirement statements with exactly one SHALL, GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios and interface agreements — that may only live in implementation-role units, and closes with composition versus dependency (illustrated by a Commerce/Checkout/Inventory Mermaid flowchart), realization and external knowledge, and completeness. Bound by module.spec as part of its Protocol text entity.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses fenced Markdown examples of requirement and scenario syntax; the Protocol explicitly notes that such fenced examples declare nothing.

nodes.name: principles.md
nodes.summary: Principles chapter of Spec Protocol 9.0.0: fixes the MUST/MUST NOT/SHOULD/MAY requirement language and defines P1 (a Module has one complete specification whose reading subset must explain purpose, terminology, usage, design, relationships and precise obligations, with formal definitions confined to implementation-role units), P2 (implementation bindings are metadata, never reading or implicit code access), P3 (one-level resolution of complete document units and explicit references) and P4 (conformance covers content, reading, structure and consistency). Bound by module.spec as part of its Protocol text entity. Observation: this authored chapter stops at P4; the Concorde Framework execution profile principles P5 to P10 that appear in the installed .concorde/protocol/principles.md bundle are authored separately in prompts/protocol/framework-profile.md, which module.spec also binds.
nodes.languageNotes: Normative prose uses capitalized MUST/SHOULD/MAY throughout; the Reading(M) subset-of-Content(M) formulation is the chapter's organizing idea.

nodes.name: spec-management.md
nodes.summary: Spec management chapter of the Protocol: separates document ownership, context inclusion, composition, dependency and implementation listing, defining the paired reading/.md.json document unit, the five independent registry relations (parent, uses, documents, references, files), entity identity and file-binding precedence, local collaboration agreements, shared interface contracts with participant bindings, authored Mermaid relationship views, and how versions, digests and semantic gaps are recorded. Bound by module.spec as part of its Protocol text entity.

nodes.name: spec-and-context.md
nodes.summary: The Spec Protocol chapter defining exact source selection: the one-level Units/Context formulas, the resolve algorithm and its per-source records, visibility versus delivery, the overlapping-references example, implementation context derived only from entity file bindings, external reference material, and how changes and gaps are handled. Bound by module.spec as part of entity.spec.protocol-text (Protocol text).
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol chapters are the independent standard: they sit outside the project Spec registry and do not have to satisfy the Module document format they define.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: The Module starter template illustrating the required format: the module.md reading member with Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships, the paired schema-2 module.md.json with document identity, entities, dependencies and bindings, and guidance for companion topic and implementation-role documents. Bound by module.spec as part of entity.spec.protocol-text (Protocol text).
nodes.languageNotes: The template states explicitly that satisfying its shape proves neither business facts nor semantic completeness.

nodes.name: scenario.md
nodes.summary: Authored Spec Protocol template showing the canonical Markdown shape of a scenario definition: a `scenario.<identity>` heading followed by GIVEN/AND/WHEN/THEN/BUT steps, plus the rules that a scenario may only be defined in an implementation-role companion and that querying it selects its owner's entire complete context. Bound by module.spec as part of entity.spec.protocol-text (Protocol text), the authored standard kept separate from its distributed Protocol assets copy.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a four-backtick fence so the inner Markdown example stays opaque and is not parsed as a real definition.

nodes.name: STUDIO.md
nodes.summary: Operator guide for running LangGraph Studio against this source checkout: starting the dev server from `generated/langgraph.json`, submitting a complete typed capability invocation in Graph mode, monitoring CLI and Skill calls, reading stage/process events and failures, consumer-project setup, and the bounded inspection surfaces a Studio session may observe. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.studio (Studio), which declares that Studio inspects the same executable Graph-API host Flows rather than a separate schematic model.
nodes.languageNotes: Emphasizes that the entry module binds project and package roots to the checkout containing it, so a second worktree needs its own server on another port.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the public `concorde-configure` Skill, declaring capability `configure`: apply the Pi worker model selection (model, thinking level, timeout and per-worker overrides) and, with `accept_protocol`, rebind the project to the installed Protocol copy. Its body is composed almost entirely of `@include` directives over `prompts/workflow-host/`, and it is bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources), the authored inputs the build resolves into Installed Skills.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the public `concorde-deliver` Skill, declaring capability `deliver`: stage a verified change, confirm and clear pending entity entries that now exist, create `concorde/delivered/<change_id>`, remove the source worktree, and only on an explicit `merge_primary:true` request merge into the primary branch under the host's repository lock. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources).
nodes.languageNotes: Written mostly as prose rather than includes, because delivery's ownership and retry rules are specific to this capability.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the public `concorde-dev-loop` Skill, declaring capability `dev_loop`: route one change, call the specify loop, then plan, task, implement, validate and review code to a ready candidate, with `specify=false` skipping authoring and `run_reviews=false` recording explicit review skips. Composed from shared workflow-host prompt includes and bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources).

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the public `concorde-init` Skill, declaring capability `init`: propose and apply explicit project initialization with a pinned Protocol and an honest registry stub. Its body is a sequence of shared workflow-host includes covering the lifecycle no-cognition rule, stdin invocation shape, task-request fields and worktree handoff. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources).

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the public `concorde-issues` Skill, declaring capability `issues`: list, show, report, reopen or solve branch-local Issues, where only `solve` starts development and ends at a verified candidate without automatic delivery, and unresolved product or design choices return as needs-decision. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources); it also states that legacy Reflections are archived history, never current approval.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the public `concorde-main` Skill, declaring capability `main`: Concorde's entry capability for answering questions, routing work and designing or applying system topology from complete Module Specs, through the actions ask, design-topology, accept-topology and apply-topology. The longest Skill source in the set, it spells out that discovery workers never read implementation files, that topology proposals must task every Module whose `uses` edges or `files` entries change, and how worktree metadata and delivery ownership are reported. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources).

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the public `concorde-review` Skill, declaring capability `review`: route a standalone Spec review, code review or source diagnosis to its owning Module and return scoped read-only findings, run in the current worktree without creating a development change, with reviewers holding no write, network or credential grants and findings authorizing no repairs. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources).

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the public `concorde-specify-loop` Skill, declaring capability `specify_loop`: route one change, author or revise its Spec, then independently review it, stopping before planning and implementation. Built from shared workflow-host includes for the invocation opener, loop task fields, specify-loop flags, handoff and completion. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.skill-sources (Skill sources).

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authored source of the user-facing `concorde-validate` Skill: frontmatter declares `capability: validate`, the body is assembled from eight `@include prompts/workflow-host/*` fragments plus prose stating what deterministic validation checks (document-unit identity and ownership, paired reading/metadata sources, reading structure, requirement and scenario syntax, registry `files` equal to the entity-entry union, test scenario declarations, and which findings are errors versus warnings). Bound by module.distribution as part of the Skill sources entity, which the Build command projects into installed Claude and Codex Skills; it invokes the deterministic `validate` lifecycle capability implemented in `capabilities/validate.py`. Observation: the prose names the reading structure as "Purpose/Usage/Design/Relationships" while the bound Protocol requires five headings including Terminology.
nodes.languageNotes: Skill sources are templates, not final prompts: `@include <path> KEY=VALUE` lines are resolved deterministically at build time into the installed Skill body.

nodes.name: collaborations.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit (document.concorde.collaborations) holding the root Module's sixteen local collaboration agreements — Spec, Harness, Development, Issues, Distribution, Views, Planning, Implementation, Spec Authoring, Review, Validation, Delivery, Query and Routing, Topology, Development Flow and Specification Flow. Each section carries the child's entity anchor plus its numbered agreement anchor and states the provider's responsibility, when the collaboration applies, and the canonical promises relied upon, with links into the provider's own definitions. Observation: the unit's declared role is implementation although it defines no req. or scenario. headings; it is the canonical container for the Module's dependency-explanation anchors.
nodes.languageNotes: Adjacent standalone anchors (entity plus agreement) on one line let the same prose serve both the entity meaning and the dependency explanation, which the Protocol permits explicitly.

nodes.name: concepts.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic (document.concorde.concepts) owned by module.concorde and referenced into the complete Spec context of all seventeen Modules: it is the project's canonical Terminology table, defining Module, Spec, Module Specs, Implementation Specs, Entity, Requirement, Scenario, Registry, Context, Grant, Snapshot, Evidence, Capability, Skill, Worker, Host, Harness, Flow, Candidate, Worktree, Ready, Delivery, Issue, Blocker and Contract for a reader who knows software development but not Concorde. It then walks one retry-behavior change end to end and warns that vocabulary is not an ownership, dependency or context declaration.
nodes.languageNotes: Every other Concorde Module imports its terms by linking this table's #terminology anchor rather than restating definitions, which is the Protocol's canonical-definition rule in practice.

nodes.name: contracts.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit (document.concorde.contracts) stating the Framework invocation agreement in one dense paragraph: installed Skills use a single schema-3 capability invocation carrying capability_id, an execute or describe-policy mode, configuration and a version-1 typed request; unsupported versions, malformed requests and configuration mismatch fail admission, and the result distinguishes succeeded, blocked, failed or described while the domain output still separates a ready candidate, gap, conflict or completed answer. Observation: the unit carries no concorde-contract fence, so it explains the invocation envelope without defining a canonical structured contract.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit (document.delivery.execution-reference) holding Delivery's precise execution and record contracts: the delivery capability agreement (candidate identity and evidence consumed from common worktree metadata, participating-session rules, atomic create-only publication of concorde/delivered/<change_id>, unchanged primary branch and index, source-worktree removal, explicit merge_primary authorization by the sole primary writer, repository-lock serialization, receipt semantics for cleanup and merge retries, and legacy schema-1 receipt handling), the integration-verification design that builds a Concorde package checkout before validating it, and the realization and reuse limits. Observation: the introduction announces executable Flow specifications, but the unit contains no %% flow: Mermaid Flow Spec — it is a prose contract only.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Reading entry (document.delivery.module, role module) of module.delivery, a child of the root Concorde Framework Module that uses Development, Harness, Spec and Distribution: it defines the terms Delivered branch and Delivery receipt, explains that concorde-deliver may only be requested from the change's source or the primary worktree, publishes concorde/delivered/<change_id>, removes the source worktree unless keep_worktree:true, and leaves the primary branch untouched until a separate merge_primary request by the sole primary writer. Design explains publication, cleanup and merging as distinct receipted transitions verified in a temporary detached worktree under the repository lock, and the four collaboration agreements state what each provider guarantees.
nodes.languageNotes: The entry keeps the destructive default visible in Usage — delivery removes the source worktree unless retention is requested explicitly — rather than hiding it behind a detail link.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit (document.delivery.requirements) defining Delivery's two Module-wide obligations: req.development.single-primary-writer (at most one agent SHALL own writes in the primary worktree at a time) and req.development.primary-writes-serialized (the host SHALL serialize shared lifecycle writes and final primary merges with the repository lock). Both identities keep their historical development. prefix while being owned by module.delivery, as recorded in the root Module's ownership migration ledger.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit (document.delivery.scenarios) defining Delivery's four GIVEN/WHEN/THEN situations: deliver-branch (publishing the independent concorde/delivered/<change_id> branch and removing the source worktree while leaving primary untouched), deliver-merge-primary (an explicitly authorized merge from the primary worktree's owning session, recorded separately from staging evidence), deliver-session-rejected (refusal with delivery_session_required or primary_session_required from an unrelated worktree) and deliver-conflict (merge_conflict or failed_merge_checks blocking the final merge while preserving the delivered branch). The identities retain their historical development. prefix under module.delivery ownership.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec of module.dev-loop holding the detailed execution and record contracts: the Development Agent Flow and revision loops, explicit `repair_task_scope:{tasks_digest}` recovery, failure/recovery outcome vocabulary (`spec_incomplete`, `waiting`, `failed`, `blocked`, `limit_exhausted`, `cancelled`), candidate lifecycle and review policy with `max_repair_iterations` recorded per target in `.concorde/worktree.json`, and the coordinated-implementation finalization rules. It also carries the Flow Spec for the LangGraph Flow `development_flow` — nodes `initialize`, `specify_loop`, `plan`, `tasks`, `implement`, `validate`, `review_code`, `ready`, `summarize` — bound by `%% flow: development_flow` and kept equal to the compiled graph by the configured Flow Spec check.
nodes.languageNotes: The Mermaid flowchart is bound to the compiled LangGraph Flow by a `%% flow: development_flow` comment; node identifiers include `__start__`/`__end__` and every edge leaving a multi-successor node carries its routing condition as a label.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Reading entry (role `module`) of module.dev-loop, the Development Flow Module: it explains how one intended change is carried through Spec preparation, planning, task authoring, implementation, validation and independent code review to a `ready` candidate, and states that delivery is always a separate decision. Its Design and Relationships sections introduce the Development Flow adapter, the durable Development candidate record and the bounded Repair policy, and its nine per-provider agreement sections (Development, Harness, Spec, Query and Routing, Specification Flow, Planning, Implementation, Validation, Review) give each collaboration's applicability condition, relied-upon guarantee and local duty.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol 9 entry layout: Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships in order, with a labeled Mermaid flowchart whose node labels are exactly the Module's own entity titles.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec of module.dev-loop defining its four Module-wide SHALL requirements: `req.development.explicit-skip-sticky` (a `run_reviews=false` retry cannot cancel an already-required Spec or code review), `req.development.repair-edge-only` (`review_code -> tasks` is the only automatic revision edge), `req.development.non-repair-stops-graph` (every other non-successful outcome stops the graph for a human decision) and `req.development.specify-loop-composition` (Spec preparation composes concorde-specify-loop).

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec of module.dev-loop defining eight GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios for the development loop: `scenario.development.resume-unbound` and `resume-bound` (resuming a handoff before or after owner binding), `dev-loop-ready` (a change reaching a ready candidate), `dev-loop-spec-gap` (stopping with status `waiting` on a necessary Spec gap), `task-scope-repair` (digest-bound recovery of an implementation phase-boundary error), `dev-loop-repair` and `dev-loop-repair-exhausted` (the bounded automatic repair edge and its unchanged-feedback / limit stops) and `dev-loop-coordinated` (a Module coordinating its own and its components' tasks).

nodes.name: capabilities.md
nodes.summary: Explanatory topic (role `module`) of module.development titled "Choosing and composing operations": it defines the public/internal Capability distinction (a public Capability has exactly one Skill or launcher entry; knowing an internal operation's name is not permission to invoke it) and explains why declared data and trusted authority stay separate, so a forged result cannot select stronger tools or another workspace. It deliberately keeps the exact inventory, State channels and compatibility rules in the Module's implementation-role units.

nodes.name: collaborations.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec of module.development holding its fourteen canonical collaboration agreements — Harness, Spec, Issues, Distribution, Planning, Implementation, Spec Authoring, Review, Validation, Delivery, Query and Routing, Topology, Development Flow and Specification Flow — each stating the provider's responsibility, when the collaboration applies, the relied-upon guarantees (linked into the included provider contexts) and Development's own duties. It also records that Development's only structural parent is module.concorde and that it has no submodules.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec of module.development holding three contract groups. The Capability registry defines a Capability as a State-based LangGraph node with `PUBLIC`, `CONTEXT_SELECTION`, `DETERMINISTIC`, `USES`, `STATE` and optional `PROFILE` properties, retires the former Operation name and parallel Agent registry, and tabulates the fourteen host-adapter capabilities with their Skill, context selection and behavioral owner. The Development host Flows section carries the Flow Specs of its six own LangGraph Flows — `capability_flow`, `dispatch_flow`, `target_flow`, `project_flow`, `coordination_flow` and `stabilization_flow` — each bound by `%% flow:` to the compiled graph. The final section defines attributed Issue blockers, candidate `issue_blockers` keyed by change/scope/Module/phase/Issue, and the release rules that keep review evidence bound to the inputs it examined.
nodes.languageNotes: Six Flow Specs share one document; each Mermaid flowchart is bound by a `%% flow: <name>` comment and kept equal to the compiled LangGraph Flow by the configured Flow Spec check.

nodes.name: flows.md
nodes.summary: Explanatory topic (role `module`) of module.development titled "How the host coordinates a request": it describes the normal request path (one common admission boundary, workspace establishment, Module selection, dispatch and result recording) and why a change touching several owners waits for all writers before final checks, since checking one consumer while another still changes shared code would yield misleading evidence. It explicitly defers the exact Flow diagrams to the Module's execution reference rather than defining a second execution graph.

nodes.name: interfaces.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec of module.development defining the host boundary in exact terms: the executable entry `python3 scripts/run-capability.py <skill-name>`, the `concorde-capability-invocation@3` stdin envelope and `concorde-capability-result@3` stdout result with their statuses and exit codes, `concorde-capability-configuration@1` model settings, the 1 MiB input limit, `unknown_capability` / `unsupported_version` / `stale_build` / `workspace_mismatch` refusals, worktree binding and handoff rules, per-phase context grants, and the wire-contract tables for capability requests/responses, stage handoffs, review, topology, project-proposal and stage-input artifact types. It also carries the local participation explanation for the required `contract.context.selection` version 3 role with module.harness.
nodes.languageNotes: Every payload is a TypedValue `{type_id, schema_version, data}`; the document pins each type's version and states its promise in prose rather than restating the JSON Schema, which lives in code and is exported by the build.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Reading entry (role `module`) of module.development, the Development capability host: it explains the single admission boundary through which every Concorde operation is requested, how the host checks a request and its workspace, selects the allowed Capability or workflow and records accepted results, and how mutating work on the primary worktree becomes an isolated candidate plus a fresh-session handoff. Design introduces its seven entities (Development host, Development capabilities, Worktree lifecycle, File transactions, Installed Skills, Developer runtime, LangGraph); an explicit Unresolved information section declares that invocation-binding mechanics still living in `capability_host.py` belong to module.harness and that extracting them is pending.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol 9 entry layout (Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design, Relationships) with a scoped Mermaid view that uses a dotted edge for the conditional worker-execution path through Harness.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec of module.development defining its eight Module-wide SHALL requirements: `req.development.stage-no-reselect` (a bound Capability cannot reselect or widen its frozen context), `req.development.no-implementation-for-non-code` (planners, task authors and Spec-only reviewers receive no implementation file contents), `req.development.project-root-is-working-directory` (the project root is the entry process's working directory, without searching parents), `req.development.distinct-outcomes`, `req.development.stage-no-skill`, `req.development.stage-in-process-only`, `req.development.langgraph-control-flow` (every orchestration executes as a LangGraph Flow) and `req.development.single-boundary` (no agent-to-agent channel bypasses the host adapter).

nodes.name: review-and-gaps.md
nodes.summary: Explanatory topic (role `module`) of module.development titled "Problems that block a task": it distinguishes a recorded Issue from a task's Blocker, shows with a worked example how a missing contract blocks one task while independent work continues, and explains repair and reassessment — an old blocker is released only by a new accepted result, a workaround may release a dependency while the Issue stays open, and closing an Issue never rewrites a review as passed. Exact blocker records and release rules are deferred to the execution reference.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec of module.development defining thirteen GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios in two groups. The capability-host group covers `execute-capability`, `execute-unregistered`, `execute-blocked-launch` (stale build or unenforceable permission), `describe-policy`, `invocation-worktree-binding`, `workspace-inventory`, `worktree-handoff`, `flow-specs` (every bound Mermaid diagram equals its compiled Flow), `graph-api-only` (no LangGraph Functional API anywhere under `src/` and `scripts/`), `flow-execution` and `flow-bounds`; the capability-registry group covers `capability-state` and `capability-result-state` (a blocked or failed envelope is preserved, never flattened into success data).

nodes.name: build.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.distribution (document.distribution.build) describing how build() renders Agent instructions, per-integration Skill files, generated/langgraph.json and the Protocol rule assets deterministically from capabilities/, protocol/, prompts/ and skills/. It explains projection identity (twelve independent worker projections, each concatenating prompts/workers/common.md with the worker's own role Spec), source/output freshness accounting in the build manifest, the one-Skill-per-public-Capability rule, and that the package supports Protocol 9.0.0 with source profile 14 and metadata schema 2 while wire envelopes stay independently versioned.

nodes.name: contracts.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.distribution (document.distribution.contracts) defining the Module's public call shapes and record contracts: the build interface (render_model_instructions, render_skill, render_langgraph, the three Protocol asset renderers, build/write_build/check_build, recompute_protocol_manifest, verify_fresh, load_model_instructions), the prompt_resolver and package_validation interfaces, and the managed_runtime interface (load_runtime_spec, runtime_python, plan_runtime, provision_runtime). It specifies the BuildOutput, BuildResult, ResolvedPrompt, SkillPrompt, WorkerBinding, ManagedRuntimeSpec and ViewerSpec records, their digest fields and the typed BuildError / PromptResolverError / ManagedRuntimeError failure semantics.

nodes.name: installation.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.distribution (document.distribution.installation) that defines the terms Installation, Update and Installation receipt and walks through a normal preview-then-apply installation into a target project. It separates installing Framework tools, Skill instructions and the Protocol copy from project initialization and Spec authoring, and explains that an update treats a locally modified installer-owned output as a conflict and that receiving a new Protocol copy is not acceptance of a new binding.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module-role reading entry of module.distribution (document.distribution.module), owned by that Module: it states that Distribution renders the Framework assets developers install and run, then explains Build (authored sources, Skill sources, build manifest, package inventory), Installation (install script, proposal, ownership receipt, target project), Managed runtime and Pi worker configuration, and the checkout-only Worktree guard, with a Mermaid Relationships view and the single declared dependency on module.spec. It ends with an explicit unresolved gap: the intended preserve-then-restore runtime replacement is not yet fulfilled by the provisioning code.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol 9 entry layout: Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships as the first five level-2 headings, with entity anchors grouped on standalone lines before the prose that explains them.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.distribution (document.distribution.requirements) defining 14 Module-wide SHALL requirements: no silent Protocol rebinding and explicit binding decisions, deterministic and I/O-free idempotent builds, one-worktree build scope, user-invocable-only checkout Skill projections, block-scoped root rule ownership with untouched surrounding user text, atomic installation rollback, and four worktree-guard obligations (decide from submitted command text, never rely on agent memory, protect only this checkout, never install into consumer projects).

nodes.name: runtime.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.distribution (document.distribution.runtime) explaining managed runtime planning before provisioning: the plan distinguishes creation, verified reuse, rebuild and ownership conflict, provisioning is separate from launching a worker or viewer, and identity is recorded only after verification succeeds. It names the failure surface (ManagedRuntimeError) and repeats that the required preserve-and-restore replacement design is still an unfulfilled obligation.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.distribution (document.distribution.scenarios) defining 19 GIVEN/WHEN/THEN acceptance cases grouped into Installation service (preview, apply, conflict rejection, root-guidance cleanup, integration switch, configure-apply, explicit Protocol acceptance, worktree-guard refusal, disposable docsite type-check), Build (deterministic render, user-invocable checkout Skills, write_build manifest digests, check_build staleness, stale-build fail-closed, load_model_instructions binding, capability determinism metadata) and Managed runtime (plan, provision, provisioning failure). It also records the distributable manifest facts: concorde.json schema_version 3, 26 Capabilities with 9 public Skill entries and 17 private nodes, 12 of them model-backed. Observation: the Module's own bound golden build fixtures under tests/concorde/fixtures/build/golden/ contain ten Skill projections including concorde-reflections-triage, while skills/ holds nine authored SKILL.md sources matching the stated nine public Skills.

nodes.name: agents-and-harnesses.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.harness (document.harness.agents-and-harnesses) distinguishing a capability (an operation) from a worker (one model-backed agent execution). It explains the one-bounded-job model — fresh worker, no inherited conversation, only accepted results passing on — why model/thinking configuration is not permission, and that named helper children use fresh conversations under the parent's bounded access and cannot delegate again.

nodes.name: context.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.harness (document.harness.context) that canonically defines the four context kinds — Spec context (the Module's complete owned and referenced units), Implementation context (bound file names visible generally, contents only with a code-phase grant), Capability context (admitted operation/tool agreements and declared external references) and Task context (task, constraints, stage results, lifecycle state). It also states the gap rule for bounded tasks: report a missing promise rather than following an undeclared link or reading implementation.

nodes.name: contracts.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.harness (document.harness.contracts) defining the Module's canonical interface contracts: context snapshot resolution (resolve_context / resolve_discovery_context / recheck_context producing the private concorde-context-snapshot@6 with context_id, protocol_binding, spec_resolution index records, implementation_entries and implementation_files), the Spec context grant, the context selection agreement, the review-result stage-input value, global Spec context assembly, the permissions and worktree interface signatures (compile_policy, verify_effective_subset, inspect_worktree, require_isolated_worktree, WorktreeBoundary), the typed-values interfaces (canonical, decode, typed, validate_typed, json_schema, artifact, schema admit/validate) and the four-kind context table. It hosts the meaning anchor for the contract.context.selection participant binding.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: The Module's largest implementation-role unit (document.harness.execution-reference, owned by module.harness): it holds the precise execution and record contracts behind every explanatory topic. It defines the capability/Harness execution model A1-A5 (instructions and execution profile, profile and Harness binding, State and composition, invocation constraints and evidence, one-level helper delegation), task contracts and the common worker rules inventory; the capability Flow rules G1-G4 with the Flow Spec convention; Agent execution including configured deterministic checks, workspace kinds, input/result, common limits, the Pi worker runtime, usage accounting, outcomes, check isolation, launch, tool gate and one-level delegation; the invocation host with the Studio execution view and the two Flow Specs bound by '%% flow: capability_node' and '%% flow: batch_flow'; permissions enforcement and policy compilation; and typed-value validation, canonical serialization, recursive dispatch and offline schema/artifact contracts.
nodes.languageNotes: Flow Specs follow Concorde's LangGraph convention: a State part, a Nodes table with in/out state, and a Mermaid flowchart bound to the compiled graph by a '%% flow: <name>' comment whose node identifiers match the compiled node names.

nodes.name: execution.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.harness (document.harness.execution) describing a normal worker execution — check the definition, fix the information, narrow tool and file access, then validate the submitted result and reverify inputs — and stating the deployment security limits in bold: the worker tool gate is not an operating-system sandbox and does not confine an authorized shell command, while configured deterministic checks use an OS-enforced read-only project mount that currently requires Linux with working bubblewrap/namespace support and fails closed when unavailable.

nodes.name: graphs-and-loops.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.harness (document.harness.graphs-and-loops) separating a Flow (which operations can run and what selects the next step) from a loop (how feedback leads to another attempt). It explains the normal specification-planning-tasks-implementation-checks-review sequence, distinguishes fixed program rules, model judgment and required human decisions, and states why control flow is declared through LangGraph so the runtime and Studio inspect the same nodes and transitions, with the exact node names and limits kept once in Implementation Specs.

nodes.name: host.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.harness (document.harness.host) describing the invocation host: it selects the worker for a requested stage, obtains current instructions, fixes the Spec and task information, narrows tools and files, chooses runtime settings and starts the checked worker, while the executor independently rechecks before launch and validates the result afterwards. It explains why orchestration stays separate from workers, that sequential batches stop when an item cannot proceed, and that Studio observing the same executable Flows and policy preview are optional, non-authorizing views.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module-role reading entry of module.harness (document.harness.module), the Module about how an agent is configured: it defines Worker profile, Tool gate and Capsule, explains that the Harness prepares a worker's task, information and permissions and then validates its result, and designs the Capability/Harness model, Model execution profiles, Context resolution, the Permissions compiler, Worker execution on the Pi worker runtime, LangGraph Host Flows, Studio and Worktree lifecycle. It declares collaboration agreements with module.spec and module.distribution, states plainly that the tool gate is not an OS sandbox, and lists four unresolved items (capability-context contracts not yet snapshot fields, no OS sandbox around the Pi process, unverified pi-subagents paths, truncated check logs). Observation: the entry still says the Harness implements Protocol 5 ownership/reference resolution and version-2 context handoffs, while the project's accepted Protocol is 9.0.0 with Profile 14 and the Module's own contracts define concorde-context-snapshot@6.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol 9 entry layout with grouped standalone entity anchors; the Relationships Mermaid flowchart carries accTitle/accDescr and labels every edge with a verb phrase.

nodes.name: permissions.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.harness (document.harness.permissions) explaining that availability of a document is not authority to change it: the worker profile declares maximum access, the host narrows it to the task's files and operations, and both must permit an action. It states that referencing another Module's Spec never makes its source writable, why the boundary is rechecked against current inputs and the intended worktree, that a rejection is not retried with broader access, and that the tool gate is a policy boundary inside the agent process rather than an OS sandbox.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.harness (document.harness.requirements) defining 24 Module-wide SHALL requirements across five subjects: context freezing (non-empty closure, scenario focus never trims membership, file names visible to every phase but contents only to code phases, Spec context delivered as an index plus read-only grant rather than embedded bodies, recheck rejects reuse after change, discovery never expands through relationships); profiles and permissions (a profile never exceeds its contract, effective permissions stay inside both grants, write authority only for code-writing invocations and never over Specs or the registry, no retry with a wider grant); configured checks (OS-enforced project read-only, fail closed when isolation is unavailable, fresh external scratch); worker execution (every tool call gated, per-worker model/thinking/timeout selection, capsule closed to its own snapshot, closed process inputs, no automatic retry, settling is not completion, one-level delegation, only the submitted result leaves); and typed values (canonical encoding digests identically).

nodes.name: runtime-values.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.harness (document.harness.runtime-values) that defines the exact in-process Python value records of the capability host: EffectDeclaration, PolicyBinding and compile_policy producing a digest-bound NormalizedPolicy with default-deny grants; Contract, Child, WorkerProfile and WorkerBinding together with validate_worker_profile, child_definitions, worker_profile and resolve_worker; the four validate_worker_input/artifacts/policy/output contract checks; and WorkerInvocation, WorkerExecutor, WorkerOutcome, ExecutionUsage and CapabilityExecutionError with its failed/cancelled/limit_exhausted/invalid_completion outcomes. Observation: the unit also carries a Design section on inline Mermaid relationship diagrams and the retired registry `diagrams` field, which is a Spec-representation topic rather than a capability runtime value, and its paired metadata declares no entities, so the Python modules realizing these records are bound by other module.harness units.
nodes.languageNotes: Contracts are given as Python signatures and attribute tables rather than JSON schemas, so the reading member is the canonical description of frozen dataclass-style records.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.harness (document.harness.scenarios) defining 31 GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios in two subject groups. The 22 Harness scenarios cover Flow inspection without authority, context freeze, invalid input, stale recheck, discovery of several explicit Module contexts and dependency gaps, external reference grants, worker binding and its rejection, permission compilation and refusal, candidate ownership, worktree boundary, execution success and failure outcomes, per-worker contract isolation, usage accounting to `.concorde/runs/<root>/usage.jsonl`, per-worker model selection and typed-value validation/rejection; the 9 Agent execution scenarios cover read-only sandboxed checks, scratch directories, result capture, unavailable enforcement and descendant lifetime, plus the Pi RPC client, Pi worker launch, its tool gate and one-level child delegation.

nodes.name: typed-values.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic owned by module.harness (document.harness.typed-values) introducing why results crossing a stage boundary need an agreed meaning and a checkable shape: a normal planner-to-task-author handoff where only an accepted, current result advances, why artifact identities derive from exact inputs through canonical serialization, and why contract validation stays offline and bounded. It states explicitly that shape checking cannot establish that a review or claim is true and defers schema vocabulary, envelope layouts and serialization rules to the Module's execution reference.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.implementation (document.implementation.execution-reference) defining the `implement` capability contract: it is a private bound provider admitted through the Development Module's invocation envelope, requires current authored tasks and their accepted plan as concorde-implementation-task@1, rejects a missing list with missing_tasks, grants a fresh programmer write access only to the selected Module's bound implementation paths (never Specs, registry, entity declarations or configuration, with network and credentials disabled), and returns concorde-implement-response@2 with every admitted task identity and acceptance preserved, reporting incomplete_tasks rather than ready. It further specifies deferred repository-level test verification as distinct from a pass and from a defect, the component-coordination limit that delegates scheduling and final shared-consumer checks to the enclosing development Flow, and the reuse limits of the shared adapter realization.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module-role reading entry of module.implementation (document.implementation.module) with the required Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships sections: implementation fulfills accepted tasks by changing only the code its worker may access, without weakening acceptance or claiming validation, readiness or delivery. Design anchors the Implementation adapter, Implementation task and Task completion entities and explains that failed execution can leave authorized partial edits rather than a rollback; Relationships carries the Mermaid flowchart and the three local collaboration agreements with Development (task admission and progress), Harness (bounded programmer grant) and Spec (code ownership resolution).

nodes.name: requirements.md
