nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.implementation (document.implementation.requirements) defining a single Module-wide requirement, req.implementation.admitted-contract, that implementation SHALL preserve every admitted task identity and acceptance condition when reporting completion.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.implementation (document.implementation.scenarios) defining four GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios: admitted-work (completion accepted only for the same task IDs with acceptance preserved and progress recorded without declaring ready or changing Specs), missing-tasks (rejected with missing_tasks before the programmer launches), incomplete-output (reported as incomplete_tasks while authorized edits stay inspectable) and failed-execution (no completion and no implied rollback; the candidate and progress are preserved and a retry re-admits current artifacts without wider permissions).

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.issues (document.issues.execution-reference) holding the Module's precise record and execution contracts: the bug/gap/limitation classification with gap subtypes, the Issue store boundary (concorde-issue-report@1 and concorde-issue-receipt@1, report_issue/read_issue/list_issues/resolve_report, `I-` plus 32 hex identities, 64 KiB report and 16 MiB record limits, the single JSON fence record format), the worker reporting service IssueReporter and its nonterminating `report_issue` tool, file-lock persistence and branch-local concurrency, the disposition boundary (dispose_issue, disposition_record, restore_issue), and the whole bounded solving lifecycle with its write-ahead journal and recovery rules. It also carries two executable Flow Specs, `issue_flow` (twelve nodes from select_operation through prepare, decide, develop, repair_spec, verify, close and ready) and `issue_verification_flow`, each with a node table and a `%% flow:`-bound Mermaid diagram.
nodes.languageNotes: The Mermaid fences carry the `%% flow: <name>` binding and `in:`/`out:` node labels required by Concorde's Flow Spec check, so the diagram is compared against the compiled LangGraph graph rather than being decorative.

nodes.name: interfaces.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.issues (document.issues.interfaces) defining the public Issue interface: concorde-issues-request@1 over the Development Module's common envelope with the actions list, show, report, reopen and solve, their required inputs and effects, append semantics through issue_id plus expected_revision, owner resolution rules, and the concorde-issues-response@1 result carrying complete records, a nullable decision and blocker references with a task-local blocked_step. It also specifies the worker `report_issue` tool returning {receipt, revision} and records that the legacy concorde-reflections-triage capability is retired while `scripts/issues.py archive-reflections` only moves an old queue into .concorde/archive/reflections/ without reclassification.

nodes.name: issues.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic owned by module.issues explaining what an Issue record is for: retaining a concrete observation beyond the current conversation with its impact, evidence and responsible Module, without stopping a task, changing code or authorizing repair. It explains appending follow-up evidence instead of rewriting history, idempotent repeats versus changed input, branch-local versioning, and what closing and reopening require. Observation: the paired metadata still declares the legacy document identity document.reflections.issues while the owner is module.issues.

nodes.name: lifecycle.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic owned by module.issues (document.issues.lifecycle) and the canonical definition site of the term Disposition. It explains that solving selects one Issue and routes it through the ordinary capabilities — Development Flow for clear implementation intent, Spec Authoring for a missing promise, Review for Issue-specific verification, or an explicit developer question when a product or design choice is unsettled — and why completion means a ready candidate with the disposition included in final validation rather than a merge, plus why an interrupted closing write must be recoverable and bounded.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module-role reading entry of module.issues (document.issues.module) with the required Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships sections: Issues keeps a durable branch-local record of observed problems and supports their explicit investigation, repair and verification without itself stopping work or authorizing code changes. Design anchors the Issue runtime, the Spec-only Issue solver and the LangGraph entity; Relationships carries the Mermaid collaboration view and the local agreements with Development, Spec, Development Flow, Spec Authoring, Review and Validation.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.issues (document.issues.requirements) defining four Module-wide requirements: req.issues.report-control (accepting a report SHALL NOT stop a worker, start repair or change task completion), req.issues.scope (selecting or reporting an Issue SHALL NOT widen a worker's Spec, implementation or command grant), req.issues.retention (disposition SHALL preserve the record and every original observation) and req.issues.ready-boundary (a successful solving flow SHALL stop at ready without delivery or primary merge).

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit owned by module.issues (document.issues.scenarios) defining 18 GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios in three subject groups: the Issue interface (inspect without starting work, admit only observed or granted references, blocker history independent of task wording, explicit legacy archival), the solving lifecycle (solve-ready, routing contract repair to the owner-only author, asking only for genuinely unsettled decisions, refusing stale selections, interrupted-disposition recovery and its unprovable-restoration refusal, and carrying an uncommitted selected report into the candidate) and records and reporting (reporting authority without write grants, nonterminating reports, survival of interrupted work, idempotent persistence, branch-independent concurrency, evidence-bound disposition history and rejection of malformed or unsafe persistence).

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Reading entry (document.concorde.module, role module) of the root Concorde Framework Module, which has no structural parent: it states the Framework's purpose, imports thirteen concepts from the Concepts terminology table, and gives a developer entry-point table mapping each installed Skill (concorde-main, -specify-loop, -review, -dev-loop, -init, -configure, -validate, -deliver, -issues) to its exact completion boundary. Design records that the Framework owns no product code and realizes its entry contract through sixteen child Modules, while its own binding is the Framework acceptance-test entity; Relationships carries two scoped Mermaid views (Flow composition and Runtime foundations) plus the project-wide diagram convention.
nodes.languageNotes: The entry deliberately delegates all unresolved business facts to the child Module that owns the affected contract, so its Unresolved information section is empty by design.

nodes.name: ownership-migration.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit (document.concorde.ownership-migration) preserving the historical capability-ownership ledger from the pre-Protocol-8 baseline: a table mapping roughly forty stable document, requirement and scenario identities from their former module.development owner and source path to their current owner and definition link across delivery, dev-loop, query-routing, review, planning, topology, validation and specify-loop, followed by a compatibility and evidence scope note stating that no runtime source was physically extracted and that affected revisions, contexts, plans and reviews need fresh evidence.
nodes.languageNotes: The ledger is explicitly labelled with its baseline so that historical locators are not mistaken for current behavior, as the Protocol requires of migration records.

nodes.name: assessment.md
nodes.summary: Explanatory topic (document role `module`) owned by module.planning that explains context assessment: whether the admitted Module Spec supplies enough meaning to plan one particular task, and why an explicit prohibition, a contradiction or a failed execution is a different outcome from a missing promise. It defines the term 'Task sufficiency', states that assessment is an internal capability rather than a developer Skill, and links exact obligations to the Module's execution reference.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol 9 explanatory topic: opens with an orienting paragraph, then Terminology as its first level-2 section, and carries no req./scenario definitions.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit owning Planning's precise execution and record contracts: `context-solve` sufficiency outcomes (sufficient, spec_incomplete, unsupported, conflicting, failed) with question/blocked_step/needed_contract gap attribution, the `plan` capability's revision-bound plan admission, and the `tasks` capability's reserved-task-ID rules around `concorde-task-identity-constraints@1` and `concorde-plan-artifact@1`. It also carries the `plan_flow` Flow Spec with its state, node table (assess_context, author_plan, persist_plan) and the bound Mermaid diagram, plus realization limits stating that these files share the existing Development adapter realization.
nodes.languageNotes: The Mermaid fence is bound to the compiled Flow by `%% flow: plan_flow`, and each node label repeats its `in:`/`out:` state so the deterministic Flow Spec check can compare diagram and code.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module reading entry (role `module`) for module.planning, with the required Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships sections. It explains that Planning assesses task sufficiency, produces a revision-bound plan and derives acceptance tasks without implementing work or declaring a candidate ready, and its Relationships flowchart ties the Planning adapter to the Development, Harness and Spec providers and to the Context assessment, Accepted plan and Acceptance tasks records. The per-provider subsections carry the local collaboration agreements referenced by the metadata companion.

nodes.name: plan.md
nodes.summary: Explanatory topic (role `module`) describing the normal planning path: assessment first, then a fresh planner that describes the work — naming separately owned participants rather than assuming access to their implementations — and a host that accepts only a nonempty plan bound to the task and Spec revision. A second section explains why plans go stale and that empty, invalid or stale output leaves the previously accepted plan intact without making it current.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit defining Planning's seven Module-wide SHALL requirements under four subject headings: req.planning.admitted-contract (assess sufficiency before persisting a plan), req.planning.assessment-context and req.planning.assessment-gap (assess only the selected contract; attribute gaps with question, blocked step, needed contract and provenance), req.planning.plan-rejection-preserves, and req.planning.tasks-require-plan, req.planning.tasks-admission and req.planning.task-collision-preserves for task authoring.
nodes.languageNotes: Each requirement is one level-3 heading `req.<id> — Title` followed by a single sentence containing SHALL exactly once, as the Protocol's requirement format demands.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit defining nine GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios for Planning: scenario.development.task-history-identities for reserved task identities, scenario.planning.assessment-sufficient and assessment-gap for context assessment, plan-current, plan-empty and plan-stale for the planning capability, and tasks-from-plan, tasks-missing-plan and tasks-id-conflict for task authoring. Observation: the first scenario carries a `scenario.development.*` identity while the unit is owned by module.planning; the Protocol states prefixes do not establish ownership, so this is an identity naming choice rather than a second owner.

nodes.name: tasks.md
nodes.summary: Explanatory topic (role `module`) about turning an accepted plan into verifiable implementation work. It defines the canonical terms 'Acceptance task' and 'Reserved task ID', explains that a fresh task author returns a nonempty list of initially incomplete tasks it cannot complete itself, and describes repair rounds that add new tasks without rewriting retained history.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit owning Query and Routing's precise execution contracts: how `concorde-main` starts from the entry Module's complete collection and expands only explicitly selected Module contexts, how single-target review and development routes return just `target_id` and nullable `focus_id` while the host copies the original task and ordered constraints (an unequal legacy echo fails with `incompatible_handoff`), and how a missing promise is reported as an attributed Spec gap distinct from a prohibition, contradiction or error. It carries two Flow Specs — `discovery_flow` (decide, expand_context, bind_routes, finish) and `query_flow` (discover, respond) — each with state, node table and a Mermaid diagram bound to the compiled Flow.
nodes.languageNotes: Both Mermaid fences carry `%% flow: <name>` bindings and label every edge with its routing condition, which is required because each source node has several successors.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module reading entry (role `module`) for module.query-routing, with Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships. It explains that the Module answers Spec-grounded questions through `concorde-main` and selects the one Module responsible for a task, that target/focus hints steer selection without granting reading authority, and that discovery expands provider references once rather than following links or code. Its Relationships flowchart ties the Query and Routing adapter to Development, Harness and Spec plus the Admitted selection record, and the per-provider subsections hold the local collaboration agreements.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit defining the Module's three SHALL requirements: req.development.global-discovery (a capability with discover context selection uses a discovery-phase worker over complete Module Spec contexts), req.development.routing-hint-not-context (a target or focus hint only steers selection) and req.development.routing-hint-no-grant (a hint never itself grants context or replaces explicit resolution). Observation: all three identities use a `req.development.*` prefix although the unit is owned by module.query-routing; under the Protocol prefixes do not establish ownership.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit defining three GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios: scenario.development.answer-question (a `concorde-main` ask resolves the selected Modules' complete contexts, indexes each document once, grants them read-only and returns a direct answer without project writes), scenario.development.answer-gap (a missing promise is reported as a Spec gap naming the blocked question, owning Module and context identity instead of reading code) and scenario.development.discovery-limit (a bounded expansion limit returns the `context_limit` outcome).

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit (document.concorde.requirements) defining the root Module's eight Framework-wide obligations: req.concorde.routing-no-access (a routing hint grants no access beyond the frozen context), read-no-mutate (read and preview operations do not modify Specs, implementation or topology), versioned-result (every invocation returns a versioned result distinguishing admission failure, execution failure and domain outcome), preserve-user-content, no-overwrite-initialized, delivery-separate, unsupported-explicit and no-stale-replay.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit owning Review's precise execution and record contracts: `concorde-review` as a public capability with discover context selection requiring task and review_mode=spec|code, the frozen `concorde-review-stage-context@4` / `concorde-review-input@1` inputs and what spec_digest and input_digest bind, the reviewer's `concorde-review-stage-result@2` with representative_tasks, Issue judgments and status, and the published `concorde-review-result@2` with semantic_completeness=not_proven. It maps review states to Skill outcomes in a table (no_findings, advisory findings, spec_incomplete, conflicting, failed, described, skipped), keeps cancelled/limit_exhausted as separate execution classifications, and its 'Scope and feedback relevance' section fixes per-listing-Module peer review of shared files, read-only grants and the rule that verification declarations are judged only for scenarios in the reviewing Module's admitted context.
nodes.languageNotes: Unlike the sibling Planning and Query-and-Routing execution references, this unit defines no Flow Spec diagram; its precision comes from digest-bound record contracts and an outcome mapping table.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module reading entry (role `module`) for module.review, with Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships. It defines the canonical terms 'Review coverage' and 'Advisory finding', explains that `concorde-review` runs a fresh read-only Spec or code reviewer that returns findings and the scope actually examined without repairing files, and stresses that a clean result is bounded evidence rather than proof of absence. The Relationships flowchart ties the Review adapter to Development, Harness, Spec and Query and Routing plus the Review input and Review result records, and the per-provider subsections carry the local collaboration agreements.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit defining Review's single Module-wide requirement, req.review.admitted-contract: Review SHALL return independent findings bound to its exact admitted task and current input revision. Its Terminology table imports only 'Evidence' and the locally defined 'Review coverage'.

nodes.name: review-result.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role interface unit defining the `concorde-review-result@2` typed envelope and its closed payload: context_id, input_digest, review_mode, status (no_findings, findings, incomplete, skipped, not_run), representative_tasks, issues, answer, target_id, focus_id, the revision object and semantic_completeness fixed to not_proven. It also defines the closed IssueJudgment (issue_id, report_id, path, severity blocking|advisory, affected_task) as a host-issued immutable receipt, rules out a parallel gaps array or free-text joins, and states how blocking judgments derive task-local blockers while version-1 results are rejected. Observation: its declared document identity is `document.development.review-result` although its owner is `module.review`; the Protocol allows this since identifier prefixes do not establish ownership.
nodes.languageNotes: The payload is specified as a field/type table with the shorthand `S` (nonblank string), `N` (nullable string) and `D` (sha256 digest) rather than a `concorde-contract` JSON fence.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit defining the single scenario scenario.development.standalone-review: in an initialized project with no managed change or preexisting Issue, invoking the public `concorde-review` Skill lets a Spec-only router select one owning Module, gives a separate fresh reviewer the complete contract and — in code mode — only the admitted implementation files and scoped changes, grants no write, network or credential authority, and returns typed coverage, findings, gaps and status with HEAD as the baseline for an unmanaged Git checkout.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit (document.concorde.scenarios) defining the root Module's eleven end-to-end GIVEN/WHEN/THEN situations: develop-change, develop-gap, develop-failure, inspect-answer, inspect-gap, adopt-initialize, adopt-conflict, configure-apply, validate-record, deliver-stage and issues. Together they describe the Framework's promised behavior from a developer request through a ready candidate, an attributed missing promise, project adoption, configuration, deterministic evidence, staged delivery and read-only Issue inspection.
nodes.languageNotes: These are the scenarios the Framework acceptance tests bound by the Module entry are expected to declare with the @verifies decorator.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.spec-authoring (document.spec-authoring.execution-reference) defining the precise `specify` capability contract: a private, bound adapter that only a declared in-process composition may call (direct Skill/CLI invocation is rejected), a fresh spec-engineer specify invocation with no inherited stage artifacts or implementation contents, and full owned document replacements returned in concorde-agent-stage-result@2 or attributed gaps with no replacements. It also states that a referencing author cannot replace a provider document, that invalid/foreign/stale output is rejected with prior bytes and blockers preserved, and the realization limits under which this Module shares Development's existing adapter rather than creating a new runtime package or public Skill.
nodes.languageNotes: Anchors `#authoring-spec-authoring-capability` and `#authoring-precise-specifications` are the stable link targets other Spec documents address.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module reading entry (role `module`, document.spec-authoring.module) of module.spec-authoring, following Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships. It explains that `specify` authors or revises only the selected Module's owned Spec documents from allowed specifications rather than from source code, that the author returns complete Markdown replacements the host checks and applies (never direct project writes), and that referencing a provider permits reading but not replacing its Spec. Its Relationships flowchart and per-collaborator sections define the Development, Harness and Spec agreement anchors and the Owned replacements record.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.spec-authoring (document.spec-authoring.requirements) holding the Module's single SHALL statement, `req.spec-authoring.admitted-contract` — Spec Authoring shall propose replacements only for the selected Module's owned documents. Its Terminology table imports Spec, Module and Ownership from their canonical tables.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.spec-authoring (document.spec-authoring.scenarios) defining five GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios: `admitted-work` (valid owner-bound replacements are applied after affected-consumer compatibility checks), `gap` (missing meaning yields attributed gaps and no replacements), `foreign-output` (a consumer cannot replace its provider's document), `stale-output` (changed admitted bytes, context or configuration reject prepared replacements) and `invalid-output` (invalid identity or metadata prevents application and does not clear prior blockers).

nodes.name: contracts.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.spec (document.spec.contracts) carrying the Module's canonical interface definitions: the SpecRepository signature block (`select`, `documents`, `contracts`, `entity_files`/`entity_for_path`, the `implementation_entries`/`implementation_paths`/`implementation_files`/`missing_entries` listing family, the external-reference queries and the `listing_users`/`affected_modules`/`covering_modules` reverse index), the required collaborator promises for the typed-data and bounded offline schema boundary, the stable-ID `spec_files`/`spec_context` queries with the version-1 `SpecResolution` record and its `{kind, id}` inclusion reasons, `context_users`, the selection and returned-value contract, the task-authoring transport values, the `validate_repository` validator interface, the concorde-init request/proposal shapes and executable boundary, and the Profile 14 / Protocol 9.0.0 / registry schema 5 configuration and admission details.
nodes.languageNotes: Anchor IDs such as `#registry-stable-id-spec-context-queries` and `#values-selection-and-returned-values` are the link targets other Modules address, so heading text may change without breaking references.

nodes.name: initialize.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.spec (document.spec.initialize) describing `concorde-init`'s propose/inspect/apply behavior. It defines the terms Initialization and Initial proposal, explains that a proposal carries the configuration, registry and a paired Module entry with absent-file preconditions, that business purpose and behavior stay explicit gaps rather than invented content, and that initialization pins Protocol 9.0.0 / Profile 14 with the installer-placed `.concorde/protocol/` manifest digest, failing with `not_installed` when that copy is absent.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module reading entry (role `module`, document.spec.module) of module.spec, the Module that owns Concorde's Spec model. Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships explain that the Module records which documents belong to each Module, resolves which specifications a task may read, checks structural consistency and creates an initial project specification without inventing business behavior. Its Relationships flowchart names the ten declared entities — Registry, Protocol binding, SpecRepository API, Validator, Initialization capability, Spec model, Typed values, File transactions, Protocol text and Protocol assets — and an Unresolved information section records that `spec_pair` is retired and that structural validation does not establish semantic completeness.

nodes.name: registry.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.spec (document.spec.registry) and the canonical Terminology table for Ownership, Composition, Use, Reference and Implementation binding. It explains why those relations are independent (using a provider does not make it a child, and reading its contract does not grant its implementation), how a Module selection expands references exactly one level, why a document split forces consumers to reference any new unit explicitly, and how the context-user and implementation reverse indexes answer different review questions. A Checkout/Inventory/Tax example makes the one-level rule concrete.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.spec (document.spec.requirements) holding 31 SHALL statements grouped under four subject headings. Spec covers metadata resolution without reading collaborator bodies, one owning entity per bound file, directory-prefix binding, no Spec document inside a listed directory, sibling sharing and the prohibition on presenting structural checks as semantic proof; Registry covers no writes during construction or queries, snapshot semantics, reconstruction, deterministic ordering and local-only `contracts`; Spec structure and validation covers structural-only checking, separately executed host checks with registered argv and a source digest per assessment; Project initialization covers the allowed file set, null before_digests, absent destinations, the exact concorde-project-proposal envelope, configuration roles, worktree handoff reporting and no blind retries.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.spec (document.spec.scenarios) defining 28 GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios across five subject groups: registry admission and rejection, shared files, external references and directory-prefix binding; Module/scenario selection, focus rejection and `query-files`; unsupported profile rejection and bounded task-metadata admission; twelve validation scenarios covering success, structural errors, pending warnings, diagram mismatches, ID-shaped link anchors, test verification declarations, reader-oriented structure, internal contracts, document roles and reference resolution; and five initialization scenarios covering propose, apply, already-initialized, stale or invalid proposals and rollback on failure. Prose after the validation group records that scripts/development/check-spec-v5.py is maintenance-only documentation evidence, not a lifecycle check.

nodes.name: structure.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.spec (document.spec.structure) and the canonical Terminology source for Structural validation and Semantic completeness. It explains what deterministic registry, reference, interface and terminology checks establish — detecting missing documents, duplicate identities, conflicting owners, unincluded definitions and mismatched participant versions — and insists that success does not prove an implementation is correct or a promise sufficient.

nodes.name: values.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic of module.spec (document.spec.values) and the canonical Terminology source for Document unit, Document role, Source-member role and Protocol binding. It distinguishes stable identities (Module, document, requirement, scenario) from snapshot identity, which changes whenever relevant bytes or declarations change, and explains that Protocol, Framework configuration, registry storage and worker-message versions are separate compatibility numbers, with plans and task lists treated as workflow artifacts rather than additional specifications.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.specify-loop (document.specify-loop.execution-reference) defining the precise `concorde-specify-loop` contract and its executable Flow Spec. It fixes the public request (task plus optional target/focus hints, constraints, change_id, specify and run_reviews, both booleans defaulting true), the committed-base handoff for mutating primary requests, reuse of accepted authoring only for the same intent, sticky Spec review requirements, and the boundary that the flow never plans, writes code, runs code checks, requires code review, marks ready or delivers. The Design section specifies the `specify_flow` State (`output`, `artifacts` under a merge reducer, `result`), a four-row Nodes table (`initialize`, `specify`, `review_spec`, `summarize`) with `in`/`out` channels, and the bound Mermaid flowchart carrying `%% flow: specify_flow` with labelled routing conditions.
nodes.languageNotes: The diagram is a LangGraph Flow Spec: node identifiers match the compiled node names including `__start__`/`__end__`, and every edge out of a multi-successor node carries its routing condition as a label.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module reading entry (role `module`, document.specify-loop.module) of module.specify-loop, titled Specification Flow. Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships explain that the Flow prepares or revises one Module's specification and obtains independent review before any coding, that `specify=false` reviews the existing contract while `run_reviews=false` records a skip only where no requirement already exists, and that completion returns Spec-stage artifacts rather than tasks, readiness or delivery. Its flowchart and six collaborator sections define the agreement anchors for Development, Harness, Spec, Query and Routing, Spec Authoring and Review, plus the "Spec completion" record.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.specify-loop (document.specify-loop.requirements) holding the Module's single SHALL statement — concorde-specify-loop shall complete Spec preparation independently of implementation readiness. Observation: the identity is `req.development.specify-loop-boundary` rather than a `req.specify-loop.` prefix; the Protocol permits this because prefixes do not establish ownership, and the owner remains module.specify-loop through the paired metadata.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role Spec unit of module.specify-loop (document.specify-loop.scenarios) defining one GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenario, `scenario.development.specify-loop` — authoring and reviewing a Spec independently: routing the owning Module, accepting only owned replacements, covering the complete contract and affected consumers with independent reviews, returning completed with artifact references and no readiness or code-review requirement, honouring the specify/run_reviews switches, stopping with inspectable progress on blocking findings, and resuming accepted authoring for a repeated intent including when concorde-dev-loop calls it first. Observation: like the requirements unit, the scenario ID carries the `development.` prefix while ownership stays with module.specify-loop.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.topology holding the Topology evolution Agent Flow and its two executable Flow Specs: `topology_flow` (prepare_authors, author_module, validate_candidate, review_contexts, persist_application) and `topology_apply_flow` (admit_application, validate_application, apply_atomically, cleanup), each with a State part, a Node/in/out table and a `%% flow:`-bound Mermaid diagram whose edges carry their routing conditions. It also fixes the stop conditions — author gap, invalid candidate, blocked review, stale or rejected application, failed transaction — and the realization limits stating that this boundary adds no new runtime package, Skill or Agent grant.
nodes.languageNotes: The two diagrams are the authoritative executable topology: node identifiers match the compiled LangGraph node names including `__start__` and `__end__`, so the configured Flow Spec check can compare them against the built graphs.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Reading entry (role `module`) of module.topology: explains when a change must alter Module identities, composition, document ownership, references and file bindings together, and why such a change passes two separate human acceptances — first the responsibility design, then the exact prepared application. Its Relationships and provider-collaboration sections declare what Topology relies on from Development (host admission and atomic application), Harness (isolated designers, owner-local authors and independent reviewers), Spec (ownership and old/candidate context resolution plus structural validation) and Query and Routing (explicit complete-context discovery).
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the Protocol 9 entry order Purpose / Terminology / Usage / Design / Relationships; its first Mermaid figure is explicitly labelled a conceptual view of the two human decisions and defers the executable node/edge topology to the implementation-role execution reference.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.topology defining its single Module-wide obligation, `req.development.shared-document-agreement`: a referenced document change SHALL be applied only from its sole owner's proposal after compatibility review in every affected consumer's resolved context. Observation: the requirement keeps the `development.` identity prefix although the defining unit is owned by module.topology — legitimate under the Protocol, which states prefixes do not establish ownership, but the name does not reveal the owner.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.topology defining four GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios for the `concorde-main` topology actions: `topology-design` (digest-bound candidate registry with no project writes), `topology-accept` (fresh target-local authors, combined overlay validation, full documents kept in a before-digest-bound artifact exposed only as an ArtifactRef), `topology-apply` (one atomic transaction) and `topology-stale` (stale, non-owner or unresolved-compatibility input is rejected and leaves files unchanged). Observation: the scenario identities carry the `development.` prefix although the owning Module is module.topology.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.validation defining the exact `concorde-validate` capability contract and the configured-check execution rules: required target_id and task with optional run_checks, host-admitted argv with an initial `{python}` expanded to the interpreter, delegation to Harness `execute_check(project_root, argv, timeout=..., environment=...)` with `PYTHONPATH` set to the package `src`, external scratch for temporary/cache/report paths, and OS denial of any project write by the check and its descendants. It fixes the record shapes and failure encodings — private byte stdout/stderr written only by the host to `.concorde/runs/<invocation_id>/<check_id>.log`, public evidence of exactly `check_id`, `target_id`, `status`, `exit_code`, `source_digest` and `log_digest`, timeout as exit code -1, and `CheckSandboxError` surfaced as `SpecError/check_sandbox_unavailable` — plus the freshness rule that the execution-policy identity `project-read-only-v1` participates in the digest.
nodes.languageNotes: Unlike the topology companion, this implementation-role unit defines a capability and record contract rather than a LangGraph Flow Spec, so it carries no `%% flow:`-bound diagram.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Reading entry (role `module`) of module.validation: explains that `concorde-validate` is a deterministic capability which launches no Agent, collects structural Spec evidence and configured-check results bound to the current candidate bytes, and then evaluates existing task and review gates to decide readiness — while explicitly never repairing defects, delivering a change or claiming semantic completeness. Its Design and provider sections declare the collaborations with Development (admission, private logs, evidence and gate evaluation), Harness (OS-enforced project-read-only check execution) and Spec (structural validation and affected-consumer resolution), and state that unavailable isolation fails closed rather than falling back to an unrestricted runner.
nodes.languageNotes: Names a concrete current platform limit in reading content rather than hiding it in detail links: the isolated runner requires Linux with system bubblewrap and working namespace/pidfd support, and validation stops when that boundary is unavailable.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.validation defining its single Module-wide obligation, `req.development.check-isolation`: validation SHALL execute configured checks through the Harness Module's OS-enforced project-read-only executor. Observation: the requirement keeps the `development.` identity prefix although the defining unit is owned by module.validation, and the unit states honestly that it needs no specialized terminology instead of inventing table rows.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit of module.validation defining three GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios: `validate-ready` (deterministic Spec validation plus every configured check of every affected Module, recorded against the exact candidate bytes and never claiming semantic completeness), `validate-blocked` (a failed, missing or stale check keeps the candidate from being recorded ready) and `validate-check-isolation` (project and lifecycle writes are denied by Harness, the outside host keeps private stdout/stderr and passed/failed/timeout evidence, and unavailable enforcement blocks readiness with `check_sandbox_unavailable`). Observation: the scenario identities carry the `development.` prefix although the owning Module is module.validation.

nodes.name: contracts.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit holding the canonical structured interface contracts of module.views: contract.views.scaffold-proposal version 2 for the docsite scaffold exchange and ownership, the publication pipeline's TypeScript interface signatures, public model types and build/validation/promotion artifacts, the required installed-runtime contract for the viewer, contract.views.ua-overlay-input version 1 for the locally serialized graph an overlay may admit, and the native UA analysis contract.

nodes.name: execution-reference.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit defining the publication pipeline's execution and record contracts: the docsite/.generated/scoped-materialization.json identity and its postBuild digest and route checks, the project-introduction and custom-documentation entry points, Mermaid rendering constraints, the Module Specs and Implementation Specs sidebars derived from registry parentage, the exact Markdown link-rewriting algorithm and its query/fragment handling, legacy redirect stubs, Module main-document validation rules, production versus preview generated directories and the Profile 14 / schema 21 compatibility status.

nodes.name: module.md
nodes.summary: Module entry of module.views (document role `module`), following Purpose, Terminology, Usage, Design and Relationships. It explains publishing registered Specs as a docsite, registry-derived UA graph export, the native UA analysis bridge and viewer launch, and defines the Publication docsite, Publication scaffold, UA graph exporter, UA analysis bridge, Viewer launcher, Canonical page, Candidate site and Published site entities with three relationship diagrams, plus the local collaboration agreements with Spec, Distribution and Harness.

nodes.name: pipeline.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic that defines the Publication candidate and Promotion terms and explains why publication separates source admission, candidate generation, validation and promotion, so that a half-rendered or stale build never replaces the working published site, with preview and production kept on separate build caches.

nodes.name: publication.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic on the publication service: the two reading paths (Module Specs and Implementation Specs) into one complete Module specification, how an explicit document role selects a tab without changing canonical routes, ownership or agent context, the creation-only scaffold, candidate materialization and promotion, and project documentation tabs that stay outside registered Spec context.

nodes.name: requirements.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit defining the 23 Module-wide SHALL requirements of module.views: registry-derived pages and navigation, no directory or link-based discovery, one canonical page per registered document, reading tabs that preserve one complete Module specification, resolving published internal links, no agent-context grant from a rendered view, the Mermaid fence as sole diagram source, removal of the docsite graph view, the Concorde-only Agent Flows tab, production/preview isolation, sha256 digest and safe relative path formats, atomic promotion of checked candidates, and the viewer and UA-exporter prohibitions on graph generation, freshness checks, dependency installation and non-registry derivation.

nodes.name: scenarios.md
nodes.summary: Implementation-role unit holding the 37 GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios of module.views, grouped by subject: publication service (scaffold propose, apply and stale rejection, candidate publication, reading collections and their rejection, homepage variants, custom docs, Protocol tab, legacy redirects, reference links), publication pipeline (Agent Flows, registry loading, materialization, identity anchors, buildSite, candidate mismatch), viewer launch and its failure modes, UA graph skeleton, overlay, shared-file layer, --check and invalid input, and native UA analysis inputs, host ownership, admission, output gate, failure handling and the permission probe.

nodes.name: ua-graph.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic covering both graph-generation paths: the deterministic registry-only exporter (ua-graph with --check and --allow-primary-worktree, its overlay ownership scope, the reserved concorde-ua-graph tag and layer namespace, and the default .ua/knowledge-graph.json target), and the native analysis bridge (ua-analyze) with its plugin and runtime prerequisites, the --approve-native-tools permission overlay, the bounded live permission probe, the prepared seed and per-Module Spec context indexes, run artifacts retained under .concorde/runs/, and failure, timeout and stale-lock recovery.

nodes.name: viewer.md
nodes.summary: Module-role explanatory topic for the deterministic Understand Anything viewer service entered at scripts/run-ua-graph-viewer.py: its --project-root, --port and --no-open argument contracts, the routing boundary against module.distribution for runtime acquisition and package verification, and its standing as a developer tool that launches no model cognition and grants no additional implementation access.

nodes.name: FLOW_AUDIT.md
nodes.summary: In-tree audit log written by successive Development capability invocations, each stamped with its invocation ID and context digest. It records a scoped-review scheduler freshness repair, a fresh implementation recheck, a table of the executing LangGraph topologies (capability admission, discovery, scoped local/component review batch, component coordination, stabilization, specification/development stops), interruption and preservation evidence, and the exact unittest command that failed to import `concorde.spec.typed_data` under the invocation's grant — so execution is explicitly deferred to Host rather than claimed as passing. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity. Observation: it is an implementation file bound as implementation, not a registered Protocol document unit, so its claims carry no Spec authority.

nodes.name: module-template.md
nodes.summary: Three-line pointer entry that redirects Module authors to the canonical Module starter in the Spec Protocol (`protocol/templates/module.md`) together with `protocol/format.md`, stating explicitly that it maintains no second template definition. Bound by module.distribution as part of the 'Installation' entity (which binds the whole `templates/` prefix), so the build ships it into installed projects; like every template it is an authoring starter, never evidence that a written Module Spec conforms.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeping the canonical starter in the Protocol bundle and shipping only a pointer avoids two competing template definitions drifting apart.

nodes.name: plan-template.md
nodes.summary: Starter skeleton for a change plan: a header line carrying target_id, optional scenario focus and context_id, an 'Intended behavior' section for the task and constraints, and a 'Contract changes and acceptance' section whose bracketed instruction tells the planner to use only the complete selected Spec and to name missing facts as gaps instead of inferring requirements from code. Bound by module.distribution through the 'Installation' entity's `templates/` prefix and shipped by the build as one of the four declared templates.
nodes.languageNotes: The bracketed placeholders encode the planner's context rule (Spec-only, gaps named explicitly) directly in the starter, so the prohibition on reading implementation to fill missing meaning travels with the artifact.

nodes.name: scenario-template.md
nodes.summary: Pointer entry that redirects authors to the canonical Scenario fragment in the Spec Protocol (`protocol/templates/scenario.md`), to be used inside a Module's registered document collection together with `protocol/format.md`, and states it keeps no separate template definition. Bound by module.distribution through the 'Installation' entity's `templates/` prefix; it scaffolds GIVEN/WHEN/THEN authoring but proves nothing about a scenario's completeness.

nodes.name: tasks-template.md
nodes.summary: Starter skeleton for a task list, stating that each task has id, target_id, description, acceptance and a boolean complete flag, that tasks are derived from the accepted plan (domain tasks select participating components, component tasks retain the selected target), and that no implementation file content is inspected during task authoring. Bound by module.distribution through the 'Installation' entity's `templates/` prefix; it is an authoring starter, not proof that authored tasks satisfy the plan.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Operator guide for Concorde's Understand Anything graph view across eight sections: generating a combined Spec and code graph with the ua-analyze native bridge and its permission flags, when export versus viewer startup is needed, source-checkout and installed-project launch routes, graph file locations and refresh semantics, startup troubleshooting, and the pinned official viewer runtime lock with its release, SHA-256 and byte count. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.managed-runtime through the viewer/ directory prefix.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: The single inventory of executable LangGraph Capabilities: a `CAPABILITIES` tuple naming all 26 entries (main, dev_loop, specify_loop, issues, init, configure, validate, deliver, specify, review, context_solve, plan, tasks, implement and the model-backed workers) plus `external_name`, which derives each entry's public `concorde-...` identifier. Its docstring fixes the contract every entry must declare (PUBLIC, CONTEXT_SELECTION, DETERMINISTIC, USES, STATE, run(state, runtime), optional PROFILE) and states that all composition names entries here, with no separate AGENTS registry. Bound by module.distribution as Build and by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Model-backed `answerer` Capability. It declares a WorkerProfile bound to capabilities/answerer/spec.md that runs in a capsule workspace for the route/ask contract, with discovery-context effects, read-only tools (read, grep, find, ls), a 900-second timeout and the outcomes completed/expand/spec_incomplete/unsupported/conflicting; `run` delegates to `run_model`. Bound by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Model-backed `code_reviewer` Capability. Its WorkerProfile runs the code-review phase in the project workspace with spec-context, implementation and references effects, read-only tools, a 3600-second timeout and two declared children (scout and verifier, each bound to its own instruction file); `run` delegates to `run_model`. Bound by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: configure.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic public Capability that applies the project's Pi worker model selection and, only on an explicit `accept_protocol` request, rebinds the project to the Protocol the installer placed under .concorde/protocol/ — its comment states this is the only way an updated installed Protocol becomes the binding, because install and update never rewrite it silently. It selects no context, runs no agent cognition, declares typed REQUEST/RESPONSE shapes and delegates `run` to `run_host`. Bound by module.distribution as Installation and by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Model-backed `context_assessor` Capability. Its WorkerProfile runs the context-solve phase in a capsule workspace with spec-context effects, read-only tools, a 1800-second timeout and the outcomes sufficient/spec_incomplete/unsupported/conflicting; `run` delegates to `run_model`. Bound by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: context_solve.py
nodes.summary: Non-public Capability that assesses a task for missing Spec information within one frozen context; it declares `USES = ('context_assessor',)`, a task REQUEST that requires a target, and delegates `run` to `run_host`. Its docstring states it is never projected as a user-invocable Skill and that the executable boundary has no direct entry for it. Bound by module.planning as the Planning adapter, module.development as a development capability and module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: deliver.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic public Capability that stages a verified change, cleans up and explicitly merges it from the primary session. Its REQUEST carries change_id, target_id, task, focus_id, constraints and the `keep_worktree` / `merge_primary` switches; it selects no context, runs no agent cognition and delegates `run` to `run_host`. Bound by module.delivery as the Delivery adapter, module.development as a development capability and module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: dev_loop.py
nodes.summary: Public development-loop Capability that routes one change, composes specify_loop for Spec preparation, then plans, tasks, implements, validates and reviews code to a ready candidate; `specify=false` skips Spec authoring and `run_reviews=false` records an explicit skip per review mode without disabling an already-recorded requirement. `FLOW = {"max_repair_iterations": 2}` bounds the loop's only automatic revision edge (review_code -> tasks), and the docstring notes that FLOW is persisted per target in .concorde/worktree.json so a resumed loop keeps the policy it started with. Bound by module.dev-loop as the Development Flow adapter, module.development as a development capability and module.harness as Model execution profiles.
nodes.languageNotes: `GRAPH = FLOW` is kept as an alias so persisted records and older Python integrations retain their existing identifiers.

nodes.name: implement.py
nodes.summary: Non-public Capability that implements or investigates tasks under a host-granted code boundary; it declares `USES = ('programmer',)`, a target-required task REQUEST and delegates `run` to `run_host`, and its docstring states it is never projected as a user-invocable Skill. Bound by module.implementation as the Implementation adapter, module.development as a development capability and module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: init.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic public Capability that proposes and then applies explicit project initialization with a pinned Protocol and an honest registry stub. Its REQUEST carries the propose/apply action, project name, target_id, typed configuration and project proposal; its RESPONSE returns the status, the proposal (or null) and the list of written files. It selects no context and delegates `run` to `run_host`. Bound by module.spec as the Spec model and by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Model-backed `issue_solver` Capability. Its WorkerProfile runs the issue-solve phase in a capsule workspace with spec-context effects and read-only tools, requires exactly the `concorde-issue-selection` stage input and produces the `issue_decision` output field; `run` delegates to `run_model`. Bound by module.issues as the Issue solver and by module.harness as Model execution profiles.

nodes.name: issues.py
nodes.summary: Declarative adapter for the public `concorde-issues` capability: it builds the request/response contract shapes for listing, showing, reporting, solving and reopening branch-local Issues, declares bound context selection plus the composed capabilities it uses (issue_solver, dev_loop, specify, review, validate), and delegates execution to the harness through `run_host`. Bound by module.issues as entity.issues.runtime (Issue runtime) and by module.harness as part of entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).
nodes.languageNotes: The module body is pure declaration: shapes composed from `concorde.spec.contract_shapes` become the capability's JSON request/response schemas, and the only executable code is a two-line LangGraph node.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: Adapter for the public `concorde-main` capability, whose four actions answer questions, route work, and design, accept or apply a system topology; it declares discovery context selection, the composed workers it uses (answerer, router, topology_designer, topology_author), and a response carrying routes, discovered targets, a typed topology proposal and workspace context. Bound by module.query-routing as entity.query-routing.adapter (Query and Routing adapter), by module.topology as entity.topology.adapter, by module.development as entity.development.development-capabilities and by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions.
nodes.languageNotes: One file carries the contract of two Modules' entry points: the same adapter is listed by module.query-routing and module.topology, which the Protocol allows as a shared implementation file.

nodes.name: plan.py
nodes.summary: Adapter for the internal `plan` capability, which plans a change from one complete Module Spec without implementation access and composes the context assessor and planner workers; its docstring states it is never projected as a user-invocable Skill, matching `PUBLIC = False`. Bound by module.planning as entity.planning.adapter (Planning adapter), and also listed by module.development and module.harness.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Model-backed worker profile for the `planner` agent: it declares the capsule workspace, phase `plan`, the `concorde-agent-stage-context` / `concorde-agent-stage-result` wire contracts, a read-only effect declaration over Spec context and external references, the `concorde-plan-artifact` stage input, the `plan` output field, read-only file tools, a single `scout` child bound to `capabilities/planner/children/scout.md` and a 1800-second timeout, then delegates to `run_model`. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Worker profile for the `programmer` agent, the only profile in this batch that runs in the project workspace with write authority: phase `implementation`, effects granting Spec context, implementation and references with implementation writes, a required `concorde-implementation-task` stage input alongside an optional `concorde-review-result`, editing and check-running tools, three children (scout, planner, verifier) and a 3600-second timeout. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).
nodes.languageNotes: The `EffectDeclaration` is where write permission is granted: every other worker in this batch declares an empty write tuple, so the permission difference is visible as data rather than as code branching.

nodes.name: review.py
nodes.summary: Adapter for the public `concorde-review` capability, which routes an observational task and then independently reviews the target's Spec or code read-only; it declares a `review_mode` enum of `spec` or `code`, requires an array of `concorde-review-result` values in its response, and composes the router, spec reviewer and code reviewer workers. Bound by module.review as entity.review.adapter (Review adapter), and also listed by module.development and module.harness.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Worker profile for the `router` agent: phase `route` with action `route`, the `concorde-main-stage-context` / `concorde-main-stage-result` wire contracts, a discovery-context-only effect declaration, a `routes` output field and the closed outcome set routed, expand, spec_incomplete, unsupported and conflicting, with read-only tools and a 900-second timeout. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Worker profile for the `spec_author` agent: capsule workspace, phase `specify`, agent-stage context and result contracts, a read-only Spec-context effect declaration and a `documents` output field carrying the Markdown replacements the host applies, with a 1800-second timeout. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Worker profile for the `spec_reviewer` agent: capsule workspace, phase `spec-review`, the dedicated `concorde-review-stage-context` / `concorde-review-stage-result` wire contracts, a read-only Spec-context effect declaration and two children (fact-check and consistency) bound to their Markdown definitions, with a 1800-second timeout. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: specify.py
nodes.summary: Adapter for the internal `specify` capability, which authors the selected target's complete Spec documents by composing the spec_author worker over a bound context; its docstring states it is never projected as a user-invocable Skill, matching `PUBLIC = False`. Bound by module.spec-authoring as entity.spec-authoring.adapter (Spec Authoring adapter), and also listed by module.development and module.harness.

nodes.name: specify_loop.py
nodes.summary: Adapter for the public `concorde-specify-loop` capability: the Spec loop that routes a task, authors or revises the Spec and then reviews it independently, stopping with a completed Spec result or an attributed blocker; its `specify` and `run_reviews` request flags let a caller review an existing Spec without authoring, and it composes the router, specify and review capabilities. Bound by module.specify-loop as entity.specify-loop.adapter (Specification Flow adapter), and also listed by module.development and module.harness.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Worker profile for the `task_author` agent: capsule workspace, phase `tasks`, agent-stage context and result contracts, read-only Spec context and references, five accepted stage inputs (plan artifact, task identity constraints, implementation task, review result and task scope feedback) of which the plan artifact and identity constraints are required, and a `tasks` output field. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: tasks.py
nodes.summary: Adapter for the internal `tasks` capability, which turns an admitted plan into implementation tasks with observable acceptance conditions and accepts a `repair_task_scope` digest for re-authoring an incomplete list; its docstring states it is never projected as a user-invocable Skill. Bound by module.planning as entity.planning.adapter (Planning adapter), and also listed by module.development and module.harness.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Worker profile for the `topology_author` agent, which authors the documents of one accepted target descriptor from a topology proposal: phase `topology-author` with its own `concorde-topology-author-context` / `concorde-topology-author-result` contracts, a read-only Spec-context effect declaration and a `documents` output field. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Worker profile for the `topology_designer` agent, which designs one candidate topology change from explicitly selected complete Module Specs and the registry: phase `route` with action `design-topology`, main-stage context and result contracts, discovery-context-only effects, a `topology_design` output field and the outcome set topology_proposed, expand, spec_incomplete, unsupported and conflicting. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-definitions (Model execution profiles).

nodes.name: validate.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic capability module for running the configured Spec and code checks and recording candidate readiness; it declares PUBLIC/CONTEXT_SELECTION/DETERMINISTIC metadata, the request and response contract shapes and a StateContract, then delegates `run` to the harness `run_host`. Bound by module.validation as entity.validation.adapter (Validation adapter), by module.development as Development capabilities and by module.harness as Model execution profiles.
nodes.languageNotes: Module-level constants (PUBLIC, CONTEXT_SELECTION, DETERMINISTIC, USES, REQUEST/RESPONSE, STATE) form the declarative capability contract that the registry and Flow inspection read.

nodes.name: flows.py
nodes.summary: Build-time exporter that compiles Concorde's own LangGraph Flows without invoking them and emits their nodes, edges, capability metadata and source digests as JSON for the Concorde-only docsite pages. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `flow.get_graph(xray=True)` for static inspection and stub node callables, so drawing the graphs never executes a capability; imports are deliberately deferred inside `export` to keep module import cheap.

nodes.name: graphs.py
nodes.summary: Compatibility entry point that loads flows.py by file path with importlib and re-exposes its `export` function plus a JSON-printing CLI. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite). Observation: the Spec declares the docsite program as a whole and does not describe this shim or the older name it preserves.

nodes.name: navigation.ts
nodes.summary: Pure navigation helpers for Concorde's Agent Flows page: builds the Capabilities / Shared flows / Guides sidebar groups from compiled Flow data, resolves a URL hash (including legacy stage anchors) to a selectable entry, and filters groups by a search query. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity, whose Spec describes concorde-only assets as project-owned extensions excluded from the packaged template.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Docusaurus React page rendering Concorde's Agent Flows tab: a hand-laid-out SVG diagram of compiled LangGraph nodes and edges, per-step detail cards, capability relation panels, and the CapabilityFlows shell with sidebar navigation, search, hash-driven selection and source provenance. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity; it realizes req.views.agent-flows, the Concorde-only execution view that the Spec excludes from the consumer template.
nodes.languageNotes: Most of the file is large static record literals of prose (step kind, agent, input, output, detail, handoff, stop reasons); the diagram is positioned with manual SVG coordinates instead of a graph layout library.

nodes.name: plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Docusaurus plugin that runs docsite/concorde-only/flows.py through the project Python interpreter to load compiled Capability and Flow data, registers the /agent-flows route with page.tsx, declares watched executable-factory sources, and re-hashes every declared source in postBuild so a source change during publication fails the build. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity.
nodes.languageNotes: Observation: getPathsToWatch still watches src/concorde/reflections/*.py, but the current source tree has src/concorde/issues/ and no reflections package; the other watched paths (development, harness, capabilities) exist.

nodes.name: style.module.css
nodes.summary: CSS module for the Concorde-only capability/flow page: a sticky-sidebar grid layout, flow-diagram canvas and node/edge styling, step and handoff cards, stop-reason callouts and responsive collapse of the navigation below 800px. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).
nodes.languageNotes: Theme-aware via Docusaurus Infima variables and `:global([data-theme='dark'])`, with explicit `:focus-visible` outlines so the diagram controls stay keyboard-accessible.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Type-only module declaring the FlowData shape the Agent Flows plugin loads from flows.py: compiled node/edge graphs, per-capability metadata (public, context_selection, deterministic, uses, State input and output), loops, factory sources, repair policy and digest-bound source records. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Concorde's project-owned CustomDocsExtension entry point: adds the Agent Flows plugin and its navbar item to the packaged docsite template without changing shared template code. The docsite README and the Views Spec describe this file as an example of a project-owned extension that generic scaffolding never copies into consumer sites. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity.

nodes.name: sidebars.protocol.ts
nodes.summary: Typed Docusaurus sidebar for the Spec Protocol documentation tab, listing the overview, principles and Module chapters, the Spec management category with Spec and Context, the required format and the Module/scenario templates. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: docusaurus.config.ts
nodes.summary: Docusaurus site configuration for the Concorde publication docsite: loads the validated site identity and Profile 14 scoped registry, serves staged `.generated/content/specs` through the classic docs preset with the concorde-content plugin, custom-docs plugins and local search, and adds the Implementation Specs navbar tab only when implementation-role pages exist. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity. Observation: `requireScoped` runs only after `loadScopedRegistry` and `customDocsConfiguration`, so a non-Profile-14 project first fails with the loader's generic message rather than the dedicated profile error.

nodes.name: contract-schema.ts
nodes.summary: Bounded offline JSON-Schema subset validator: admits a canonical `concorde-contract` schema (fixed keyword vocabulary, direct `#/$defs/` references only, nesting limit) and checks the contract's example against it. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite); realizes the pipeline rule that contract examples are checked offline without loading remote or Spec resources.

nodes.name: custom-docs.ts
nodes.summary: Builds Docusaurus plugin, navbar and search settings for project-owned customDocs collections and the optional `custom-docs/index.ts` extension, rejecting collections that contain registered Spec sources and malformed extension exports. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite); keeps custom docs separate from registered Spec context.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: The `concorde-content` Docusaurus plugin: loads the scoped registry and requires a matching materialization identity, publishes page metadata without bodies as global data, watches config/registry/source members, and in postBuild checks source freshness and route coverage, then writes build-manifest.json (schema 21) and legacy alias redirect stubs; it also exports `validateScopedBuild`, which checks a candidate's manifest, stubs and internal links before promotion. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite). Observation: `validateScopedBuild` does not call `requireScoped` itself and relies on the loader's own Profile 14 check.

nodes.name: internal-links.ts
nodes.summary: Parses every HTML file of a built candidate with parse5 and verifies that required page routes, internal links, meta-refresh redirects and fragment anchors resolve within the configured site origin and base URL, following alias redirects with cycle detection and never fetching URLs. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite); implements the published-internal-links check.

nodes.name: materialize.ts
nodes.summary: Stages publication inputs: writes each registered page with rewritten links, definition anchors and Docusaurus front matter under `docsite/.generated/content/specs`, generates the registry-parent `moduleSpecsSidebar` and the optional `implementationSpecsSidebar`, and finally records the `scoped-materialization.json` source-digest identity. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: model.ts
nodes.summary: Core Profile 14 publication model: symlink-free strict UTF-8 source reading, the Profile 14 guard, and `loadScopedRegistry`, which validates registry schema 5, paired document units and metadata, entity file bindings, one-level references and inclusion provenance, relationship diagrams, terminology links and canonical contract bindings before returning schema-21 pages with canonical routes, legacy aliases and a source digest; it also rewrites local Markdown links and injects definition anchors. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite). Observation: `Target.references` also admits and validates `{kind: "external", path}` entries, whereas the Views public model types declare only module/document reference kinds.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on TypeScript assertion signatures (`requireThat(...): asserts value`) so each validation step also narrows the types used afterwards.

nodes.name: reading-format.ts
nodes.summary: Protocol reading and metadata admission helpers: strict JSON parsing (duplicate keys, non-finite numbers), fence-aware prose/heading/fence scanning, anchor meaning extraction, Terminology table checks, module.md section order, role-based placement of formal definitions and Flow catalogs, requirement/scenario syntax, schema-2 metadata validation and Relationships flowchart label extraction. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite). Observation: its header comment and a metadata error message still cite Protocol 8, although the accepted Protocol is 9.0.0 and the checks already include its Terminology rules.
nodes.languageNotes: Fence handling blanks fenced lines to spaces instead of deleting them, so regex offsets computed on the prose view stay aligned with the original Markdown.

nodes.name: routes.ts
nodes.summary: Small shared route helpers that strip trailing slashes and remove the configured base URL prefix, used by both the plugin's post-build route check and the theme's page lookup. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: site-identity.ts
nodes.summary: Parses and validates `docsite/site.json` (site identity schema 1): title, URL, base URL, organization and project names, optional repository and tagline, customDocs collections with distinct routes outside `specs/`, and the optional homepage presentation object; the removed `protocolDocs` option fails with migration guidance. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: build.ts
nodes.summary: Production build entry point (`npm run build`): requires Profile 14, prepares publication in build mode, runs Docusaurus into `.generated/candidate`, validates it with `validateScopedBuild`, and only then promotes it over `docsite/build` through a rename-based transaction that restores the previous site on failure. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite) as part of the Docsite build interface.

nodes.name: prepare-publication.ts
nodes.summary: Shared preparation step for preview and production: checks Profile 14, loads the registry, materializes staged content and clears the mode-specific Docusaurus generated directory (`.docusaurus` or `.generated/docusaurus-production`) so each run reads only the fresh materialization. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite). Observation: its doc comment still speaks of "Architecture" sections, while entries now carry their diagrams under Relationships.

nodes.name: start.ts
nodes.summary: Preview entry point (`npm start`): prepares publication in preview mode and launches `docusaurus start` with forwarded arguments, failing on a non-zero exit. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: validate.ts
nodes.summary: Validation CLI (`npm run validate`): checks Profile 14 for the `--project-root` or default root, loads the scoped registry and rewrites every page's links to surface invalid or unregistered sources, then prints target and document counts. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: sidebars.specs.ts
nodes.summary: Two-line barrel that re-exports the generated specs sidebar JSON so Docusaurus consumes registry-derived Spec navigation rather than a hand-maintained tree. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: ContentProvenance.tsx
nodes.summary: React aside shown on Spec pages that labels a page as Module Spec or Implementation Spec, shows its canonical source, links a Module entry and its implementation companions, and exposes document ID, owner, inclusion reasons and reading/metadata digests in a collapsible panel. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite); realizes page provenance display.

nodes.name: custom.css
nodes.summary: Site-wide Docusaurus theme overrides: the light and dark Infima primary palettes, Concorde surface/border tokens, the inline-SVG masked GitHub navbar mark, the content-provenance strip and a global focus-visible outline with a 640px narrow-layout breakpoint. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: index.module.css
nodes.summary: CSS module for the docsite landing page: dark gradient hero, contract card, feature and workflow step grids, quickstart and reference tables, with token-based light/dark theming and breakpoints at 996px, 700px and 380px plus a reduced-motion rule. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: index.tsx
nodes.summary: Site root page: redirects to the registered entry Module when no homepage is configured, otherwise renders the project-owned introduction (hero, features, workflow, quickstart and optional reference tables) from site identity data. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite). Observation: its fixed "Module contract" panel still presents the retired "Usage & Contract" and "Architecture & Realization" parts, which Protocol 9 no longer admits and the reading validator rejects as headings.

nodes.name: index.tsx
nodes.summary: Swizzled Docusaurus DocItem layout wrapper that finds the current page in the concorde-content global data by base-URL-normalized route and renders ContentProvenance above the original layout. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: favicon.svg
nodes.summary: Spec-declared binding of module.views (entity.views.publication-docsite: Publication docsite). The file exists (1 non-empty lines) but UA's built-in default ignore rules excluded it from the native scan, so its contents were not analyzed.

nodes.name: capture-process.ts
nodes.summary: Test helper that runs a child process synchronously with stdout/stderr redirected to temporary files instead of pipes, which restricted runners may deny, and returns the captured text. Bound by module.views (Publication docsite) as test support.

nodes.name: build-failures.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest contract tests with mocked filesystem and child process showing that preparation, spawn, exit or validation failures never promote the candidate, that validation precedes directory replacement with isolated production generated modules, and that promoteCandidate attempts restoration when backup removal fails. Declares scenario.views.publish-preserves-previous-on-failure and scenario.views.build-site; bound by module.views.
nodes.languageNotes: `vi.hoisted` plus `vi.mock` replace module dependencies before the build script is imported.

nodes.name: build-interface.test.ts
