nodes.summary: Contract tests for the docsite package command surface (validate, start, build, test, typecheck and check scripts; package version 0.7.0) and for the validate CLI's non-zero diagnostics on an unconfigured project or a non-Profile-14 configuration. Bound by module.views; declares no scenario.

nodes.name: document-unit-format.test.ts
nodes.summary: Contract tests for reading-format and contract-schema: Terminology tables, explicit schema-2 roles, placement of formal definitions and Flow catalogs, grouped anchors, reserved Mermaid identifiers, identity/meaning fields, strict JSON and opaque fenced examples, plus offline contract example validation. Declares scenario.views.reject-reading-collection; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: accessibility.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest integration test asserting the site's accessible presentation contract by reading the built sources: the navbar exposes Module Specs and Implementation Specs but no Graph tab, the root page keeps its refresh fallback and Link, ContentProvenance carries its ARIA labels, and custom.css keeps focus-visible plus the narrow-layout breakpoint. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).
nodes.languageNotes: The test asserts over file text rather than a rendered DOM, so it checks authored source contracts without booting Docusaurus.

nodes.name: atomic-promotion.test.ts
nodes.summary: Integration tests for promoteCandidate on real temporary directories: a successful replacement removes stale backups, a missing candidate rolls back, and a failing backup rename preserves both the published output and the candidate. Bound by module.views; declares no scenario.

nodes.name: agent-flows.test.ts
nodes.summary: Repository test that parses `docsite/concorde-only/page.tsx` with the TypeScript compiler API to collect literal, concatenated and base-URL Spec links, and checks that each resolves to a published registry page and section. Declares scenario.views.agent-flows; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: compact-module-navigation.test.ts
nodes.summary: Repository test asserting that consolidated Modules publish a single Module-collection entry as a direct sidebar document while their requirements, scenarios and execution references sit under the Implementation Specs sidebar, that retired topic files are gone, and that every page's links rewrite. Declares scenario.views.publish-reference-link; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: flow-navigation.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest repository test that executes flows.py and then asserts every exported Capability and shared Flow has a unique selectable link, that search matches both an enclosing loop and its composed Capability, and that legacy or malformed hashes select their containing flow or fall back to development. Each test declares scenario.views.agent-flows. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication docsite entity.

nodes.name: framework-guides.test.ts
nodes.summary: Repository test over Concorde's own registry: every registered document is published exactly once without README or control sources, the development Module's Relationships distinguish capability dispatch from worker execution, and every Module entry follows Purpose/Terminology/Usage/Design/Relationships without retired parts. Bound by module.views; declares no scenario.

nodes.name: fresh-project-scaffold.test.ts
nodes.summary: End-to-end test that initializes a temporary Profile 14 project through Concorde's Python API, proposes and applies the docsite scaffold with `scripts/concorde.py docsite`, then validates and builds the received adapter, including a custom docs tab and invalid custom candidates that must preserve the published site. Declares scaffold-propose, scaffold-apply, publish-homepage-default, publish-without-graph, id-anchors, custom-docs and publish-preserves-previous-on-failure scenarios; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: github-pages.test.ts
nodes.summary: Repository test pinning Concorde's GitHub Pages identity in `docsite/site.json`, base-URL route canonicalization, and the deploy-docsite workflow (single checkout, verified build output, graph-inspection dependencies only in Concorde's own workflow rather than the scaffold copy). Bound by module.views; declares no scenario.

nodes.name: module-graph.test.ts
nodes.summary: Repository test confirming that the loaded schema-21 registry keeps parent and uses relationships without a graph `edges` projection and that repeated loads yield identical digests and targets. Declares scenario.views.load-registry; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: production-build.test.ts
nodes.summary: Repository test that runs the real production build over output seeded with obsolete graph files, then checks the promoted manifest, per-Module section anchors, both reading paths, Agent Flows and Protocol tabs, the homepage, legacy redirect stubs, graph absence and a repeat build. Declares publish-candidate, reading-collections, agent-flows, protocol-docs-tab, publish-homepage, publish-legacy-redirect, publish-without-graph and publish-repeat-without-graph scenarios; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: run-checks.py
nodes.summary: Host-only repository regression runner: it copies the listed project directories and files into a disposable temporary project, refuses to run when the registry lists implementation roots the copy would omit, then runs npm ci, the Concorde build, the views unit tests and vitest against that copy so all dependency preparation and generated output stay outside the candidate. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).
nodes.languageNotes: Derives its completeness complaint from the registry's `files` listing roots, so adding a new listed root cannot silently empty the checks.

nodes.name: scoped-registry.test.ts
nodes.summary: Large fixture-driven suite that builds temporary Profile 14 projects to exercise registry loading (ownership, references, bindings, file entries, cycles, digests, routes and aliases), materialization and sidebars, the concorde-content plugin hooks, build validation, custom docs and promotion. Declares most publication pipeline scenarios (materialize, load-registry, reading-collections, validate-candidate-mismatch, custom-docs, build-site and others); bound by module.views.

nodes.name: setup.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest setup file that clears the CONCORDE_PROJECT_ROOT and CONCORDE_BUILD_OUT_DIR environment variables after each test so build-path overrides cannot leak between cases. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).

nodes.name: definition-titles.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for injectAnchors: requirement and scenario headings publish readable titles with stable `{#id}` anchors, duplicate titles stay addressable, and ordinary headings, inline code and fenced examples are left untouched. Declares scenario.views.id-anchors; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: internal-links.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for validateInternalLinks over synthetic HTML trees: cross-collection, alias, query and encoded-fragment navigation resolves, while missing pages or anchors, redirect cycles, traversal, foreign bases and percent-encoding edge cases are rejected. Declares scenario.views.publish-legacy-redirect and scenario.views.validate-candidate-mismatch; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: site-identity.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for site identity schema 1: valid and optional fields, missing-file and invalid-JSON errors, retired protocolDocs rejection, custom docs collection admission and route conflicts, and homepage/reference validation. Declares scenario.views.publish-homepage-invalid and scenario.views.custom-docs; bound by module.views.

nodes.name: vitest.config.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest configuration for the docsite suite: the node environment, global test APIs, the shared tests/setup.ts hook and a 30-second timeout for the slower build-driven cases. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.publication-docsite (Publication docsite).
nodes.languageNotes: Written as CommonJS (`require`/`module.exports`) with a typed cast, unlike the ESM sources around it.

nodes.name: concorde-worker.ts
nodes.summary: The Pi extension every Concorde worker and child session loads: it reads the host-issued policy file named by CONCORDE_WORKER_POLICY, replaces the system prompt with the rendered rules, gates every tool call against the granted tools and canonicalized read/write roots, scrubs environment variables from bash commands, bounds delegation to one level via the pi-subagents capability ceiling and required child extensions, and registers submit_result, report_issue and run_checks over a host socket. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.pi-worker-runtime (Pi worker runtime).
nodes.languageNotes: Its own header states this is an in-process policy gate, not an OS sandbox: shell commands are not confined by it, matching the harness Spec's explicit limitation. Symlinks are resolved through the longest existing path prefix before a grant check, so a missing target cannot escape its root.

nodes.name: concorde.ps1
nodes.summary: Three-line PowerShell shim that resolves `concorde.py` next to itself, runs it with the forwarded arguments and propagates the child exit code. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.installation (Installation), giving Windows developers the same portable CLI entry point as the shell wrapper.

nodes.name: concorde.py
nodes.summary: Portable Python entry point that locates the package root relative to its own file, prepends `src/` to `sys.path` and hands control to `concorde.distribution.cli.main`, exiting with its return code. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.installation (Installation); this is the `python3 scripts/concorde.py build` command the checkout's bootstrap instructions and STUDIO.md rely on.

nodes.name: concorde.sh
nodes.summary: POSIX shell shim that resolves its own directory without relying on `CDPATH` and execs `python3 concorde.py` with the forwarded arguments. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.installation (Installation), the Unix counterpart of the PowerShell wrapper.

nodes.name: check-docsite-types.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic check that runs the docsite's TypeScript compiler against an external temporary copy of `docsite/`, reusing an already-installed `node_modules` through a digest marker over package.json/package-lock.json or falling back to `npm ci`, then generating the real scoped sidebar with tsx before invoking `tsc --noEmit`. Observation: it is bound by module.distribution under entity.distribution.installation (Installation), whose readable meaning is the install preview/apply boundary, while the script itself is a source-checkout type check rather than installation logic.

nodes.name: check-flow-specs.py
nodes.summary: Thin command wrapper that compiles the Flow catalog with inert nodes and prints every finding from `concorde.development.flow_specs.flow_spec_findings`, so each executable Flow's Mermaid `%% flow:` diagram must match the compiled LangGraph topology, every Flow must have a diagram, and no file under `src/` or `scripts/` may import the forbidden Functional API. Bound by module.development as part of entity.development.development-host (Development host); it exits 1 when any finding has error severity.
nodes.languageNotes: Parses the Flow catalog rather than executing it, keeping the check offline and side-effect free.

nodes.name: check-reference-versions.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic check that the vendored external reference submodules are honest: it compares `reference/langgraph`'s declared pyproject version against the installed distribution and the `uv.lock` pin, and `reference/pi-subagents`' package version against the pin in `pi/package.json`, printing remediation commands and exiting 1 on any mismatch. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.context (Context resolution), the entity that freezes a Module's external references as part of its context identity.

nodes.name: check-spec-v5.py
nodes.summary: Offline Spec source audit built on `DocumentUnitRepository`: it validates every registered document unit, checks that each Markdown reading member has its paired `.md.json`, resolves anchors and relative Markdown links to real definitions, tallies requirements, scenarios, entities, contracts and bindings, and with `--base` compares stable identities and source digests against a committed git baseline. Bound by module.spec as part of entity.spec.spec-model (Spec model). Observation: the file name still says `v5` while its docstring describes a Protocol-9 audit, retained as a historical command path for configured checks.

nodes.name: init-references.py
nodes.summary: Checks out the vendored external reference submodules the way the Framework expects: a blobless partial clone with the per-submodule sparse-checkout patterns recorded in `.gitmodules` under `concorde-sparse`, pinned to exactly the commit the superproject records, so hundreds of megabytes of upstream media are never downloaded; `--check` reports without cloning. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.installation (Installation); it is the second bootstrap step in a fresh clone after the build.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads submodule configuration through `git config -f .gitmodules` rather than parsing the file, so an unusual layout cannot silently be misread.

nodes.name: run-tests.py
nodes.summary: Parallel test runner that discovers the same modules as `unittest discover` under `tests/concorde` and runs each in its own interpreter, fanning out the few dominating modules one subprocess per test method and running any SERIAL modules alone afterwards, then parsing each unit's summary into a per-module report with timings and an optional JSON dump. Observation: it is bound by module.distribution under entity.distribution.installation (Installation) although it is a development test scheduler, not installation behavior.
nodes.languageNotes: Enumerates test ids inside the target interpreter with a small embedded script, so fan-out uses unittest's own loader view instead of a source-level guess.

nodes.name: studio.py
nodes.summary: LangGraph dev entry module for this source checkout: it pins the package root to its own parent, globs `skills/*/SKILL.md` and exports one module-level graph per skill by calling `build_studio_flow`, with hyphens replaced by underscores so the names match the `generated/langgraph.json` build output. Bound by module.harness as part of entity.harness.studio (Studio).
nodes.languageNotes: Assigns into `globals()` in a loop so LangGraph's config can reference one attribute per skill without hand-written declarations.

nodes.name: install-concorde.py
nodes.summary: The installer's preview/apply boundary: it loads and validates a standalone package manifest, enumerates the distributable package roots, computes the desired installed outputs (framework bytes, Protocol copy, project defaults, docsite template, managed Python runtime and the pinned Understand Anything viewer), diffs them against the prior ownership receipt at `.concorde/install.json`, prints the plan, and applies it transactionally with a refreshed receipt. Bound by module.distribution as entity.distribution.install-script/entity.distribution.installation, matching the declared rule that a receipt records installed bytes and their before-state and is not permission to overwrite unrelated user content.
nodes.languageNotes: All manifest-supplied paths pass through `_safe_relative`, rejecting absolute or escaping paths before any file is written.

nodes.name: issues.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic CLI for branch-local Issues that never launches a model: `list` and `show` read the Issue store, `archive-reflections` explicitly preserves legacy Reflection history, and every result or error is printed as JSON with exit code 2 on failure. Bound by module.issues as part of entity.issues.runtime (Issue runtime), whose declared responsibility includes host-only file transactions and immutable individual reports.

nodes.name: requirements.lock
nodes.summary: Spec-declared binding of module.distribution (entity.distribution.installation: Installation). The file exists (1 non-empty lines) but UA's built-in default ignore rules excluded it from the native scan, so its contents were not analyzed.

nodes.name: run-capability.py
nodes.summary: Executable boundary for Concorde's public Skills: it accepts exactly one of the nine public skill names, reads that skill's `capability:` front-matter field from `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` to resolve the capability module, and runs the shared trusted stdin/envelope handling through that module's `run`; `--runtime-check` is an offline smoke check confirming the capability's JSON data boundary and an importable LangGraph Graph API. Bound by module.distribution as part of entity.distribution.installation (Installation) and named as the installed runtime launcher.
nodes.languageNotes: Stage capabilities deliberately have no launcher, so only Skills are directly invocable.

nodes.name: run-ua-graph-viewer.py
nodes.summary: Offline launcher for the installer-owned Understand Anything viewer: it validates the installed framework manifest and viewer entry point, admits an existing raw knowledge-graph JSON from the declared graph paths, resolves a safe Node interpreter and port, and starts the viewer process without regenerating the graph. Bound by module.views as part of entity.views.viewer-launcher (Viewer launcher), which declares exactly that launch admits an existing graph plus the verified installed viewer from the Distribution Module and never checks graph freshness against source.
nodes.languageNotes: Every externally supplied path passes a symlink and traversal check before use, so an untrusted manifest cannot redirect the launch.

nodes.name: worktree-guard.py
nodes.summary: Hook script registered in `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json` that reads one tool-call payload from stdin and refuses native worktree creation inside agent sessions of this checkout: Claude Code `WorktreeCreate`, `EnterWorktree`, subagents with `isolation: "worktree"`, and shell commands matching `git ... worktree add/move` or a `claude --worktree`/`-w` launch; a refusal prints a deny decision and exits 2, unreadable input exits 1, everything else is silently allowed. Observation: it is bound by module.distribution under entity.distribution.installation (Installation) although its own docstring states the installer does not ship this script and consumer projects never receive the hook.
nodes.languageNotes: Inspects the whole command text including quoted strings and here-documents, which is why files mentioning these commands must be written with an editor tool.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Root package of the Concorde runtime ("Deterministic Concorde architecture services"). Its only behavior is to derive `__version__` from the `version` field of the packaged `concorde.json` build manifest two directories above the package, degrading to the literal "source" whenever the manifest is missing, undecodable, invalid JSON or lacks a usable string. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Package entry point for `python -m concorde`: imports the Distribution CLI `main` and exits with its status code. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity. Observation: the code contains no Spec-model logic; it only delegates to the Distribution-bound tool CLI.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the Development runtime, whose single docstring states its responsibility: host and run every Concorde development capability on a coding agent. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity, which dispatches admitted requests to the executable capabilities.

nodes.name: capability_flow.py
nodes.summary: Builds the capability admission/dispatch/result LangGraph `StateGraph` that both local calls and Studio execute: initialize, admit_request, bind_workspace, check_configuration, a nested dispatch subflow at `execute`, then finalize, with every conditional edge short-circuiting to finalize as soon as `result` is set. It compiles stateless (`checkpointer=False`) with a deliberately large CAPABILITY_RECURSION_LIMIT, and re-attaches that same child instance so Studio/xray topology discovery stays accurate. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity, which separates admission from domain work so a model's proposed result cannot choose its own permissions.
nodes.languageNotes: The successor is captured as a default argument in each routing lambda (`next_node=successor`), which is what keeps the loop-built conditional edges from all closing over the last value.

nodes.name: capability_host.py
nodes.summary: Trusted host that admits and executes every public Concorde capability as LangGraph Flows: it supplies the node bindings for capability admission, dispatch, target admission, project, topology preparation and application, component coordination and the development loop, freezes each stage's context, compiles its least-privilege policy, launches Pi workers, records evidence and usage, and returns the typed capability result envelope. Bound by module.development as its Development host entity, realizing the Flow Specs in that Module's execution reference. The Development Module entry itself records that the invocation-binding mechanics of Invocation.stage and MainInvocation.stage still live here although they belong to Harness's own host contract.
nodes.languageNotes: Flow nodes are built as closures over an Invocation or nonlocal stage variables, so the compiled graph stays inspectable while host authority and callbacks never enter LangGraph state.

nodes.name: capability_service.py
nodes.summary: Public host API facade for Profile 14 scoped capabilities: re-exports CapabilityHost and run_capability from capability_host so callers and capability modules import one stable boundary. Bound by module.development (Development host).

nodes.name: configuration.py
nodes.summary: Loads, admits, proposes and atomically applies the project's typed capability configuration under .concorde/config.json, validating the Pi model selection of every worker and child and binding each proposal to the source file's sha256 digest so a changed file is rejected instead of overwritten. Bound by module.development (Development host).

nodes.name: coordination_flow.py
nodes.summary: Compiles the two LangGraph flows that let coordinated component writers finish before shared-consumer verification: `coordination_flow` runs reconcile_specs, validate_specs, implement_components, implement_local, finalize_components, record_completion with every intermediate stage able to end once it produces `output`; `stabilization_flow` runs snapshot, verify_components, check_stability and loops back to snapshot when the routing decision says so. Both compile stateless. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity.

nodes.name: discovery_flow.py
nodes.summary: Compiles the bounded Module discovery Flow (discovery_flow): decide runs one discovery worker, expand_context admits further Module contexts and loops back, and bind_routes or finish end the run. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity; the matching Flow Spec 'Discovery Flow' is owned by module.query-routing's execution reference, and the factory itself performs no project access and starts no worker.

nodes.name: dispatch_flow.py
nodes.summary: Compiles the capability dispatch Flow (dispatch_flow): select_capability routes an admitted request to an entry leaf or to target admission, which routes to the bound leaf, while query, topology, plan, project, issues, development-loop, specification and target-admission subflows are embedded and exposed for Studio. Bound by module.development, whose execution reference owns the 'Capability dispatch Flow' Flow Spec; a per-capability build compiles only the entry and bound leaves that capability can reach.

nodes.name: flow_catalog.py
nodes.summary: The single registry of Concorde's executable Flows: it maps each compiled graph name to the same factory execution uses and builds it with inert stub nodes, so inspection, publication and the deterministic Flow Spec check all read exactly the topology execution compiles. Its seventeen factories are imported lazily inside `catalog()` from the development, harness and issues packages, and building an entry never resolves a context or starts a worker. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity. Observation: `catalog()` imports `worker_profile` from the harness package but never uses it.

nodes.name: flow_specs.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic Flow Spec checker: extracts Mermaid diagrams bound with `%% flow: <name>` from registered Spec documents, compares their nodes, edges, routing labels and in/out state labels with the compiled LangGraph Flow catalog, and refuses any non-StateGraph Flow or any `langgraph.func` (Functional API) import found by AST parsing. Bound by module.development under the Development host entity; findings are structural evidence only, never semantic proof.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `ast` parsing with a `TypeGuard` predicate so source files are inspected without being imported or executed.

nodes.name: loop_flow.py
nodes.summary: Defines the executable development topology (development_flow): a typed state whose artifact channel merges through a reducer, the stage successor map and per-stage handover destinations, the compiled Flow factory and the Command helper each stage returns. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity; the matching Flow Spec 'Development Flow' is owned by module.dev-loop's execution reference. The factory itself performs no project access and runs no worker.
nodes.languageNotes: Stage handover is expressed with LangGraph Command returns and declared node destinations rather than conditional edges, so the compiled graph still states every permitted transition.

nodes.name: loop_graph.py
nodes.summary: Compatibility shim that re-exports build_loop_flow under the older build_loop_graph name together with loop_successors, for callers written before the Flow terminology. Bound by module.development (Development host); it adds no behavior of its own.

nodes.name: plan_flow.py
nodes.summary: Compiles the `plan_flow` graph in which context assessment precedes planning and only a successful plan is persisted: assess_context and author_plan each route on `state["route"]` to the next stage or straight to END, and persist_plan ends the flow. After compiling, it exposes the context_assessor and planner CapabilityNode subflows on the two model-backed nodes so inspection shows the worker inside. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity. Observation: `worker_profile` is imported here but never used.

nodes.name: project_flow.py
nodes.summary: Compiles the `project_flow` graph in which project initialization and configuration select explicit deterministic operations: select_action routes to configure, propose, apply or END, and each of those three actions ends the flow directly. Compiled stateless. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity.

nodes.name: query_flow.py
nodes.summary: Compiles query_flow, the Flow concorde-main runs for ask and design-topology: the discovery Flow executes as a subflow and respond turns its last decision into the main response unless discovery already produced a terminal result. Bound by module.development; its Flow Spec 'Query Flow' is owned by module.query-routing, and the compiled subflow is exposed so Studio can inspect it.

nodes.name: review.py
nodes.summary: Independent, target-bound Spec and code review: it builds a digest-bound review input from scoped Git history, runs exactly one reviewer worker with no write authority, persists the review artifact and its change-state evidence, expands the scope to Spec consumers and changed-file peers in separate contexts, and decides when existing revision-bound evidence may be reused or must be refreshed before readiness. Bound by module.development (Development host).

nodes.name: specify_flow.py
nodes.summary: The standalone Spec authoring and review Flow (specify_flow), also composed as the development loop's specify_loop stage: it compiles initialize, specify, review_spec and summarize, decides whether authoring was already accepted for this intent, and supplies host node bindings that invoke the concorde-specify and concorde-review child capabilities, reuse current Spec review scope or an explicit skip, and record stopping transitions on the change. Bound by module.development; the 'Specification Flow' Flow Spec is owned by module.specify-loop's execution reference.

nodes.name: target_flow.py
nodes.summary: Compiles target_flow for target admission: initialize_target either binds a recorded or routed owner directly or, for discovering capabilities, enters an embedded discovery subflow before bind_target selects the bound leaf. Bound by module.development, whose execution reference owns the 'Target admission Flow' Flow Spec; discovery composition is optional through the discover argument.

nodes.name: topology_flow.py
nodes.summary: Compiles the two Module-topology flows shared by execution and inspection: `topology_flow` authors a candidate (prepare_authors and author_module both routing back to author_module, forward to validate_candidate, or to END, then validate_candidate, review_contexts and persist_application), and `topology_apply_flow` admits, validates, applies atomically and cleans up, ending early at each step whenever a `result` is already present. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the Distribution runtime, whose single docstring states its responsibility: package, validate, install and update Concorde. Bound by module.distribution as part of the Installation entity, which owns the preview/apply boundary and the ownership receipt of installed bytes.

nodes.name: build.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic build of every distributed projection: worker instructions, the public Skills for the Claude and Codex integrations, the Studio graph list, Protocol principles and kind assets and the exported JSON schemas, together with a source/output build manifest and the freshness checks the host and worker resolution fail closed on. Bound by module.distribution as its Build entity, realizing the Build command and Build manifest it declares.
nodes.languageNotes: Exported schemas are evaluated through a private MetaPathFinder that loads the root's own schema sources under a unique namespace and bypasses bytecode caches, so build identity covers those bytes.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Stable argparse command-line interface for installed Concorde Tools: dispatches `validate`, `docsite`, `ua-graph`, `ua-analyze`, `build`, `protocol-manifest` and `usage`, requires an isolated worktree for mutating tools, and always prints the canonical JSON result envelope with a status-derived exit code. Bound by module.distribution as part of the Installation entity. Observation: most subcommands realize Views, Spec and Harness tools, so this single Installation-bound file fronts responsibilities that the Spec assigns to other Modules.
nodes.languageNotes: Subcommand handlers import their providers lazily inside `dispatch`, keeping CLI start-up independent of optional dependencies.

nodes.name: managed_runtime.py
nodes.summary: Installer-owned lifecycle of the managed Python virtual environment and its paired Node viewer and Pi worker extensions. `load_runtime_spec` validates the build manifest into a `ManagedRuntimeSpec` (safe relative paths, a requirements file that is exactly one pinned `langgraph==X.Y.Z` line, a locked viewer package with its integrity string, a pinned `pi-subagents` semver) and derives the digests that identify the runtime; `plan_runtime` decides create, unchanged, rebuild or conflict from the ownership marker, the installation receipt and a live health probe without mutating anything; `provision_runtime` builds the venv, installs everything offline, verifies each Skill's `--runtime-check` and finally writes the `.concorde-runtime.json` marker. Bound by module.distribution as the Managed runtime entity, which the Spec says records a verified runtime only after its checks succeed.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses act as validated value objects and module-level compiled regexes pin the manifest's accepted shapes; every subprocess runs under an explicitly offline environment so provisioning never reaches the network implicitly.

nodes.name: package_validation.py
nodes.summary: Single package validator producing stable CONCORDE-* findings over prompt sources and their reachability, the capabilities/ inventory with its PUBLIC/CONTEXT_SELECTION/DETERMINISTIC/USES/STATE declarations and Skill pairing, worker profiles and role Specs, exported contract schemas, Spec alignment (the concorde.capabilities metadata inventory, versioned type tokens and the error-code table of the Development interfaces document) and build freshness. Bound by module.distribution (Build).

nodes.name: project_defaults.py
nodes.summary: Defines what installing Concorde places in a project besides the Framework tree: the verified Protocol bundle copied from `generated/protocol/` to `.concorde/protocol/` and Concorde-owned ignore-file defaults seeded only when absent. Bound by module.distribution as part of the Installation entity, matching the Spec rule that installation (not initialization) deploys the Protocol copy.

nodes.name: prompt_resolver.py
nodes.summary: Pure, deterministic resolution of prompt sources: it parses audience front matter, expands whole-line @include directives with per-inclusion variable bindings, enforces scope, audience and Protocol isolation plus cycle and diamond rules, and reports prompt files no root reaches. Bound by module.distribution (Build). Observation: the resolve_model_instructions docstring still cites workflow/agents-and-harnesses.md, a path that no longer exists in this repository.

nodes.name: protocol_guidance.py
nodes.summary: Manages the Concorde-owned Protocol block inside a target project's root agent instruction file — `AGENTS.md` for Codex, `CLAUDE.md` for Claude. The block only references `.concorde/protocol/principles.md` so Protocol prose stays in the packaged asset; `split` refuses forged, duplicated or misordered `<!-- concorde-protocol: -->` markers rather than consuming arbitrary user text, and `plan` verifies any existing block against the receipt digest before touching it, prepends a new block so it cannot be hidden inside user Markdown, and returns a change record with before/after digests plus merged bytes without normalizing user newlines. Bound by module.distribution as part of the Installation entity, whose receipt records installed bytes and their before-state and is not permission to overwrite unrelated user content.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the Harness runtime, whose single docstring states its responsibility: configure every bounded agent invocation — context, permissions, execution and worktrees. Bound by module.harness as part of the Capability and Harness model entity, which defines a worker's task contract, effects, workspace, tools and children.

nodes.name: batch_flow.py
nodes.summary: Provides the shared LangGraph primitive for sequential bounded composition of independently admitted work items: `build_batch_flow` compiles a named two-node loop (select_item and a caller-chosen item node) that ends as soon as `stop` is set, and `run_batch_flow` drives a materialized item sequence through that same graph, stopping at the first non-None item result and capping recursion at `2 * len(items) + 3`. Bound by module.harness as part of the Capability and Harness model entity; the development flow catalog and scoped review both instantiate it.

nodes.name: capability_node.py
nodes.summary: One State-based node interface for code, model and composed Capabilities: CapabilityNode resolves a registered capability from capabilities/, derives TypedDict input and output schemas from its declared types and compiles run(state, runtime) as a single-node LangGraph subgraph whose trusted context travels in Runtime, never in State. Bound by module.harness (Capability and Harness model); its 'Capability node' Flow Spec is in that Module's execution reference.

nodes.name: capability_state.py
nodes.summary: Dependency-free State contracts and trusted runtime context every Capability shares: the host result channel, a StateContract whose schemas resolve lazily, the CapabilityContext carrying host, configuration or launcher, and the run_model and run_host adapters for model-backed and host-backed capabilities. Bound by module.harness (Capability and Harness model).

nodes.name: change_worktree.py
nodes.summary: Host-owned change-worktree lifecycle: lists Git worktrees, serializes registry updates with a repository lock, reads and validates `.concorde/worktree.json` state, creates linked candidate worktrees with guidance blocks, tracks owner binding, target progress, repair-graph records and Issue blockers, and snapshots the exact deliverable tree without touching the caller's index. Bound by both module.harness and module.development as the Worktree lifecycle entity. Observation: it lazily imports Issue store/references and Distribution build code, while module.harness declares uses only of Spec and Distribution.
nodes.languageNotes: `read_change` uses `typing.overload` with `Literal[True]` so callers that require a change get a non-optional `dict` type.

nodes.name: check_executor.py
nodes.summary: OS-enforced read-only execution of configured checks: a trusted root-owned bubblewrap runs each check in user, PID and IPC namespaces over a read-only host bind with one fresh writable scratch, gated until its namespace PID 1 is pinned by a pidfd so timeout and cleanup kill every descendant, with no unsandboxed fallback. Bound by module.harness (Capability and Harness model), realizing the Linux-only deterministic check boundary the Harness entry describes.
nodes.languageNotes: Missing CPython pidfd wrappers are resolved through ctypes against libc so cleanup never falls back to signalling a reusable numeric PID.

nodes.name: context.py
nodes.summary: Freezes the immutable cognitive inputs of an invocation: a per-Module context snapshot (Spec resolution, implementation entries, file names and, in code phases, artifact bytes, external references, Protocol files, stage inputs and workspace), the multi-Module discovery context and the topology-author context, each identified by a digest, plus grant computation, byte-verified materialization into a capsule and rechecks that turn any changed selection into stale context. Bound by module.harness as its Context resolution entity.
nodes.languageNotes: A decorator wraps every recheck so a formerly admitted selection that no longer resolves is reported as stale evidence rather than as a new resolution error.

nodes.name: effects.py
nodes.summary: Shared effect vocabulary for worker contracts and permission compilation: the closed PATH_ROLES set and the frozen EffectDeclaration of read and write path roles plus network and credential posture. Bound by module.harness (Capability and Harness model). Observation: the module docstring still names roles.py as a consumer, but no such file exists in the package.

nodes.name: harness.py
nodes.summary: Declares SAFE_ENVIRONMENT, the host environment-variable allowlist every Pi worker process inherits, and frames a Harness as context, control flow, models and per-worker permissions. Bound by module.harness (Capability and Harness model), matching the entry's statement that this model supplies the host environment allowlist to the Pi worker runtime. Observation: the docstring cites workflow/agents-and-harnesses.md, a path that no longer exists; the topic now lives under specs/concorde/harness/.

nodes.name: model_selection.py
nodes.summary: Resolves the Pi model, thinking level and timeout of each worker and child from the project capability configuration, letting the most specific entry win value by value, and rejects override keys that name no worker or child, child timeouts, non-positive timeouts and model names that are not provider/id. Bound by module.harness (Capability and Harness model).

nodes.name: permissions.py
nodes.summary: Least-privilege policy compilation: it intersects a worker contract's declared effects with a host-issued narrowing binding and the concrete role paths of the invocation into one digest-bound NormalizedPolicy with default deny and credential deny paths, refusing any widening, and verifies that an effective policy stays within the declared one. Bound by module.harness as its Permissions entity.

nodes.name: pi_rpc.py
nodes.summary: Strict JSONL client for one Pi process in RPC mode: it sends a single prompt, collects events and tool results until the agent settles, answers every interactive dialog as cancelled, reads session statistics and maps deadlines, host interruption and protocol faults onto distinct timeout, cancelled and error classes, always killing the process. Bound by module.harness as part of the Pi worker runtime.

nodes.name: pi_worker.py
nodes.summary: Launches one Concorde worker as an isolated Pi process: it validates the launch against its tools, children and write grants, builds a private run directory with copied credentials, settings, child agent definitions, the one-level pi-subagents configuration, the policy the worker extension enforces and the system prompt, serves the host run_checks and report_issue tools over a Unix socket, and admits exactly one submitted result. Bound by module.harness as its Pi worker runtime entity; consistent with the entry's stated limitation, shell commands are only protected by credential scrubbing and the in-process tool gate, not by an OS sandbox.

nodes.name: session_handoff.py
nodes.summary: Renders the Protocol P10 session-handoff prompt draft from facts the runtime already knows, substituting an explicit "Unknown to the runtime" placeholder for everything it was not given. It refuses a non-absolute initial directory and deliberately never resolves, stats or reads the destination worktree; the rendered text instructs the new session to start fresh, read that worktree's own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, use only that worktree's Skills, and treat the handoff as granting no additional read, write, merge or delivery authority. Listed by both module.harness and module.development as the Worktree lifecycle entity.
nodes.languageNotes: The output fence length is computed from the longest backtick run inside the body, so an embedded fenced block can never terminate the draft's own fence early.

nodes.name: studio.py
nodes.summary: Optional LangGraph Studio adapter: build_studio_flow compiles one graph per public capability that validates the invocation envelope and the server's workspace identity, then runs the same capability admission Flow as an inspectable subflow with an observed worker executor, streaming host events and returning the result, the described policies and the event log. Bound by module.harness as its Studio entity, which the entry describes as starting or observing the same capability host as worker execution.

nodes.name: studio_client.py
nodes.summary: Opt-in, standard-library HTTP transport that submits a capability invocation to a local LangGraph Studio server, polls the run and validates the returned capability result shape; it refuses non-localhost URLs, proxies and redirects and never retries run creation. Bound by module.harness as the Studio entity, consistent with Studio observing the same capability host.

nodes.name: usage.py
nodes.summary: Per-invocation token accounting: it writes one labelled usage line per worker launch under .concorde/runs/<root invocation>/usage.jsonl, swallowing persistence errors so observability never fails a completed launch, and reads those lines back into totals broken down by step, stage, target, agent and run. Bound by module.harness (Capability and Harness model); the records are diagnostics, never evidence.

nodes.name: worker_executor.py
nodes.summary: Binds and runs one worker invocation: build_worker_invocation freezes capability, stage, workspace, canonical context and receipt, policy, WorkerProfile binding, instructions and model selections into a digest-identified record, and WorkerExecutor re-verifies the binding against the current build, the granted Protocol bytes, the rendered instructions and the contract's context and policy before launching the Pi runtime and admitting the single typed result with its usage. Bound by module.harness as its Worker execution entity.

nodes.name: worker_profile.py
nodes.summary: Optional model execution configuration for Capabilities with no separate agent registry: the profile, contract, child and binding records, their consistency rules, loading of profiles from capabilities.CAPABILITIES, admission of a worker's context, result and compiled policy, and resolve_worker, which binds one profile byte for byte to the current build manifest. Bound by module.harness (Capability and Harness model); the entry names worker_profile and resolve_worker as the realization of Capability profile and Harness binding.

nodes.name: worktree.py
nodes.summary: Fail-closed Git worktree boundary for agent-authored mutations. `inspect_worktree` derives a frozen `WorktreeBoundary` from `git rev-parse` alone — toplevel, absolute git dir, common dir and verified HEAD commit — marking the checkout isolated when the git dir differs from the common dir, without reading working-tree file contents; `require_isolated_worktree` then refuses symlinked roots, non-directories and directories that are not Git worktrees, and refuses the primary worktree with a message naming the HEAD to branch from, unless `allow_primary_worktree` records the developer's explicit authorization. Listed by both module.harness and module.development as the Worktree lifecycle entity, which checks the mutation boundary.

nodes.name: worktree_delivery.py
nodes.summary: Delivers a verified candidate change from either participating worktree session: admits only the source or primary session, re-checks the validated tree, confirms pending file markers, builds a merge commit onto `concorde/delivered/<change_id>`, re-validates the merged tree in a detached worktree, writes a durable receipt before ref updates, cleans up, and performs an explicit primary fast-forward merge only on request. Bound by module.harness and module.development as the Worktree lifecycle entity. Observation: it imports `Invocation` and `_check` from the Development capability host at runtime, a dependency not declared in module.harness's uses.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Git plumbing (`commit-tree`, `merge-tree --write-tree`, `update-ref` with old values) to build and publish merges without touching the working index.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the Issues runtime, whose single docstring states its responsibility: branch-local, evidence-bound project issues and host-mediated reporting. Bound by module.issues as part of the Issue store entity, which owns durable observations and disposition history under `.concorde/issues/`.

nodes.name: archive.py
nodes.summary: Explicitly and losslessly retires the legacy `.concorde/reflections` queue by renaming it to `.concorde/archive/reflections` under the Issue lock; it is never an Issue migration or disposition. Bound by module.issues as the Issue store entity (entity id `entity.reflections.issue-store`).

nodes.name: flow.py
nodes.summary: LangGraph Graph-API `issue_flow` for listing, showing, reporting, reopening and bounded solving of Issues: compiles the declared nodes and conditional routes, validates pending disposition journals, binds the selected Issue before workspace creation, and implements solve nodes that call ordinary development, Spec repair, Issue-specific review and final validation with a six-decision limit and write-ahead restoration. Bound by module.issues as the Issue store entity; the Spec describes this as the Issue runtime plus LangGraph `issue_flow`.
nodes.languageNotes: `issue_nodes` returns closures that share `nonlocal` solve state, and a nested `issue_verification_flow` StateGraph loops over review items instead of a hand-written loop.

nodes.name: references.py
nodes.summary: Issue reference helpers: projects receipts from report references, derives review blockers, builds the admitted `concorde-issue-context` of contract-level observation text, validates that worker results cite only admitted or reported observations, and detects gap reports requiring contract repair. Bound by module.issues as the Issue store entity.

nodes.name: reporting.py
nodes.summary: Report-only host service bound to one admitted worker invocation: `IssueReporter` validates provenance, owner scope and evidence paths before persisting a report and returning an immutable receipt, and `reporter_for_invocation` derives its scope from the frozen context snapshot rather than worker-supplied claims. Bound by module.issues as the Issue store entity.

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: Git-versioned Issue record store under `.concorde/issues/`: one Markdown file per Issue holding one closed JSON record, with schema and history validation, idempotent report allocation per invocation and report key, file-locked digest-bound publication, disposition and restoration, and resolution of immutable observations by receipt. Bound by module.issues as the Issue store entity.
nodes.languageNotes: Issue identities are deterministic `uuid5` values over the invocation ID and report key, making retried reports idempotent.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the Spec runtime, whose single docstring names the accepted Framework profile: "Profile 14: complete Module content with a defined reading subset whose entities list implementation files." Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity, which the SpecRepository API and Validator share so a query and a check never invent different meanings of ownership.

nodes.name: changes.py
nodes.summary: Digest-bound, rollback-safe file transaction primitive: `apply_files` checks before-digests and host-authorized paths, writes each file atomically with fsync, runs an optional verifier and restores prior bytes on any failure; also exposes pending-file confirmation. Bound by module.spec, module.development and module.views as their File transactions entity.

nodes.name: content_changes.py
nodes.summary: Owner-scoped authoring proposals and pending-marker confirmation over the document-unit backend: validates complete digest-bound replacements of a Module's own reading/metadata members in an overlay repository, applies them atomically with context-identity rechecks, and removes pending entries whose files now exist without editing reading prose. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity.

nodes.name: content_migration.py
nodes.summary: Offline, read-only planner for migrating legacy Protocol 6 inline Spec documents to Protocol 9 document units: checks legacy reading parts, moves retired metadata fences into schema-2 metadata, splits formal definitions into implementation-role companions, and previews a registered legacy schema-4 registry without writing. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity; reports always mark the semantic rewrite as not completed.

nodes.name: content_model.py
nodes.summary: Protocol 9 document-unit primitives: `DocumentUnit` and `SourceMember` records, metadata companion naming, reading-anchor meaning resolution, Terminology and reading-structure checks, JSON fence extraction, metadata identity reading, and full admission of one reading/metadata pair including entity, dependency and participant-binding declarations. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity; it admits one unit, leaving registry-wide checks to callers.

nodes.name: content_repository.py
nodes.summary: Protocol 9 document-unit repository backend: `DocumentUnitRepository` loads registry schema 5, supports byte overlays, indexes document identities without reading unselected bodies, admits units, resolves one-level Spec context with source records and inclusion reasons, parses definitions and canonical contracts, and exposes implementation listings and validation. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity (realizing the SpecRepository API).

nodes.name: contract_shapes.py
nodes.summary: Shared JSON Schema building blocks for capability request and response contracts (task fields, check results, routes, workspace context, worktree summaries) plus `task_request` and `capability_response` factories, importing only dependency-free wire and Issue shapes. Bound by module.harness and module.spec as the Typed values entity.

nodes.name: contracts.py
nodes.summary: The capability registry and versioned JSON contracts: it imports the capabilities/ inventory, derives the public, internal, discovery, deterministic, composite and model capability sets, maps each bound stage and review mode to its worker, and defines the schemas of the internal data types (context snapshots, discovery and topology-author contexts, review inputs and results, stage results, topology design, proposal and application) together with every capability's request and response. Bound by both module.spec and module.harness as the shared Typed values entity.

nodes.name: diagnostics.py
nodes.summary: Canonical diagnostics and result serialization for Concorde Tools: deterministic finding ordering, the schema-2 result envelope, canonical JSON output, status-to-exit-code mapping and a newline-normalized source digest. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity.

nodes.name: frontmatter.py
nodes.summary: Constrained YAML front-matter parser shared by Concorde's Markdown readers: it accepts a small safe subset of mappings, lists, JSON-style inline collections, quoted scalars, integers, booleans and null and rejects tags, anchors, aliases, merge keys, block scalars, tab indentation and duplicate keys. Bound by module.spec and module.harness as the shared Typed values entity.

nodes.name: initialize.py
nodes.summary: Initializes a Profile 14 project with an honest Module stub: reads the installed Protocol binding, builds a proposal containing configuration, registry and a paired `module.md`/metadata draft that states unknowns instead of inventing behavior, and applies it creation-only with post-write validation and rollback. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity (realizing the Initialization capability). Observation: module.spec declares no uses, yet this file imports Distribution build and project-defaults code at runtime.

nodes.name: issue_shapes.py
nodes.summary: Closed JSON wire shapes for Issue reports, provenance, receipts, task-local blockers, review Issues, observations, dispositions and records, depending only on the wire primitives so worker tool schemas and the store share one contract. Bound by module.spec (Spec model) and module.issues (Issue store).

nodes.name: model.py
nodes.summary: Immutable result dataclasses shared by Concorde Tools: `Finding`, `ToolResult` and the compatibility `ProposalFile` record. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity; the Spec explicitly notes that `model.py` retains `ProposalFile`.

nodes.name: repository.py
nodes.summary: Public Protocol 9 / Profile 14 repository entry: re-exports the shared repository-base surface and defines `SpecRepository`, which checks `.concorde/config.json` fields and profile version, loads the configured registry through the document-unit backend and admits the installed Protocol copy. Bound by module.spec as the Spec model entity realizing the SpecRepository API.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `from .repository_base import *` to keep an established import surface for shared value types and helpers.

nodes.name: repository_base.py
nodes.summary: Shared Spec model foundations: stable-identity and Markdown grammar patterns, safe file reading, listing-entry coverage and expansion rules, fence-aware line walking, value records (SpecTarget, SpecDocument, SpecResolution, Requirement, Scenario, SpecEntity, ModuleDefinitions), the large `RepositoryCore` query mixin (Protocol admission, registry loading, context selection, contracts, definitions, verifications, external references, implementation listings, affected Modules) and requirement/scenario section parsing. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity. Observation: module.spec declares no uses, yet `RepositoryCore._protocol` imports Distribution build and project-defaults code.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Offline, advertised subset of JSON Schema used by published Concorde contracts: `admit` rejects unsupported keywords, types and non-local references, and `validate` checks values including anyOf/oneOf/allOf, enums, bounds, uniqueness, patterns and the `project-path` format. Bound by module.harness and module.spec as the Typed values entity.

nodes.name: typed_data.py
nodes.summary: Versioned typed JSON values admitted at capability and leaf boundaries: strict duplicate-free JSON decoding, canonical serialization, a standard-library schema checker, safe project-relative path checks that reject symlinks, `typed`/`validate_typed` envelopes with request-action rules, artifact digests and Draft 2020-12 schema export; the capability contract table is populated from `contracts.py` at import time. Bound by module.harness and module.spec as the Typed values entity.

nodes.name: validation.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic Spec validator: parses Mermaid flowcharts, checks reading structure, requirement/scenario/entity definitions, relationship diagrams, unlisted files, document context, dependency agreements, Terminology links, local ID links and test verification coverage, and `validate_repository` assembles all findings with contract-binding checks, Issue inputs and optional package validation into a ToolResult that states semantic completeness is not proven. Bound by module.spec as the Spec model entity realizing the Validator. Observation: it imports Issue store and Distribution package validation at runtime although module.spec declares no uses.

nodes.name: verification.py
nodes.summary: Test-declared scenario verification: the `verifies` decorator for Python tests and a scanner that reads Python decorators by AST and TypeScript `// verifies:` comments line by line, without importing or executing tests, to produce `Verification` records. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity, matching the Framework profile's test-declaration convention.

nodes.name: wire_shapes.py
nodes.summary: Dependency-free JSON Schema shape helpers (`obj`, `array`, string/path/digest/artifact primitives) and the type-version table plus `typed_schema` envelope used by every capability schema declaration. Bound by module.harness and module.spec as the Typed values entity.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the Views runtime, whose single docstring states its responsibility: scaffold and publish one validated project docsite. Bound by module.views as part of the Publication scaffold entity, which creates only the exact accepted site files and never rewrites project Specs.

nodes.name: docsite_scaffold.py
nodes.summary: Preview-first docsite scaffold tool: `propose_docsite` resolves site identity from arguments or the Git origin, inventories the packaged adapter template and optional GitHub Pages workflow, reports conflicts and missing prerequisites, and `apply_docsite` re-verifies the accepted proposal digest and creates only missing exact files through a file transaction. Bound by module.views as the Publication scaffold entity, consistent with the Spec rule that scaffolding never overwrites existing files.

nodes.name: docsite_template.py
nodes.summary: Single inventory rule for the packaged `docsite/` adapter template shared by the installer and the scaffold tool: safe directory walk with exclusions, package-root verification, template and adapter file sets, workflow template bytes and a deterministic template digest. Bound by module.views as the Publication scaffold entity.

nodes.name: ua_analysis.py
nodes.summary: Developer-authorized native Understand Anything host bridge (`ua-analyze`): preflights the UA plugin, Node and Claude CLI versions, prepares a Spec-derived seed graph and per-Module context indexes, writes run-local native settings, runs a bounded parent/child permission probe, launches the native analysis host under a lock, and checks completion, schema, seed identities and input freshness. Bound by module.views as the UA analysis bridge entity, consistent with the Spec's explicit-consent and probe-first design.

nodes.name: ua_graph.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic Understand Anything graph exporter derived only from the Spec registry: builds Module, document and file nodes, containment/dependency edges and layers, strips only elements from a prior Concorde export (tagged `concorde-ua-graph`) when overlaying an existing graph, supports a no-write `--check`, and writes atomically. Bound by module.views as the UA graph exporter entity.

nodes.name: ua_native_host.py
nodes.summary: Opt-in native host permission overlay and prompts for UA analysis: builds run-local allow/deny settings (plugin read, UA directory edits, node/python execution, no git mutations), the analysis-only host profile prompt, native workspace preparation that archives prior scratch, and the bounded permission-probe prompt. Bound by module.views as the UA analysis bridge entity; it is an interpreter/tool grant, not an OS sandbox.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Root of the repository test package. Importing it inserts `<repo>/src` onto `sys.path` exactly once, so any test module runs standalone (for example `python -m unittest tests.concorde.harness.test_boundaries`) instead of depending on unittest discovery order to import whichever module happened to perform that insertion first. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity. Observation: this shared bootstrap for every Module's tests is listed only by module.spec.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Docstring-only package marker for the Concorde feature tests, under which the per-Module test packages live. Bound by module.spec as part of the Spec model entity.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker that makes tests/concorde/development importable as a test package. Bound by module.development under its Development host entity.

nodes.name: test_capability_modules.py
nodes.summary: Contract tests for Concorde's capability inventory and in-process composition: one checked inventory covers model code and composed nodes, property and transport contracts stay independent, `uses` is the only dependency relation and is acyclic, a model subgraph projects parent state while preserving unrelated channels, a module's run is directly a LangGraph node, the host state node preserves the failure envelope and runtime context, and the wire adapter rejects a wrong identity before state projection. It declares `scenario.development.capability-state` and `scenario.development.capability-result-state` through the `verifies` decorator. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity.

nodes.name: test_check_execution.py
nodes.summary: Integration tests for configured check execution reached through the host's check path: a check cannot forge logs while the host persists private output and digests, real project writes fail validation and never record readiness, an unavailable sandbox or a timeout is reported without leaking private diagnostics, and external changes still invalidate the post-check digest. Bound by module.development (Development host) and module.validation (Validation adapter). Observation: its @verifies declarations name only scenario.development.* IDs, none owned by module.validation.

nodes.name: test_flow_specs.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests proving that every compiled LangGraph Flow has exactly one matching Flow Spec diagram (nodes, routing-labeled edges, in/out state) and that Functional API use (langgraph.func) is found by parsing rather than running. Verifies scenario.development.flow-specs and scenario.development.graph-api-only; bound by module.development as part of its Development host entity.
nodes.languageNotes: Scenario coverage is declared with the @verifies decorator from concorde.spec.verification, which tooling reads by parsing the test rather than executing it.

nodes.name: test_flow_surfaces.py
nodes.summary: Mock-instrumented tests of the development host's LangGraph flow surfaces: review membership retirement, code-owner review with and without recorded components, fresh discovery through the inspected factory, the discovery domain limit, coordination and stabilization flows stopping before dependent nodes, and scoped review stopping after the first unsuccessful result. Bound by module.development, module.harness (Studio) and module.query-routing (Query and Routing adapter); it verifies development and harness scenarios.

nodes.name: test_review.py
nodes.summary: Large mechanism suite for review and the development loop: review modes with full collections and fresh sessions, diff admission, policy previews, result validation, gap persistence and Spec repair, plan/tasks/implementation prerequisites, domain and component review aggregation, and the code-review repair loop. Process doubles replace Pi workers, so semantic detection quality is not measured. Bound by nine Modules (Framework acceptance tests of module.concorde plus the dev-loop, development, harness, implementation, planning, review, spec-authoring and validation entities). Observation: its @verifies declarations name development, planning, harness, implementation, spec-authoring and concorde scenarios but no scenario owned by module.review, module.validation or module.dev-loop.

nodes.name: test_run_capability.py
nodes.summary: Subprocess tests for the public launcher scripts/run-capability.py: it routes each of the nine public Skill names to the dispatcher, answers --runtime-check with LangGraph and Python identity, and refuses private, bare, unknown or multiple names with exit code 3 and unknown_capability. Verifies scenario.development.execute-unregistered, scenario.development.describe-policy and scenario.development.standalone-review; bound by module.development (Development host) and module.review (Review adapter). Observation: scenario.development.standalone-review is defined in module.review's scenarios.md despite its development prefix, and it is this file's only link to the review binding.

nodes.name: test_specify_loop.py
nodes.summary: Tests the specification Flow (concorde-specify-loop) standalone and inside development: reuse of unchanged owner and consumer review evidence, fresh reviews after consumer contract changes, rejection of author output prepared from changed sources, gap blocking, skip options, spec-only policy previews and Studio exposure. It borrows setUp, double and call_capability from ReviewTests. Bound by module.dev-loop, module.development, module.spec-authoring and module.specify-loop (Specification Flow adapter). Observation: its @verifies declarations name only development and spec-authoring scenarios, none owned by module.specify-loop.

nodes.name: test_standalone_review.py
nodes.summary: Tests the public concorde-review entry run through the Studio graph: the route result schema asks only for routing judgment, selection-only routes bind the exact intent to a read-only reviewer, rewritten routes fail with field diagnostics, and previews or blocked routes never launch a reviewer or create a change. Bound by module.development and module.review (Review adapter). Observation: it declares only scenario.development.* IDs, none owned by module.review.

nodes.name: test_structured_results.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the canonical structured tool-result envelope in concorde.spec.diagnostics: sorted artifacts and findings, schema_version 2, the status-to-exit-code mapping, and a live validate_repository result that carries only the normative envelope fields. Bound by module.development as Development host. Observation: it declares no @verifies scenarios, and the code it exercises lives in the concorde.spec package rather than in module.development's own sources.

nodes.name: test_target_discovery.py
nodes.summary: Tests target discovery and dispatch for public parent flows: the parent executes its inspected child and resume skips discovery, blocked discovery keeps typed output without entering dependent work, trusted bound targets and policy previews preserve admission, and target/dispatch flow revisions invalidate review evidence. It reuses WorktreeLifecycleTests fixtures. Bound by module.dev-loop, module.development, module.harness (Studio) and module.review.

nodes.name: test_typed_flows.py
nodes.summary: Exercises the typed Development loop and specify Flow state built by `loop_flow` and `specify_flow`: the artifact reducer keeps the newest reference per id in order, stage commands select their declared destinations while stops summarize, and both flows run on LangGraph `Command` objects while accumulating artifacts. Declares `scenario.development.flow-execution`. Bound by module.development as part of the Development host entity.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Docstring-only package marker that makes the distribution test directory importable, which lets test_protocol_guidance reuse the installer module loaded by test_install_concorde. Bound by module.distribution as part of its Installation entity.

nodes.name: test_build.py
nodes.summary: Extensive tests of the deterministic build in concorde.distribution.build: golden agent bodies and Skill projections, user-invoked checkout Skills, byte-identical rebuilds, check_build staleness detection that never writes, verify_fresh and load_model_instructions freshness gating, wire-helper invalidation and fail-closed build errors. Verifies scenario.distribution.build-render, build-write, build-check, build-stale-blocks-execution, build-checkout-skills-user-invoked and load-agent; bound by module.distribution as its Build entity.
nodes.languageNotes: Golden comparisons normalize the generated Skill 'source:' line with a regex so the tests stay independent of the source path recorded at build time.

nodes.name: test_check_docsite_types.py
nodes.summary: Tests scripts/development/check-docsite-types.py with a patched subprocess.run to prove that docsite preparation, npm dependency installation and the tsc --noEmit type check run only in disposable temporary copies, reuse a matching dependency marker, propagate the compiler exit code and leave the source tree unchanged. Verifies scenario.distribution.check-docsite-external; bound by module.distribution as Installation.

nodes.name: test_configure.py
nodes.summary: Tests concorde-configure: Pi worker model, thinking and timeout selections are proposed and applied atomically (re-applying is unchanged); retired launcher fields, unknown shapes and forged proposals are rejected; and an upgraded installed Protocol is rebound only when accept_protocol is requested, never rewriting the installer-owned copy. Verifies scenario.distribution.configure-apply, scenario.concorde.configure-apply and scenario.distribution.accept-protocol; bound by module.concorde (Framework acceptance tests) and module.distribution (Installation). Observation: its fixture config declares profile_version 13, while the Framework execution profile names profile_version 14.

nodes.name: test_consumer_install_end_to_end.py
nodes.summary: Out-of-process acceptance test that runs scripts/install-concorde.py --apply against a fresh git project using an offline LangGraph wheel index. It then checks the generated projections, the nine receipt-owned public Skills, the absence of legacy operation roots, the CLAUDE.md Protocol block and an installed run-capability describe-policy call. Verifies scenario.distribution.install-apply and scenario.concorde.adopt-initialize; bound by module.concorde (Framework acceptance tests) and module.distribution (Installation).

nodes.name: test_fresh_clone_bootstrap.py
nodes.summary: Acceptance test that makes a local shared git clone at HEAD and proves one 'scripts/concorde.py build' bootstraps it: build manifest, Protocol projection, Claude and Codex Skills, and a worktree guard that refuses 'git worktree add'. It also proves that editing a prompt without rebuilding makes invocations fail with stale_build and makes 'build --check' report invalid. Verifies scenario.distribution.build-write, worktree-guard-refuses, build-stale-blocks-execution and build-check; bound by module.distribution as Installation.

nodes.name: test_install_concorde.py
nodes.summary: In-process tests of the native installer scripts/install-concorde.py (loaded through importlib) and concorde.distribution.managed_runtime. They cover preview-by-default parsing, manifest authority, viewer lock integrity, native Codex output paths, idempotent preview and apply, preservation of unowned files, managed runtime rebuilds, rollback after dependency, smoke-test or Node failures, integration switching and safe relative paths. Verifies scenario.distribution.install-preview, install-apply, install-switch-integration, runtime-plan, runtime-provision and runtime-provision-failure; bound by module.distribution as Installation.
nodes.languageNotes: The hyphenated installer script cannot be imported normally, so it is loaded with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location and registered in sys.modules for reuse by other tests.

nodes.name: test_manifests.py
nodes.summary: Contract tests for the single concorde.json manifest: schema 3, version 7.0.0, architecture profile 14, workspace protocol 15, the install layout, the runtime launcher and the pinned UA viewer 2.9.0. They also check agreement with the runtime version, the capability, Skill and template inventory and lock files, the removal of legacy layouts, and a native source install that passes verify_fresh. Only the install test declares a scenario (scenario.distribution.install-apply); bound by module.distribution as Installation.

nodes.name: test_package_validation.py
nodes.summary: Large rule-by-rule suite for concorde.distribution.package_validation, built on temporary fixture packages. It covers prompt resolver and name-lint findings, capability module metadata (PUBLIC, DETERMINISTIC, USES cycles, context selection, Skills), WorkerProfile agents and children, schema contracts, build-output drift, and Spec alignment of capability inventories, types and error codes, plus an end-to-end run on the real package. Verifies scenario.distribution.capability-determinism and scenario.distribution.build-check; bound by module.distribution as Build. Observation: its fixtures still name the target 'service.alpha' and exercise a 'concorde.agents' metadata extension, while the Framework profile names only 'concorde.capabilities' as the project-owned extension.

nodes.name: test_prompt_resolver.py
nodes.summary: Rule tests for @include resolution in concorde.distribution.prompt_resolver: cycles, diamonds, missing or unsafe targets, unbound variables, malformed directives, worker/ambient audience separation, exclusion of Skill sources and Spec documents, Protocol prompt isolation, and prompt reachability, each asserting its reported rule ID. Bound by module.distribution as Build. Observation: none of its tests declare @verifies scenarios.

nodes.name: test_protocol_guidance.py
nodes.summary: Tests concorde.distribution.protocol_guidance through the real installer plan/apply transaction, with runtime provisioning mocked. Both integrations load a single installed Protocol asset without checkout policy; user bytes and modes survive upgrades, integration switches and cleanup; markers, symlinks, stale previews and modified owned blocks conflict without writing; and failures restore the prior state. Verifies scenario.distribution.install-apply, install-switch-integration, install-remove-guidance, install-conflict-rejected and scenario.concorde.adopt-conflict; bound by module.concorde (Framework acceptance tests) and module.distribution (Installation).

nodes.name: test_worktree_guard.py
nodes.summary: Offline tests of this source checkout's own worktree guard and the checked-in configuration that registers it. The module loads `scripts/worktree-guard.py` by file path with importlib, drives twenty worktree-creating and twenty ordinary command strings through the decision function for the Claude, Codex and PowerShell shell tools, checks that the EnterWorktree tool and worktree-isolated subagents are refused while other subagents pass, runs the guard as a real subprocess to pin its stdout/stderr/exit-code contract, and asserts the Claude settings deny rules, Codex hooks, Codex rules and Codex execpolicy all register it. Nothing here touches a real agent runtime or creates a worktree. Declares `scenario.distribution.worktree-guard-refuses`. Bound by module.distribution as part of the Installation entity.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the harness test package. Bound by module.harness under its Capability and Harness model entity.

nodes.name: test_boundaries.py
nodes.summary: Boundary tests for Spec context and authority: shared Markdown stays one-hop context, consumer and target authors cannot change provider truth or duplicate identities, implementation listing rules, code appears only as digests in implementation snapshots, Protocol tampering and profile-7 downgrade are rejected, policy previews launch no model, changed Specs or intent force replanning, and stale or failed file replacements never overwrite content. Bound by module.harness (Context resolution) and module.spec-authoring (Spec Authoring adapter).

nodes.name: test_capability_node.py
nodes.summary: Unittest suite checking that a CapabilityNode's LangGraph state schema contains exactly the declared contract fields, that invocation validates typed context in and result out, and that the compiled plan flow exposes its worker nodes for inspection. Bound by module.harness as entity.harness.agent-model (Capability and Harness model); declares scenario.harness.agent-node and scenario.harness.flow-inspection via @verifies.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Concorde's @verifies decorator from concorde.spec.verification to bind test methods to Spec scenario IDs, which the deterministic coverage check reads by parsing rather than executing.

nodes.name: test_change_worktree.py
nodes.summary: Tests concorde.harness.change_worktree.create_worktree on a committed fixture repository: a self-hosted candidate worktree (package root equals project root) is built and passes verify_fresh, while worktree creation for an unrelated project or without a package root attempts no build. Bound by module.development and module.harness as Worktree lifecycle. Observation: it declares no @verifies scenarios, so this lifecycle behavior is not linked to any scenario.

nodes.name: test_check_executor.py
