nodes.summary: Reads the registry's target file listings and returns the top-level roots this check's copy would leave out, tolerating an unreadable registry so stub fixtures still run.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Fails fast on uncopied listing roots, then copies the listed directories and files into a temporary project while ignoring disposable and generated trees, and runs npm ci, the Concorde build, the views unit tests and vitest there, returning the first non-zero exit code.

nodes.name: loadPolicy
nodes.summary: Loads and validates the host-issued worker policy named by CONCORDE_WORKER_POLICY, refusing to start outside a Concorde worker or on an unsupported policy schema version.

nodes.name: canonical
nodes.summary: Resolves a target to its canonical absolute path by realpath-ing the longest existing prefix and re-appending the missing components, so a not-yet-created path still resolves through symlinks.
nodes.languageNotes: Resolving symlinks before the grant comparison is what keeps a symlinked path from escaping its read or write root.

nodes.name: hostRequest
nodes.summary: Sends one newline-terminated JSON request over the host's Unix socket and resolves with the parsed JSON reply, rejecting on a connection or parse error.

nodes.name: concordeWorker
nodes.summary: Default extension entry point: canonicalizes the policy's read and write roots, registers the subagent capability ceiling and required child extensions on session start, overrides the system prompt, blocks every tool call outside the grants (including child delegation and child submissions), and registers the submit_result, report_issue and run_checks tools.

nodes.name: check_copy
nodes.summary: Runs the TypeScript check inside a temporary docsite copy: it derives a dependency identity digest from package.json plus package-lock.json, symlinks an already-validated `node_modules` when the marker matches or otherwise runs `npm ci`, generates the real scoped sidebar with a small inline tsx program, then invokes `tsc --noEmit` and returns its exit code.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Compares the vendored LangGraph version with the installed distribution and the lockfile pin, then the vendored pi-subagents version with the pin in `pi/package.json`, printing the comparison and returning 1 with concrete submodule remediation commands when either disagrees.

nodes.name: audit
nodes.summary: The whole Spec audit: validates the document-unit repository, collects requirements, scenarios, entities, contracts and bindings across all targets, verifies that every `specs/**` Markdown file is registered with its paired metadata member, resolves heading and standalone anchors plus relative Markdown links to real definitions, and with a git baseline re-reads committed sources to report identities and digests that changed.

nodes.name: submodules
nodes.summary: Reads `.gitmodules` through `git config --list` and groups each submodule's keys (path, url, and the Concorde-specific sparse-checkout patterns) into one entry per submodule name, returning an empty list when the file is absent.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Performs the media-free checkout of one submodule: verifies the superproject records a commit, refuses to clobber an existing directory, creates a blobless partial clone, applies the recorded sparse-checkout patterns, fetches only the pinned commit and checks it out, failing with the fetch's stderr.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command entry point that parses `--check`, enumerates the declared submodules, reports those already checked out, and either lists or initializes the missing ones, printing each resulting pinned commit.

nodes.name: Unit
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing one scheduled test subprocess — its module, target (module or single test id), serial flag, measured duration, return code, captured output and the parsed counts of tests, failures, errors, skips, expected failures and unexpected successes — with helpers for its fan-out part name and failure state.

nodes.name: ModuleReport
nodes.summary: Dataclass aggregating all units belonging to one test module, exposing the module's wall-clock time (the slowest unit), total test count and whether any unit failed.

nodes.name: run_unit
nodes.summary: Executes one unit as `<python> -m unittest <target>` from the repository root, timing it, capturing combined output and return code, then delegating to the summary parser to fill in the counts.

nodes.name: parse_summary
nodes.summary: Extracts unittest's textual result summary from a unit's output — the `Ran N tests` line and the OK/FAILED line with its parenthesised failure, error, skip, expected-failure and unexpected-success counts — and derives the unit's status, tolerating output that contains no recognisable summary.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Renders one unit as a single human-readable line combining its module or fan-out part name, status, duration and the non-zero outcome counts.

nodes.name: build_units
nodes.summary: Builds the schedule: concurrently enumerates test ids for the fan-out modules using the target interpreter's own loader, expands each into per-test units, keeps the remaining modules as whole units, and sorts everything longest-file-first so the slowest work starts earliest.

nodes.name: print_report
nodes.summary: Prints the final per-module table and the aggregate totals — units, tests, failures, errors, skips, wall-clock versus summed CPU time and the achieved speedup — followed by an explicit list of every failed unit.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command entry point that parses interpreter, job, sequential and JSON options, discovers or filters the test modules, builds the unit schedule, runs the parallel batch through a thread pool with live completion lines followed by the serial units, prints the report, optionally writes a JSON dump and returns non-zero if any unit failed.

nodes.name: load_package
nodes.summary: Loads and validates the standalone package manifest at the given root, rejecting a symlinked or missing manifest, checking the declared version, required keys and root set, and normalising every declared relative path before returning the immutable Package record.

nodes.name: _package_files
nodes.summary: Walks the distributable package roots to build the exact inventory of framework files the installer may write, applying the deterministic exclusion rules and refusing symlinks or paths escaping the package root.

nodes.name: desired_outputs
nodes.summary: Computes the complete map of project-relative output paths to their intended bytes — installed framework files, the Protocol copy, project default files, docsite template files and integration configuration — which the plan and receipt are both derived from.

nodes.name: installation_plan
nodes.summary: Diffs the desired outputs against the target project's current state and the prior ownership receipt to produce the ordered action list — create, update, keep, remove of previously owned files, plus managed runtime and viewer provisioning steps — refusing to touch unrelated user content that the receipt does not claim.

nodes.name: _receipt
nodes.summary: Builds the ownership receipt written to `.concorde/install.json`: the schema version, package version, integration selection, each installed output with its digest, and the managed runtime record, so a later run knows exactly which bytes it owns.

nodes.name: apply_plan
nodes.summary: Executes the planned actions against the target project — creating parents, writing framework and default files, removing outputs the receipt no longer claims, provisioning the managed Python runtime and the pinned viewer, and finally writing the fresh receipt — restoring owned installation state when a step fails.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command entry point that parses the target, integration and protocol-guidance options, loads the package, computes the plan, prints it, and either stops at the preview or applies it, mapping install and runtime errors to a readable message and a non-zero exit code.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses the action (`list`, `show`, `archive-reflections`), optional Issue id and project root, refuses a project without `.concorde/config.json`, dispatches to the Issue store or the Reflection archiver, and prints either the result or an error object as JSON.

nodes.name: _declared_capability
nodes.summary: Reads `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, parses its YAML front matter and returns the declared `capability` value, raising an unknown-capability error when the source is unreadable or declares no capability.

nodes.name: _runtime_check
nodes.summary: Offline smoke check used by the managed runtime provisioner: confirms the capability module exposes a callable `run` and a `REQUEST` data boundary and that LangGraph's Graph API exports START, END and StateGraph, then prints the resolved versions as JSON without touching stdin or launching an agent.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command entry point that admits exactly one public skill name, disables ambient bytecode caches beside the receipt-owned framework bytes, resolves the skill's capability module, and either runs the offline runtime check or hands the invocation to the shared trusted stdin/envelope handler.

nodes.name: _installed_viewer
nodes.summary: Resolves the installer-owned viewer for a project: reads `.concorde/framework/concorde.json`, refuses symlinked framework paths, validates the declared viewer package, version and entry point, and returns the viewer record together with the real path of its executable module.

nodes.name: _raw_graph
nodes.summary: Admits the existing raw knowledge-graph input by checking the declared graph paths in order, requiring a single real JSON object file, and reporting a readable error when none of the declared locations holds a usable graph.

nodes.name: _node
nodes.summary: Locates a usable Node interpreter on PATH and verifies it satisfies the viewer's declared minimum version by parsing `node --version` with a strict semver pattern.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command entry point that resolves the project root, installed viewer, raw graph, Node interpreter and port, then starts the viewer process, translating launch errors into a readable message and a non-zero exit code.

nodes.name: _command_text
nodes.summary: Extracts the inspectable command text from a hook payload's tool input, handling the different shapes Claude Code and Codex use for shell invocations so the guard sees the whole command including quoted strings.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: The guard's decision function: returns a blocking verdict for `WorktreeCreate`, for `PreToolUse` on `EnterWorktree`, for subagent tools requesting `isolation: "worktree"`, and for shell tools whose command text matches `git worktree add/move` or a `claude --worktree` launch; everything else is allowed.

nodes.name: _deny_output
nodes.summary: Renders a refusal in the shape both hosts understand: a `permissionDecision: deny` object with the reason on stdout, keyed to the payload's hook event so Claude Code and Codex both treat it as a block.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command entry point that either prints the long `--explain` rationale or reads one JSON hook payload from stdin, evaluates it, and exits 0 to allow silently, 2 with the deny object and reason to block, or 1 on unreadable input so a hook error stays visible without refusing every tool call.

nodes.name: _package_version
nodes.summary: Reads the packaged `concorde.json` manifest relative to the package file and returns its `version` string, returning the literal "source" when the file cannot be read, decoded or parsed or holds no usable version.

nodes.name: CapabilityFlowState
nodes.summary: Total-optional TypedDict state channel for the capability flow: the terminating `result`, the accumulated `policies` and `events`, the `invocation` record and the optional `expected_workspace`.

nodes.name: build_capability_flow
nodes.summary: Compiles the named capability graph with the caller's node factory, wiring each admission stage to jump straight to finalize once a `result` is present, nesting the dispatch subflow at `execute`, compiling without a checkpointer, and exposing that child for inspection.

nodes.name: expose_stateless_subflow
nodes.summary: Registers the actual compiled child on a parent node's `subgraphs` so LangGraph's Studio/xray discovery sees it, refusing any child not compiled with `checkpointer=False` so the adapter cannot suggest that internal checkpoints are resumable.

nodes.name: CoordinationState
nodes.summary: TypedDict state shared by both coordination graphs: the optional terminating `output` and the `route` a stability decision selects.

nodes.name: build_coordination_flow
nodes.summary: Compiles the six-stage component writer graph as a straight chain in which any stage that sets `output` ends the flow immediately instead of advancing to its successor.

nodes.name: build_stabilization_flow
nodes.summary: Compiles the shared-consumer stabilization loop: snapshot then verify_components, stopping on output, otherwise check_stability, which routes back to snapshot or ends according to the recorded `route`.

nodes.name: catalog
nodes.summary: Returns the compiled-name to factory map of every executable Concorde Flow, lazily importing the development, harness and issues factories and binding each to a stub node factory so the inert build matches the executed topology.

nodes.name: topology
nodes.summary: Projects one compiled Flow into the plain node list and source/target/conditional edge list that the Flow Spec check and publication read.

nodes.name: PlanState
nodes.summary: TypedDict state for the plan graph: the `route` each node selects, the terminating `result` and the produced `output`.

nodes.name: build_plan_flow
nodes.summary: Compiles assess_context, author_plan and persist_plan with explicit route-driven edges so an unsuccessful assessment or plan ends the flow, then attaches the two worker CapabilityNode subflows for inspection.

nodes.name: ProjectState
nodes.summary: TypedDict state for the project graph: the selected `route`, the produced `output` and the terminating `result`.

nodes.name: build_project_flow
nodes.summary: Compiles the four-node project graph whose single fan-out from select_action names configure, propose, apply and END as the only admissible destinations.

nodes.name: TopologyState
nodes.summary: TypedDict state for both topology graphs: the terminating `result`, the authoring `occurrence` counter, the selected `route` and the produced `output`.

nodes.name: build_topology_flow
nodes.summary: Compiles the topology authoring graph with a per-Module authoring loop followed by candidate validation, affected-context review and persistence, every stage able to end the flow through its route.

nodes.name: build_topology_apply_flow
nodes.summary: Compiles the atomic application graph (admit_application, validate_application, apply_atomically, cleanup) where a present `result` short-circuits to END before the next mutating step.

nodes.name: ManagedRuntimeError
nodes.summary: Error raised when a managed runtime cannot be planned or provisioned safely; every validation and verification failure in this module fails closed through it.

nodes.name: ViewerSpec
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the validated viewer contract read from the build manifest: provider, version, npm package and lock with their integrity string and digest, asset URL, SHA-256 and byte size, install-relative path, entrypoint, launcher and graph paths.

nodes.name: ManagedRuntimeSpec
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing the whole desired managed runtime: venv, requirements and launcher paths, the Python to use, requirements and combined runtime digests, the pinned LangGraph and Concorde versions, the Skills to verify, the nested ViewerSpec, and the Pi lock digest with its pinned subagents version.

nodes.name: _json_object
nodes.summary: Reads a regular non-symlink file, decodes it as UTF-8 JSON and requires the result to be a JSON object, raising ManagedRuntimeError with the caller's label at each step.

nodes.name: _load_viewer_spec
nodes.summary: Validates the manifest's viewer configuration into a ViewerSpec: requires every declared string, forces relative install paths, demands an https asset URL with a `sha256:` digest, checks the graph paths, then cross-reads the viewer's package.json and package-lock.json to confirm the locked version, its `sha512-` integrity and resolved URL before digesting the lock.

nodes.name: load_runtime_spec
nodes.summary: Validates the whole managed-runtime section of a build manifest into a ManagedRuntimeSpec: safe relative venv, requirements and launcher paths, a requirements file consisting of exactly one pinned `langgraph==X.Y.Z` line, the packaged Pi sources with their pinned `pi-subagents` semver, and the combined requirements/viewer/pi digest that identifies the runtime.

nodes.name: _runtime_path
nodes.summary: Resolves the venv path under the target project one component at a time, refusing absolute or escaping paths and any symlinked or non-directory intermediate component.

nodes.name: _read_marker
nodes.summary: Reads the runtime's `.concorde-runtime.json` ownership marker, returning None when it is absent, unreadable, not a JSON object, or not the expected marker schema and owner.

nodes.name: _offline_environment
nodes.summary: Copies the process environment and overrides the package-manager variables that force fully offline, non-interactive installs, so provisioning never reaches the network implicitly.

nodes.name: _run
nodes.summary: Runs one subprocess with captured text output, an explicit working directory and a caller-supplied environment, centralizing how this module invokes external tools.

nodes.name: _tool_version
nodes.summary: Invokes an external tool with its version flag in the given directory and returns the reported version, raising ManagedRuntimeError with the caller's label when the call fails.

nodes.name: _verify_viewer
nodes.summary: Checks that an installed viewer matches its spec — install root and entrypoint present, locked package version as recorded — so a stale or hand-modified install is never accepted as verified.

nodes.name: _install_viewer
nodes.summary: Installs the pinned viewer npm package into the managed runtime from its offline lock, staging the install before it becomes the live root and verifying the result afterwards.

nodes.name: _install_pi
nodes.summary: Installs the pinned Pi worker extension package from the packaged `pi/` sources and their lock into the runtime's share directory under the offline environment.

nodes.name: _healthy
nodes.summary: Probes an existing runtime: the venv Python must exist and, under an isolated interpreter, report exactly the pinned LangGraph version, and the installed viewer must still verify; any failure returns False rather than raising.

nodes.name: plan_runtime
nodes.summary: Decides the runtime action without changing anything: conflict for unsafe, symlinked, non-directory or unowned paths, create when absent, unchanged when the marker's requirements, viewer, Pi and verified-Skill facts all match a healthy runtime, and rebuild otherwise.

nodes.name: _verify_skills
nodes.summary: Runs each declared Skill's launcher with `--runtime-check` in the target project under the offline environment, parses the JSON reply and returns the Skills that verified against one consistent Python interpreter.

nodes.name: _write_marker
nodes.summary: Writes the `.concorde-runtime.json` ownership marker recording the schema, owner, requirements/viewer/Pi digests, verified Skills and the observed Python, Node and npm versions, so a later plan can recognize the runtime this installer created.

nodes.name: provision_runtime
nodes.summary: Creates or rebuilds the managed virtual environment for the planned action: builds the venv with the bootstrap Python, installs the pinned requirements offline, installs the viewer and Pi packages, verifies the declared Skills and only then writes the ownership marker.

nodes.name: GuidanceError
nodes.summary: Error raised when the root agent instruction file's Concorde-owned Protocol block is malformed, forged, unowned, or at a path the installer does not own.

nodes.name: entry
nodes.summary: Builds the delimited Concorde-owned block for the given integration, referencing the packaged Protocol file as a plain read instruction for Codex and an `@` include for Claude rather than inlining Protocol prose.

nodes.name: split
nodes.summary: Splits file bytes into the text before the owned block, the block itself and the text after, rejecting duplicated, extra or misordered Concorde Protocol markers instead of consuming arbitrary user text.

nodes.name: plan
nodes.summary: Plans the owned edit to AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md: validates the relative path and file kind, requires any existing block to match the receipt digest before modification, prepends a new block so user fences and size limits cannot hide it, and returns the change record with before/after digests alongside the merged bytes.

nodes.name: BatchState
nodes.summary: TypedDict state for the batch graph: the current `index`, the last item `output` and the `stop` flag that ends the loop.

nodes.name: build_batch_flow
nodes.summary: Compiles a named, stateless two-node loop between select_item and the caller's item node, where either node routes to END the moment `stop` is set.

nodes.name: run_batch_flow
nodes.summary: Runs an operation over a materialized item sequence through the compiled batch graph, advancing on a None result, stopping and returning the first non-None result, and bounding LangGraph recursion by the item count.

nodes.name: handoff_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the P10 handoff draft: validates that the initial directory is absolute, assembles the known facts into a JSON block with explicit unknown placeholders, appends next steps, completion criteria and the no-extra-authority statement, and wraps it in a backtick fence longer than any run inside the text.

nodes.name: WorktreeBoundaryError
nodes.summary: Error raised when a requested mutation has no authorized isolated Git worktree, or when the Git preflight itself cannot be trusted.

nodes.name: WorktreeBoundary
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding a checkout's immutable Git identity — project root, repository root, HEAD commit, git dir, common dir and whether it is an isolated linked worktree — with a `to_dict` projection for reporting.

nodes.name: _git
nodes.summary: Runs one `git -C <root>` command and returns its trimmed stdout, converting an OS error, a non-zero exit status or an empty result into WorktreeBoundaryError.

nodes.name: inspect_worktree
nodes.summary: Returns the checkout's immutable Git identity from `git rev-parse` queries alone, refusing a symlinked or non-directory project root and marking the boundary isolated when the git dir differs from the common dir; it never reads working-tree file contents.

nodes.name: require_isolated_worktree
nodes.summary: Enforces the mutation boundary before agent-authored writes: rejects symlinked or non-directory roots and directories that are not Git worktrees, and rejects the primary worktree with a message naming the committed HEAD to branch from, returning the boundary only for a linked worktree or when `allow_primary_worktree` carries the developer's explicit authorization.

nodes.name: CapabilityModuleContractTests
nodes.summary: Asserts the single checked capability inventory covers model code and composed nodes, keeps property and transport contracts independent, makes `uses` the only acyclic dependency relation, projects parent state into a model subgraph without disturbing unrelated channels, runs a module directly as a LangGraph node, preserves the failure envelope and runtime context in the host state node, and rejects a wrong wire identity before state projection.

nodes.name: InProcessCompositionTests
nodes.summary: Checks that in-process composition refuses an unregistered capability identity before any dynamic import, and that child resolution matches the declared `uses` pairs exactly, including model nodes.

nodes.name: TypedFlowStateTests
nodes.summary: Checks the typed Development flow state end to end: newest-reference-per-id ordering in the artifact reducer, declared destination selection and stop summarization for stage commands, and artifact accumulation while the loop and specify flows run on LangGraph `Command` values.

nodes.name: GuardDecisionTests
nodes.summary: Drives the guard's decision function over the creating and ordinary command tables for the Claude, Codex and PowerShell shell tools, and checks that the EnterWorktree tool and worktree-isolated subagents are refused while other subagents, worktree inspection commands and unrelated events and tools pass.

nodes.name: GuardProcessTests
nodes.summary: Runs the guard script as a real subprocess to pin its process contract: a refusal prints the permission decision on stdout and the reason on stderr, a worktree-create refusal uses only the exit code and stderr, allowed calls stay silent, unreadable input is a visible non-blocking error, and check mode decides a command text for people and scripts.

nodes.name: IntegrationFilesTests
nodes.summary: Pins the checked-in integration files that register the guard: Claude settings deny native worktree creation and wire up the hook, Codex hooks register it for shell commands, Codex rules forbid `git worktree add` and `move`, and the Codex execpolicy accepts those rules.

nodes.name: _stage_context
nodes.summary: Builds a typed stage-context fixture used by the capability-node tests, assembling the invocation context values the node contract requires.

nodes.name: CapabilityNodeTests
nodes.summary: Three test methods asserting exact node state schemas against DATA_SCHEMAS, typed validation of invocation input and output including TypedDataError rejection, and that build_plan_flow's compiled graph names its worker nodes.

nodes.name: SessionHandoffTests
nodes.summary: Patches pathlib.Path.resolve to assert the prompt builder never enters the target directory, then verifies absolute-path validation, complete-context preservation and fence escaping in the generated P10 handoff prompt.

nodes.name: UsageRecordTests
nodes.summary: Provides host and invocation SimpleNamespace factories plus three tests covering append-only usage recording, per-dimension summary totals, and best-effort persistence that degrades without breaking worker execution.

nodes.name: ArchiveTests
nodes.summary: Two temporary-directory tests covering byte-preserving reflection archival with an empty issue list afterwards, and fail-closed behavior on destination conflicts and symlinks.

nodes.name: source
nodes.summary: Builds the canonical legacy Markdown fixture containing the retired concorde-document, concorde-entities, concorde-dependencies and concorde-contract-binding blocks that migration must convert.

nodes.name: migrate
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper invoking plan_document_migration on encoded fixture bytes so individual tests can vary the source text and primary-document flag.

nodes.name: ContentMigrationTests
nodes.summary: Thirteen tests asserting the conversion contract: recorded meaning moves to reading once without a file inventory, metadata keeps only anchors rather than copied semantics, companions do not acquire the entry template, unknown machine fields and profile inventories are preserved or flagged, and old visibility is never reinterpreted as reading membership.

nodes.name: RegisteredMigrationPreviewTests
nodes.summary: Three tests covering registry-level migration preview: an activated checkout refuses repeated legacy conversion without writing, missing or invalid members block the preview instead of claiming partial success, and registration never discovers neighbor files or accepts duplicate ownership.

nodes.name: admit
nodes.summary: Fixture factory that admits a reading/metadata pair into the content model under test, letting each case vary the Markdown body, JSON companion and primary-entry flag.

nodes.name: DocumentUnitTests
nodes.summary: Fifteen tests over document-unit admission: role explicitness, immutability of admitted sources through declaration views, meaning derivation that stops at the next anchor, no I/O during admission, safe deterministic companion filenames, and mechanical entity/dependency/participant identity rules without a reading inventory.

nodes.name: ReadingStructureTests
nodes.summary: Seven tests over the required reading shape: early nonempty Terminology that is not an entity inventory, the five front sections as a reading path, plain-prose Purpose alongside structured contracts elsewhere, and invalid duplicate or redirected identity anchors.

nodes.name: unit
nodes.summary: Constructs a named document-unit fixture with its reading Markdown and schema-2 metadata companion, optionally wired to a peer Module for reference and participant-binding cases.

nodes.name: fixture
nodes.summary: Materializes a complete multi-Module project fixture under a temporary root — registry, owned documents, references and bound implementation files — that the repository tests resolve contexts against.

nodes.name: DocumentUnitRepositoryTests
nodes.summary: Twenty-nine tests plus setUp/repository/save/change helpers covering context resolution, grant materialization, stale-input and forged-identity rejection, registry-only files that cannot widen an implementation grant, closed resolution wire shapes, and atomic overlay application with rollback.

nodes.name: terminology_rows
nodes.summary: Parses a reading document's Terminology table into rows while skipping fenced code blocks and stopping before unrelated later tables, giving the tests a fence-aware view of declared terms.

nodes.name: TerminologyReferenceTests
nodes.summary: Ten tests loading the live SpecRepository in setUpClass and asserting that every selected Module context contains definitions for its included reading, that reader dependencies have definition entries, and that problem definitions stay distinct from Module navigation.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads the prompt command from stdin, branches on the selected scenario, and emits the scripted response, dialog request, tool_execution_end, settle frame and session-statistics records.

nodes.name: ScaffoldCreationTests
nodes.summary: Three temporary-directory tests that patch changes.os.replace to inject concurrent creation and staging failures, asserting SpecError or OSError propagation with no orphaned or clobbered files.

nodes.name: ViewerLauncherTests
nodes.summary: Builds a temporary project containing a runtime marker, installed viewer entrypoint and knowledge graph derived from the real concorde.json viewer lock, then runs seven tests over launch forwarding, graph selection, runtime verification and interruption handling.

nodes.name: _implementation_digest
nodes.summary: Digests a Module's implementation context: its declared listing entries plus the current bytes of every file those entries bind, giving the implementation half of the revision identity that stale-input checks and evidence records compare against.

nodes.name: _target_revision
nodes.summary: Digests a Module's Spec revision: the target declaration, the accepted Protocol binding and the resolved Spec context value, giving the Spec half of the revision identity that invalidates plans, reviews and evidence when any of them changes.

This collaboration applies when staging the selected change, resuming cleanup or processing a separately authorized primary merge.

- [Host admission](../development/interfaces.md#capability-execution-boundary); Recheck admitted intent and returned identities before accepting host state; a rejected result cannot advance the dependent step.

This collaboration applies when the actual integration tree contains concorde.json and therefore represents a Concorde package checkout.

- [Integration build and package validation](../distribution/build.md); Require the integrated checkout's own fresh build and validation; a build failure prevents delivery.

tour.title: Start Here: The Launcher
tour.description: Concorde is a framework for architecture-aware Specs, project understanding, and scoped agent workers invoked from Codex or Claude. The README lays out the five reasons the framework exists and the workflow it supports, while scripts/concorde.py is the portable entry point every bootstrap instruction uses: it locates the package root relative to its own file, prepends src/ to sys.path and hands control to concorde.distribution.cli.main. concorde.json is the package manifest that declares the compatibility numbers, the Skill namespace, the Python floor and everything the installer may distribute. The graph's imports edge connects this launcher to the CLI module, which provides the traversal backbone for subsequent steps.
tour.languageLesson: A Python launcher can add its src directory to sys.path so imports work from a source checkout without package installation. scripts/concorde.py then uses an ordinary static from-import. Path setup can challenge an import resolver, but does not make the statement a dynamic import.

tour.title: The Spec Protocol
tour.description: Everything in Concorde serves one standard: the Spec Protocol, authored here as a five-chapter bundle that the topology analysis found to be the most tightly interlinked cluster in the whole project. It defines a Module as one cohesive software responsibility with a complete specification and a human-readable subset, splits documents into module role (explanation) and implementation role (requirements, scenarios, canonical contracts), and fixes exactly how a Module's context is resolved from its owned documents plus one level of explicit references. The format chapter prescribes the physical representation, and the prompts manifest composes these same chapters into the rule bundle delivered with every worker's system prompt.
tour.languageLesson: A Protocol document unit is a pair: a Markdown reading file and a same-path `.md.json` metadata companion. Reading prose carries meaning; the JSON carries identity, ownership, role, entity file bindings and dependency declarations. Registering the Markdown path registers both members, and neither can be owned or included alone.

tour.title: Charter and Vocabulary
tour.description: With the Protocol understood, read how Concorde applies it to itself. The root Module Spec states the Framework's purpose and maps each installed Skill to its exact completion boundary, recording that the root owns no product code and realizes its contract through child Modules. The concepts topic is the single most referenced document in the graph: it is the canonical Terminology table defining Module, Context, Grant, Capability, Worker, Harness, Flow, Candidate and Issue, and it is pulled into the Spec context of all seventeen Modules. The project control record binds this checkout to Protocol 9.0.0 with an exact manifest digest, and AGENTS.md is the policy governing anyone — human or agent — working in the checkout.

tour.title: The Spec Model
tour.description: This is where the Protocol stops being prose and becomes Python. SpecRepository checks the config's profile version, loads the registry through the document-unit backend and admits the installed Protocol copy; repository_base holds the shared surface beneath it, and content_model defines the DocumentUnit and SourceMember primitives that admit one reading/metadata pair, resolve anchors and check reading structure. typed_data is the single most depended-upon file in the project (44 incoming edges): every capability and leaf boundary passes values through its strict JSON decoding, canonical serialization, schema checking and digest-bound envelopes.
tour.languageLesson: typed_data rejects duplicate JSON keys rather than silently keeping the last one, and refuses project-relative paths that resolve through symlinks. Treating decoding itself as a trust boundary is a recurring pattern here: data crossing an agent or process boundary is validated structurally before any code interprets it.

tour.title: Command Line Surface
tour.description: cli.py is the stable argparse interface for the installed Tools, dispatching validate, docsite, ua-graph, ua-analyze, build, protocol-manifest and usage, requiring an isolated worktree for mutating commands and always printing a canonical JSON result envelope with a status-derived exit code. Observation: most of its subcommands actually realize Views, Spec and Harness responsibilities, so this one file — bound by the Distribution Module — fronts work the Specs assign elsewhere. The validator behind `validate` is deterministic: it parses Mermaid diagrams, checks reading structure, requirement and scenario grammar, entity bindings, Terminology links and test coverage, and it explicitly reports that passing does not prove semantic completeness.

tour.title: Context and Permission
tour.description: The Harness is the heart of the framework: how a bounded agent is configured. context.py freezes the immutable cognitive inputs of one invocation — the per-Module Spec resolution, implementation entries, file names and, in code phases, artifact bytes, external references and stage inputs — each identified by a digest, so any changed selection becomes stale context rather than a silent drift. permissions.py compiles least privilege by intersecting the worker contract's declared effects with the host's narrowing binding and the invocation's concrete paths into one digest-bound policy that defaults to deny and refuses any widening. worker_profile.py binds a Capability's optional model execution profile byte for byte to the current build manifest.

tour.title: Candidate Worktrees
tour.description: A change under Concorde lives in its own Git worktree, and change_worktree.py owns that lifecycle: it lists worktrees, serializes registry updates under a repository lock, validates .concorde/worktree.json state, creates linked candidate worktrees, tracks owner binding, target progress, repair-graph records and Issue blockers, and snapshots the deliverable tree without touching the caller's index. This is what makes partial work inspectable and resumable instead of being presented as finished delivery. Observation: it lazily imports Issue store and Distribution build code even though the Harness Module declares uses only of Spec and Distribution.

tour.title: Capabilities as Nodes
tour.description: Concorde has exactly one unit of executable work: a Capability, which is a State-based LangGraph node declaring PUBLIC, CONTEXT_SELECTION, DETERMINISTIC, USES, STATE and an optional model PROFILE. CapabilityNode resolves a registered capability from capabilities/, derives TypedDict input and output schemas from its declared types, and compiles run(state, runtime) into a single-node subgraph. The key design decision is visible here: trusted context travels in LangGraph's Runtime, never in State, so state channels carry data while permission and context remain the host's business. The execution reference is the implementation-role Spec that tabulates the host-adapter capabilities and owns the matching Flow Specs.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph's Graph API builds a StateGraph by declaring nodes and edges before compiling. Nodes are execution logic that read a typed state and return updates; edges are routing logic. Concorde requires this API (not the Functional API) precisely because a declared graph can be inspected — by a Flow Spec check and by Studio — while control flow hidden in ordinary Python cannot.

tour.title: The Development Host
tour.description: capability_host.py has the highest fan-out in the entire project (79 outgoing edges): it is the trusted host that admits and executes every public capability as a LangGraph Flow. For each stage it freezes the context from Step 6, compiles the least-privilege policy, launches the worker, records evidence and usage, and returns the typed result envelope — tying together nearly everything seen so far. Observation: the Development Module's own entry records that the invocation-binding mechanics of Invocation.stage and MainInvocation.stage still live in this file even though they belong to the Harness host contract, which is a known structural mismatch rather than a settled design.

tour.title: The Lifecycle Flows
tour.description: These are the graphs the host executes. dispatch_flow routes an admitted request to an entry leaf or through target admission, embedding the query, topology, plan, project, issues, loop and specification subflows so Studio can observe them. loop_flow declares the development topology: a typed state whose artifact channel merges through a reducer, a stage successor map and the Command helper each stage returns — while performing no project access itself. dev_loop is the public Capability a user reaches through the concorde-dev-loop Skill: route one change, compose the specify loop, then plan, task, implement, validate and review to a ready candidate, with `FLOW = {"max_repair_iterations": 2}` bounding the loop's single automatic revision edge from code review back to tasks.
tour.languageLesson: Two LangGraph mechanics carry this design. A reducer on a state channel says how concurrent updates merge instead of overwriting each other, which is what lets parallel stages contribute artifacts. A node returning a Command combines a state update with an explicit routing decision, so a stage can say both what it produced and where control goes next.

tour.title: Running a Worker
tour.description: This is where a model-backed Capability actually becomes a process. pi_worker.py launches one worker as an isolated Pi process: it validates the launch against its tools, children and write grants, builds a private run directory with copied credentials, child agent definitions, the compiled policy and the system prompt, serves host tools over a Unix socket and admits exactly one submitted result. pi_rpc.py is the strict JSONL client that drives that process, answering every interactive dialog as cancelled and mapping deadlines, host interruption and protocol faults onto distinct timeout, cancelled and error classes while always killing the process. Note the honest limitation the Spec itself states: shell commands are protected only by credential scrubbing and the in-process tool gate, not by an OS sandbox.

tour.title: Review and Issues
tour.description: Work produced by the flows in Step 10 is judged by an independent reviewer and by a durable Issue record. review.py builds a digest-bound review input from scoped Git history, runs exactly one reviewer worker with no write authority, persists the artifact with its change-state evidence, and expands scope to Spec consumers and changed-file peers in separate contexts — deciding when existing revision-bound evidence may be reused or must be refreshed. The Issue store keeps one Markdown file per Issue under .concorde/issues/ with a closed JSON record, file-locked digest-bound publication and idempotent report allocation, while issue_flow is the LangGraph graph for listing, reporting, reopening and bounded solving with a six-decision limit and write-ahead restoration.

tour.title: Docsite and Graph Views
tour.description: The Views layer turns Specs into things people read. The concorde-content Docusaurus plugin loads the scoped registry, requires a matching materialization identity, publishes page metadata without bodies as global data, and in postBuild checks source freshness and route coverage before writing a build manifest and alias redirect stubs; model.ts is the shared registry model beneath it, with 18 files depending on it. On the Python side, ua_analysis.py is the developer-authorized bridge that preflights the Understand Anything plugin, prepares a Spec-derived seed graph and per-Module context indexes, probes permissions and runs the native analysis under a lock — the same mechanism that produced this tour. Observation: validateScopedBuild does not call requireScoped itself and relies on the loader's own profile check.
tour.languageLesson: A Docusaurus plugin is a lifecycle object: loadContent gathers data, contentLoaded registers routes and global data, and postBuild runs after the static site is emitted. Doing verification in postBuild means the check sees the real build output rather than the author's intent — the same fail-closed philosophy as the digest checks in Step 6.

tour.title: Build, CI and Tests
tour.description: Finally, what ships and what proves it. build.py deterministically produces every distributed projection — worker instructions, the public Skills for the Claude and Codex integrations, the Studio graph list, Protocol assets and exported JSON schemas — plus a source/output manifest and the freshness checks that host and worker resolution fail closed on; generated output is never edited as source. The CI workflow runs that build, re-runs it with --check, validates the Specs and executes the full test suite plus the docsite checks. The test support library builds a four-Module fixture project and a ModelProcessDouble that replaces only the Pi worker process, leaving the executor, contract checks and host admissions real. Observation: nearly every Module's tests import tests/concorde/support/paths.py, yet only module.spec binds it.
tour.languageLesson: Concorde's Python test suites declare which scenario they verify with a `@verifies("scenario.<id>")` decorator, and the validator reads those declarations by parsing — never by running the tests. Coverage is therefore evidence about the tests, not a change to the contract: an undeclared scenario is reported as uncovered, and a declared one is not proof that the promise is fulfilled.
